13021.description: Macon and Bibb County share a consolidated city-county government in central Georgia. The county lies wholly within the Upper Ocmulgee River sub-basin and had 157,346 residents in 2020.

13023.description: Cochran is the county seat of this upper Coastal Plain county. Its drainage spans the Lower Oconee and Little Ocmulgee sub-basins; the 2020 population was 12,583.

13025.description: The Satilla River runs through this southeastern Georgia county, which forms part of the Brunswick metropolitan area. Nahunta is the county seat.

13027.description: Quitman is the county seat of this Georgia county on the Florida border. The Little River and Withlacoochee River wind along its eastern boundary.

13029.description: This Savannah-area county is best known as the site of Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America, which became operational in 2024 and is its largest employer. Pembroke is the county seat.

13031.description: Bulloch County’s mostly flat coastal plain becomes somewhat hillier in its northwest and central portions. Statesboro is the county seat and center of its micropolitan area.

13033.description: This large eastern Georgia county spans the Piedmont, with its southern half draining into the Upper Ogeechee River basin. Waynesboro is the county seat, within the Augusta metropolitan area.

13035.description: Jackson is the county seat of this Atlanta-area county, wholly within the Upper Ocmulgee River sub-basin. Georgia’s center of population was located in the county’s northeast in 2010.

13037.description: The Ichawaynochaway Creek basin drains most of this rural southwestern Georgia county. Morgan is the county seat; local farms grow corn, oats, sorghum and wheat.

13039.description: Woodbine is the county seat and Kingsland the largest city in this southeastern Georgia county. The Satilla River basin covers much of the area; paper and pulpwood production have long been economic mainstays.

13043.description: Metter is the county seat of this southeastern Georgia county, where the Canoochee River basin drains most of the area. Its western edge drains toward the Ohoopee River.

13045.description: Carrollton is the county seat in this west-central Georgia county along the Alabama border. The western two-thirds drain to the Upper Tallapoosa River basin, while the eastern third is in the Middle Chattahoochee River–Lake Harding basin.

13047.description: This northwestern Georgia county lies wholly within the Middle Tennessee–Chickamauga river basin. Ringgold is the county seat; the 2020 population was 67,872.

13049.description: Charlton County occupies Georgia’s southernmost corner, where much of its interior lies within the Okefenokee Swamp and protected lands. Folkston is the county seat.

13051.description: Georgia’s easternmost county borders the Atlantic, with the Savannah River to its northeast and the Ogeechee River to the southwest. Savannah is both county seat and largest city; water covers nearly a third of the area.

13053.description: The county shares a consolidated government with Cusseta, which remains a geographically distinct municipality within its boundaries. Most of the area drains toward the Chattahoochee River and Walter F. George Lake.

13055.description: Summerville is the county seat of this northwest Georgia micropolitan area. The Upper Coosa and Oostanaula river basins divide its western and eastern portions.

13057.description: This Atlanta suburb includes Lake Allatoona, fed by the Etowah and Little rivers, and rolling terrain rising in the north. Canton is the county seat; the 2020 population was 266,620.

13059.description: Athens and Clarke County share a consolidated government in Georgia’s Piedmont. Most of the area drains toward the Upper Oconee River; the 2020 population was 128,671.

13061.description: Fort Gaines is the county seat of this southwestern Georgia county, where water covers 10.1 percent of the area. Much of the county drains toward the Lower Chattahoochee River.

13063.description: Most of Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport lies in this small Atlanta-area county. Jonesboro is its county seat; the west and east drain toward different river basins.

13065.description: The Okefenokee Swamp and its protected lands extend into the eastern and southeastern portions of this large southeastern Georgia county. Homerville is the county seat.

13067.description: Marietta is the county seat and Mableton the largest city of this core Atlanta county. The area sits in the upper Piedmont, with Kennesaw Mountain and the Chattahoochee River among its landscape features.

13069.description: Douglas is the county seat of this southern Georgia micropolitan area, where most of the land drains into the Satilla River basin. The county had 43,092 residents in 2020.

13071.description: Moultrie is the county seat and center of this southwestern Georgia micropolitan area. The western half of the county drains toward the Ochlockonee River basin.

13073.description: The Savannah River borders this eastern Georgia county just above the fall line, where the Piedmont meets lower terrain. Appling is the legal county seat, while Evans is the government center.

13075.description: Adel is the county seat of this south-central Georgia county. Its western half lies in the Little River sub-basin and its eastern half in the Withlacoochee basin.

13077.description: Newnan is the county seat of this Atlanta-area county in Georgia’s Piedmont. Its eastern half drains toward the Flint River basin; the 2020 population was 146,158.

13079.description: The fall line roughly bisects this central Georgia county, leaving hillier terrain in the north and flatter farmland to the south. Knoxville is the county seat, and Roberta its largest municipality.

13081.description: Cordele is the county seat of this central Georgia micropolitan area, where the Flint River basin drains the western part of the county. The 2020 population was 20,128.

13083.description: Dade County occupies Georgia’s northwest corner within the southern Appalachians. Trenton is its county seat and only incorporated municipality; the county is part of metropolitan Chattanooga.

13085.description: Amicalola Falls, Georgia’s highest waterfall, lies in this Blue Ridge foothills county. Dawsonville is the county seat, and part of Lake Lanier reaches its southeastern corner.

13087.description: Bainbridge is the county seat of this southwestern Georgia county, which forms part of the Tallahassee–Bainbridge metropolitan area. Much of the land drains through the Lower Flint River basin.

13089.description: Decatur is the county seat of this core Atlanta county, whose upper Piedmont terrain is crossed by the South River and numerous creeks. Its population was 764,382 in 2020.

13091.description: Eastman is the county seat of this south Georgia county, where the Ocmulgee and Little Ocmulgee river basins divide the drainage. The 2020 population was 19,925.

13093.description: Vienna is the county seat of this central Georgia county in the upper Coastal Plain. Cotton and peanuts are important crops, and the annual Big Pig Jig barbecue competition is held here.

13095.description: Albany is the county seat and only incorporated city in this southwest Georgia county. Most of the area drains to the Lower Flint River; its 2020 population was 85,790.

13097.description: This Atlanta-area county spans elevations from the Chattahoochee River to uplands near Douglasville. Douglasville is the county seat; the 2020 population was 144,237.

13099.description: The Chattahoochee River forms the western boundary of this southwest Georgia county. Blakely is the county seat, and the 2020 population was 10,854.

13101.description: Whitehead Bay swamp lies in southeastern Georgia’s Echols County. Its western half is in the Alapaha River basin and its eastern half in the Upper Suwannee basin; Statenville is the county seat.

13103.description: Springfield is the county seat of this Savannah-area county, most of whose eastern and central parts drain toward the Savannah River. Agriculture was historically a mainstay, including Irish and sweet potatoes.

13105.description: Elberton is the county seat of this northeastern Georgia county, located in the Piedmont. Water covers about 6.2 percent of its area; the 2020 population was 19,637.

13107.description: Swainsboro is the county seat of this eastern Georgia county, where waterways drain toward the Ogeechee River basin. The 2020 population was 22,768.

13109.description: The Canoochee River flows through this southeastern Georgia county toward the Ogeechee. Claxton is the county seat; manufacturing, education, healthcare and retail are major employment sectors.

13111.description: Blue Ridge is both county seat and largest city in this Appalachian county, where about 90 percent of residents live in unincorporated areas. The Toccoa River crosses the Blue Ridge Mountains toward Tennessee.

13113.description: The Flint River passes through this Atlanta-area county and historically provided transportation for commodity crops. Fayetteville is the county seat; the 2020 population was 119,194.

13115.description: Rome is the county seat of this northwest Georgia metropolitan area, where the Oostanaula and Etowah river basins meet. The county had 98,584 residents in 2020.

13117.description: Cumming is the county seat and only incorporated city in suburban Forsyth County. The eastern two-thirds lie in the Upper Chattahoochee basin, while the northwestern third is in the Etowah basin.

13119.description: Carnesville is the county seat of this northeastern Georgia county in the Piedmont. Most of the land drains into the Broad River sub-basin of the Savannah River system.

13121.description: Atlanta, Georgia’s capital, is the county seat and most populous city in the state’s most populous county. The northern landscape rises from the Piedmont toward the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains.

13123.description: Ellijay is the county seat of this Blue Ridge Mountains county, where the Coosawattee River basin drains most of the area. Poultry raising and processing are the largest parts of local agriculture.

13125.description: Gibson is the county seat of this small east-central Georgia county, where most of the land lies in the Upper Ogeechee River sub-basin. The 2020 population was 2,884.

13127.description: Brunswick is the county seat of this southeastern Georgia county, where water covers 28.3 percent of the area. Much of the county lies in the Cumberland–St. Simons coastal river basin.

13129.description: Baugh and Horn mountains rise in this northwest Georgia county, where the Coosawattee River basin drains the eastern half. Calhoun is the county seat; manufacturing, including flooring, is a major economic base.

13131.description: Cairo is the county seat of this southwest Georgia county, centered on the Upper Ochlockonee River basin. The county had 26,236 residents in 2020.

13133.description: Greensboro is the county seat of Greene County in Georgia’s Lake Country. Most of the county lies in the Upper Oconee basin, with other portions in the Little River and Upper Ogeechee basins.

13135.description: Lawrenceville is the county seat of this core Atlanta county, about nine miles northeast of the city limits. Gwinnett had 957,062 residents in the 2020 census, second-most in Georgia.

13137.description: This county in the Blue Ridge Mountains includes part of Chattahoochee National Forest. Clarkesville is the county seat; the area is part of the Cornelia micropolitan region.

13139.description: Gainesville is the county seat of Hall County in northeastern Georgia, in the upper Piedmont near the Blue Ridge foothills. Its eastern portion lies in the Upper Oconee basin and its western portion in the Upper Chattahoochee basin.

13141.description: Sparta is the county seat of this east-central Georgia county, where the Oconee River basin drains the western portion. The 2020 population was 8,735.

13143.description: Buchanan is the county seat of this Atlanta-area county, where most land drains into the Upper Tallapoosa River basin. The landscape includes upper Piedmont foothills of the Appalachians.

13145.description: The Chattahoochee River forms this west-central county’s border with Alabama. Hamilton is the county seat; Pine Mountain and Franklin D. Roosevelt State Park anchor the county’s largest resort community.

13147.description: Hartwell is the county seat of this Piedmont county, where Lake Hartwell covers part of the landscape. The southern portion drains toward the Savannah River; the 2020 population was 25,828.

13149.description: Franklin is the county seat of this west-central Georgia county, where most land drains toward the Chattahoochee River and Lake Harding. The county had 11,412 residents in 2020.

13151.description: McDonough is the county seat of this Atlanta-area county, where most land drains to the Upper Ocmulgee River basin. The 2020 population was 240,712.

13153.description: Most of Houston County drains to the Lower Ocmulgee basin of the Altamaha. Perry is the county seat; Warner Robins is the larger city.

13155.description: Most of Irwin County drains to the Alapaha River in the Suwannee basin. Ocilla is the county seat.

13157.description: Most of Jackson County lies in the Upper Oconee sub-basin of the Altamaha. Jefferson is the county seat.

13159.description: Jasper County sits in Georgia’s Piedmont, with its western side draining toward the Ocmulgee and Altamaha system. Monticello is the county seat, surrounded by a largely rural landscape of rolling uplands.

13161.description: Parts of Jeff Davis County drain toward the Lower Ocmulgee River. Agriculture and timber are important local industries, and Hazlehurst is the county seat.

13163.description: Jefferson County is largely within the Ogeechee River basin, with a small northern section draining toward the Savannah system. Louisville, the county’s largest community, sits within a predominantly rural landscape.

13165.description: Much of Jenkins County’s southern portion drains toward the Lower Ogeechee basin. Millen is the county seat, near Magnolia Springs State Park.

13167.description: Johnson County is centered on the Ohoopee River watershed within the Altamaha basin. Wrightsville is the county seat in a lightly settled stretch of east-central Georgia.

13169.description: Jones County’s western and northeastern sections drain toward the Ocmulgee and Oconee rivers, both in the Altamaha basin. Gray is the county seat.

13171.description: Lamar County lies in Georgia’s Piedmont, where its western side drains toward the Flint River. Barnesville is the county seat in this inland landscape of rolling terrain.

13173.description: Most of Lanier County is in the Alapaha River sub-basin of the Suwannee basin. Lakeland is the county seat; education, health and social services were leading employment sectors in 2006.

13175.description: Laurens County is among Georgia’s largest counties by area, and most of it is in the Lower Oconee sub-basin of the Altamaha. Dublin is the county seat.

13177.description: Lee County lies in southwest Georgia, with most of its western side draining through the Kinchafoonee and Muckalee creeks toward the Flint. Leesburg and the Albany metropolitan area shape its settlement pattern.

13179.description: The eastern and southern parts of Liberty County drain to the Ogeechee Coastal sub-basin, while northern and western areas drain to the Canoochee. Hinesville is the county seat.

13181.description: Lincoln County lies in the Piedmont above the fall line, with most of its land in the Upper Savannah basin. Clarks Hill Lake development and a logging industry are noted local economic features.

13183.description: Long County is centered on Ludowici, with its central area draining to the Altamaha and the northeast toward the Canoochee. The county is part of the Hinesville metropolitan area.

13185.description: Parts of Lowndes County drain to the Withlacoochee River sub-basin of the Suwannee. Valdosta is the county seat and principal city.

13187.description: Lumpkin County reaches into the Blue Ridge Mountains, including the high terrain around Blood Mountain. Dahlonega is the county seat, set amid mountainous forest and river valleys.

13189.description: McDuffie County’s southern half is largely in the Brier Creek sub-basin of the Savannah River. Thomson is the county seat.

13191.description: McIntosh County is a coastal county with extensive water area; most of its land drains toward the Ogeechee estuary, while the southwest reaches the Altamaha basin. Darien sits among tidal rivers, marshes and barrier islands.

13193.description: Macon County is in Georgia’s upper Atlantic Coastal Plain, with much of its southern half draining toward the Flint River system. Oglethorpe is the county seat.

13195.description: Most of Madison County lies in the Broad River sub-basin of the Savannah basin. Danielsville is the county seat.

13197.description: Marion County is an inland west-central county, with its southern portion draining toward the Flint River system. Buena Vista is the county seat in a rural landscape of uplands and creek valleys.

13199.description: Meriwether County’s Piedmont terrain rises into the Pine Mountain range near Warm Springs and Manchester. Greenville is the county seat, with the southern ridges and springs distinguishing the landscape.

13201.description: Most of Miller County lies in the Spring Creek sub-basin of the ACF River Basin. Colquitt is the county seat.

13205.description: Most of Mitchell County is in the Lower Flint River sub-basin of the Chattahoochee–Flint basin. Camilla is the county seat.

13207.description: Most of Monroe County drains to the Upper Ocmulgee sub-basin of the Altamaha. Forsyth is the county seat.

13209.description: Montgomery County’s drainage is divided among the Altamaha, Lower Oconee and Ohoopee basins. Mount Vernon is the county seat.

13211.description: Morgan County is a Piedmont county within the Upper Oconee watershed. Madison, its county seat, is the principal town in a landscape of rolling hills and lakes.

13213.description: Most of Murray County is in the Conasauga River sub-basin, with its southeast in the Coosawattee sub-basin. Chatsworth is the county seat.

13215.description: Muscogee County occupies the fall line where the Piedmont meets the Coastal Plain, with Columbus beside the Chattahoochee River. The river and the city’s urban footprint define this compact county.

13217.description: Newton County is in the Piedmont, largely within the Upper Ocmulgee watershed. Covington is its county seat and a focal point for settlement east of metropolitan Atlanta.

13219.description: Oconee County is a small Piedmont county whose streams drain entirely to the Upper Oconee River. Watkinsville and nearby communities form part of the Athens area.

13221.description: Oglethorpe County occupies rolling Piedmont uplands, mostly within the Broad River basin of the Savannah system. Lexington is the county seat, with small communities spread across its rural interior.

13223.description: The Tallapoosa River begins in Paulding County, which lies in the Piedmont region of the Appalachian Mountains. Dallas is the county seat.

13225.description: Most of Peach County is in the Lower Ocmulgee sub-basin of the Altamaha. Fort Valley is the county seat.

13227.description: Pickens County reaches into the Blue Ridge Mountains, with Mount Oglethorpe among its high points. Jasper is the county seat in a landscape of wooded ridges and valleys.

13229.description: Part of Pierce County drains to the Little Satilla River sub-basin. Blackshear is the county seat.

13231.description: Pike County lies in the Piedmont and entirely within the Upper Flint River sub-basin. Zebulon is the county seat.

13233.description: Polk County includes rolling hills and small mountains associated with the Piedmont Plateau and Ridge-and-Valley regions. Cedartown is the county seat.

13235.description: Pulaski County lies entirely in the Lower Ocmulgee sub-basin of the Altamaha. Hawkinsville is the county seat.

13237.description: Putnam County is a rolling Piedmont county in the Upper Oconee basin, with farms and lakes across much of its landscape. Eatonton is its county seat.

13239.description: Quitman County borders the Chattahoochee River and Walter F. George Lake, which define its western setting. Georgetown is the small county seat within this west Georgia river landscape.

13241.description: About 60 percent of Rabun County’s land is in national forest and state parks, and much of the Chattahoochee National Forest is within its borders. Clayton is the county seat.

13243.description: More than half of Randolph County drains to Ichawaynochaway Creek, while the northwest drains toward the Chattahoochee. Cuthbert is the county seat.

13245.description: Richmond County is centered on Augusta along the Savannah River, with most of its drainage in the river’s middle basin. The county’s urban core contrasts with wooded and less-developed land toward its southwest.

13247.description: Rockdale County lies entirely within the Upper Ocmulgee sub-basin of the Altamaha. Conyers is the county seat.

13249.description: Schley County’s central area is in the Middle Flint River sub-basin of the Chattahoochee–Flint basin. Ellaville is the county seat.

13251.description: Screven County is bordered by the Savannah River to the east and the Ogeechee River to the southwest. Its terrain rises from low river margins toward higher ground around Sylvania.

13253.description: Seminole County lies at Georgia’s southwest corner, with Spring Creek and the Chattahoochee River shaping its watersheds and western border. Donalsonville sits amid a network of waterways and farm country.

13255.description: The western part of Spalding County lies in the Upper Flint River sub-basin. Griffin is the county seat.

13257.description: Stephens County occupies the upper Piedmont foothills of the Blue Ridge, with the Tugaloo and Savannah river system shaping its northern drainage. Toccoa is its main town in this hilly northeast Georgia landscape.

13259.description: Stewart County lies mainly in Georgia’s upper Gulf Coastal Plain, with most of its drainage in the Middle Chattahoochee sub-basin. Lumpkin is the county seat.

13261.description: Sumter County centers on Americus and includes Lake Blackshear, Muckalee Creek and Kinchafoonee Creek. The western part drains toward the Flint River system, while its rural surroundings include farmland and wooded stream corridors.

13263.description: Talbot County straddles the fall line, with its northern area hillier than the south. Talbotton is the county seat.

13265.description: Taliaferro County is a small, rural Piedmont county drained by tributaries of the Ogeechee and Little rivers. Crawfordville is the county seat, surrounded by rolling uplands and stream valleys.

13267.description: Part of Tattnall County lies within the Ohoopee and Altamaha river basins. Reidsville is the county seat.

13269.description: Taylor County straddles the fall line, where rolling Piedmont uplands give way to the Coastal Plain. The Flint River basin drains much of the county, with Butler serving as the county seat.

13271.description: Telfair County contains at least 50 artesian wells; its southern two-thirds is within the Lower Ocmulgee basin. McRae–Helena is the county seat.

13273.description: Terrell County’s west and south drain toward Ichawaynochaway Creek, while the northeast drains to the Kinchafoonee–Muckalee system; both are in the ACF River Basin. Dawson is the county seat.

13275.description: Thomas County is in Georgia’s Coastal Plain, with its drainage divided between the Ochlockonee and Suwannee river systems. Thomasville is the county seat.

13277.description: Tift County’s west drains toward the Alapaha and Suwannee basin. Tifton is the county seat.

13279.description: Toombs County is centered on Vidalia; its streams drain toward the Ohoopee and Altamaha rivers. Vidalia is the county seat.

13281.description: Towns County is set in the Blue Ridge Mountains, mostly within the Hiwassee River watershed. Hiawassee and Young Harris are small communities surrounded by steep ridges, forests and mountain lakes.

13283.description: About 90 percent of Treutlen County is forested. Soperton serves as its county seat.

13285.description: Troup County lies on the fall line, and the Chattahoochee River borders its west. LaGrange is the county seat.

13287.description: Most of Turner County’s eastern area lies in the Alapaha River sub-basin of the Suwannee. Ashburn is the county seat.

13289.description: Twiggs County crosses the fall line, with hillier land in the north and flatter areas to the south. Jeffersonville is the county seat.

13291.description: Brasstown Bald, Georgia’s highest mountain, rises in Union County. Blairsville is the county seat.

13293.description: Upson County is mostly in the Upper Flint River sub-basin. Thomaston is the county seat.

13295.description: Most of Walker County’s north lies in the Middle Tennessee–Chickamauga sub-basin. LaFayette is the county seat.

13297.description: Walton County is a Piedmont county east of Atlanta, with Monroe as its county seat and principal town. Its western communities are part of the metropolitan fringe, while the eastern side remains more rural.

13299.description: Ware County is Georgia’s largest county by area, and much of it lies within the Okefenokee Swamp and its protected refuge. Waycross is the county’s principal settlement on the swamp’s northern side.

13301.description: Warren County is a rural Piedmont county whose northern drainage reaches the Savannah River system. Warrenton is the county seat amid rolling inland terrain.

13303.description: Washington County’s western part is in the Lower Oconee sub-basin. Sandersville is the county seat.

13305.description: Most of Wayne County’s north and east lies in the Altamaha River sub-basin. Jesup is the county seat.

13307.description: Most of Webster County is in the Kinchafoonee-Muckalee sub-basin. Preston is the county seat.

13309.description: Part of Wheeler County drains toward the Oconee River basin. Alamo is the county seat.

13311.description: White County lies in the foothills of the Blue Ridge, with higher elevations in its northern half and the Chattahoochee River along part of its edge. Cleveland is its county seat in a mountainous, forested setting.

13313.description: Most of Whitfield County lies in the Conasauga River sub-basin. Dalton is the county seat.

13315.description: Most of Wilcox County’s north and east lie in the Alapaha River sub-basin of the Suwannee. Abbeville is the county seat.

13317.description: Wilkes County lies in the Piedmont above the fall line, with the northern area draining toward the Broad River and Savannah system. Washington is its county seat in a landscape of rolling uplands.

13319.description: Wilkinson County lies mainly in Georgia’s upper Atlantic Coastal Plain, with rolling hills toward the fall line. Irwinton is the county seat.

13321.description: Worth County’s eastern third lies in the Little River sub-basin of the Suwannee basin. Sylvester is the county seat.

15001.description: Hawaiʻi County encompasses the Island of Hawaiʻi, whose land spans more than half of the state’s total land area. Its volcanic landscapes range from coastal plains to high mountain slopes, with communities distributed around the island’s perimeter.

15003.description: Honolulu County is a consolidated city-county covering Oʻahu and surrounding ocean waters. Most residents and services are concentrated in Honolulu and the island’s southern urban corridor, while the rest of Oʻahu includes smaller communities and rugged interior ranges.

15005.description: Kalawao County covers a peninsula on Molokaʻi’s north coast and is the smallest U.S. county by land area. It is also the second-smallest by population among counties in the 50 states.

15007.description: Kauaʻi County includes Kauaʻi, Niʻihau and smaller nearby islands. The county’s landscape ranges from high, wet mountain interiors to coastal communities and dry leeward lowlands.

15009.description: Maui County encompasses Maui, Lānaʻi, Molokaʻi (apart from Kalawao), Kahoʻolawe and nearby islets. The islands’ volcanic mountains, valleys and coastlines create sharply varied terrain across the county.

16001.description: Ada County is in southwestern Idaho, with Boise as its county seat and largest city. The Boise River flows through its northern portion, and the northwest edge meets the foothills.

16003.description: Adams County is described as rural, with Council as its county seat and largest city. Its western boundary faces Oregon across the Snake River.

16005.description: The Portneuf River crosses Bannock County and meets the Snake River at American Falls Reservoir. Pocatello is the county seat and largest city.

16007.description: Bear Lake County occupies Idaho’s southeast corner beside Bear Lake, with Wyoming to the east and Utah to the south. Paris is the county seat, and agriculture and tourism are local industries.

16009.description: Benewah County lies along Idaho’s western boundary with Washington and in the rolling Palouse region. St. Maries is its county seat and largest city.

16011.description: The Snake River flows southwest through Bingham County and enters American Falls Reservoir near its southwest corner. Blackfoot is the county seat and largest city.

16013.description: Blaine County is home to the Sun Valley ski resort near Ketchum. Hailey is the county seat and largest city.

16015.description: Boise County is a rural mountain county, with historic Idaho City as its county seat. Thompson Peak marks its highest point on the eastern border.

16017.description: Bonner County lies in northern Idaho and has extensive water area. Sandpoint is its county seat and largest city, and Scotchman Peak is its highest point.

16019.description: The Snake River flows northwest through Bonneville County from the Wyoming border, beginning as Palisades Reservoir. Idaho Falls is its county seat and largest city.

16021.description: Boundary County is Idaho’s northernmost county, with Bonners Ferry as its county seat and largest city. It had 12,056 residents in the 2020 census.

16023.description: Butte County is rural and among Idaho’s least populous counties, with Arco as its county seat. Big Southern Butte is a prominent landmark in the county.

16025.description: Camas County includes the Camas Prairie and the Soldier Mountains. Fairfield is both its county seat and largest city.

16027.description: Canyon County had 231,105 residents in the 2020 census. Caldwell is its county seat, and Nampa is its largest city.

16029.description: Caribou County is in southeastern Idaho, with Meade Peak as its high point. Soda Springs is the county seat and largest city.

16031.description: Cache Peak in the Albion Mountains is Cassia County’s highest point. Burley is both the county seat and largest city.

16033.description: The Bitterroot Range forms Clark County’s northern border. Dubois is its county seat and largest city; the county had 790 residents in the 2020 census.

16035.description: Clearwater County is part of the rolling Palouse region and includes Elk Creek Falls. Orofino is the county seat.

16037.description: Custer County is Idaho’s third-largest county by area, and the Lost River Range contains the state’s highest mountain. Challis is the county seat.

16039.description: Snowyside Peak is the highest point in Elmore County. Mountain Home is both the county seat and largest city.

16041.description: Franklin County had 14,194 residents in the 2020 census, with Preston as its county seat and largest city.

16043.description: Fremont County reaches into the northeastern tip of the Snake River Basin. St. Anthony is its county seat and largest city.

16045.description: Gem County is Idaho’s fifth-smallest county by area. Emmett is both its county seat and largest city.

16047.description: Gooding County had 15,598 residents in the 2020 census. Gooding is its county seat.

16049.description: Idaho County is the state’s largest county by area and includes part of the Nez Perce Indian Reservation. Grangeville is its county seat.

16051.description: Jefferson County had 30,891 residents in the 2020 census, with Rigby as its county seat and largest city.

16053.description: Jerome County had 24,237 residents in the 2020 census. Jerome is both its county seat and largest city.

16055.description: Kootenai County includes extensive lake and river water area and is centered on Coeur d’Alene. The city is the county seat and the county had 171,362 residents in the 2020 census.

16057.description: Latah County is part of the rolling Palouse region in north-central Idaho. Moscow is the county seat and home to the University of Idaho.

16059.description: Lemhi County is Idaho’s fourth-largest county by area, and Bell Mountain is its highest point. Salmon is both the county seat and largest city.

16061.description: Lewis County is Idaho’s fourth-smallest county by area and includes the northern portion of the Nez Perce Indian Reservation. Nezperce is the county seat.

16063.description: Shoshone is the county seat and largest city in Lincoln County. The county is part of the Hailey micropolitan area and had 5,127 residents in 2020.

16065.description: Rexburg is the county seat and largest city in Madison County. Part of the Rexburg micropolitan area, it is Idaho’s third-smallest county by area.

16067.description: Minidoka County is part of the Magic Valley region of the Snake River Plain, where irrigated farmland covers the valley. Rupert is its county seat and largest city.

16069.description: The Clearwater and Snake rivers meet at Lewiston, the Nez Perce County seat. Lewiston is also the county’s largest city.

16071.description: Oneida County’s highest point is Oxford Peak. Malad City is both its county seat and largest city.

16073.description: Owyhee County is Idaho’s second-largest county by area, with nearly all of it described as high intermountain desert. Murphy is its county seat.

16075.description: Payette County is Idaho’s smallest county by area, with Payette as its county seat and largest city.

16077.description: Power County had 7,878 residents in the 2020 census. American Falls is its county seat and largest city.

16079.description: Wallace is the county seat and Kellogg the largest city of Shoshone County. Known as the Silver Valley, the area has a long history of silver, lead and zinc mining.

16081.description: Teton County is Idaho’s second-smallest county by area. Driggs is its county seat, and the county had 11,630 residents in the 2020 census.

16083.description: Twin Falls County is in south-central Idaho and had 90,046 residents in the 2020 census. Twin Falls is its county seat and largest city.

16085.description: Valley County is rural and Idaho’s fifth-largest county by area. Cascade is its county seat; ski resorts are among its major employers.

16087.description: Washington County had 10,500 residents in the 2020 census, with Weiser as its county seat and largest city.

17001.description: Adams County is Illinois’ westernmost county, with Quincy as its county seat. Its 2020 population was 65,737, and it is part of the Quincy metropolitan area.

17003.description: Alexander County occupies Illinois’ southern tip between the Mississippi and Ohio rivers. Cairo sits at their confluence, while low river bottoms and floodplain landscapes characterize much of the county.

17005.description: Bond County had 16,725 residents in the 2020 census, and Greenville is its county seat. It is part of the St. Louis metropolitan area.

17007.description: Boone County counted 53,448 residents in the 2020 census, with Belvidere as its county seat. The county is part of the Rockford metropolitan area.

17009.description: Brown County is a small west-central Illinois county along the Illinois River. Its hills and river valley surround Mount Sterling and smaller agricultural communities.

17011.description: Bureau County is a northern Illinois agricultural county crossed by Big Bureau Creek. Princeton anchors the region’s rail and road connections across a level to gently rolling farm landscape.

17013.description: Calhoun County is a narrow peninsula between the Mississippi and Illinois rivers, with high rolling ground above low river bottoms. Its farms and small towns are closely tied to the two bordering waterways.

17015.description: Carroll County had 15,702 residents in the 2020 census, with Mount Carroll as its county seat. Mississippi Palisades State Park is just north of Savanna within the county.

17017.description: Cass County had 13,042 residents in the 2020 census, with Virginia as its county seat. It is home to Jim Edgar Panther Creek State Fish and Wildlife Area.

17019.description: Champaign County is the fifth-largest Illinois county by land area and is 27 miles wide by 36 miles long. Champaign–Urbana and the University of Illinois anchor its research and education economy.

17021.description: Christian County counted 34,032 residents in the 2020 census, with Taylorville as its county seat. The county is in central Illinois.

17023.description: Clark County lies along the Indiana state line in southeastern Illinois. Marshall is the county seat; the county had 15,455 residents in the 2020 census.

17025.description: Clay County is in southeastern Illinois, with Louisville as its county seat since 1842. It had 13,288 residents in the 2020 census.

17027.description: Clinton County had 36,899 residents in the 2020 census, with Carlyle as its county seat. The county includes Eldon Hazlet and South Shore state recreation areas and is part of the St. Louis metropolitan area.

17029.description: Coles County had 46,863 residents in the 2020 census, with Charleston as its county seat. Charleston is also home to Eastern Illinois University, and the county is coterminous with its micropolitan area.

17031.description: Cook County is Illinois’ most populous county and the second-most populous in the United States. More than 40 percent of Illinois residents live there, with Chicago at its center and Lake Michigan accounting for most of its water area.

17033.description: Crawford County had 18,679 residents in the 2020 census, with Robinson as its county seat. The Wabash River defines part of the county’s eastern boundary.

17035.description: Cumberland County counted 10,450 residents in the 2020 census, with Toledo as its county seat. It is part of the Charleston–Mattoon micropolitan area.

17037.description: DeKalb County had 100,420 residents in the 2020 census, with Sycamore as its county seat. It is part of the Chicago–Naperville metropolitan area.

17039.description: DeWitt County counted 15,516 residents in the 2020 census, with Clinton as its county seat. The county was formed as De Witt County in 1839.

17041.description: Douglas County had 19,740 residents in the 2020 census, with Tuscola as its county seat.

17043.description: DuPage County is a densely developed western suburb of Chicago, crossed by the DuPage River and Salt Creek. Residential and commercial development intersperses with forest preserves and parklands.

17045.description: Edgar County counted 16,866 residents in the 2020 census, with Paris as its county seat. It lies along Illinois’ eastern border.

17047.description: Edwards County had 6,245 residents in the 2020 census, with Albion as its county seat. It is Illinois’ fourth-smallest county by area.

17049.description: Effingham County is in south-central Illinois, with Effingham as both its county seat and largest city. Its population was 34,668 in the 2020 census.

17051.description: Fayette County counted 21,488 residents in the 2020 census, with Vandalia as its county seat. Vandalia is also the site of the state house historic site.

17053.description: Ford County had 13,534 residents in the 2020 census, with Paxton as its county seat. The county is part of the Champaign–Urbana metropolitan area.

17055.description: Franklin County is part of the Metro Lakeland area of southern Illinois, in the region known as Little Egypt. Benton is its county seat, West Frankfort its largest city, and Wayne Fitzgerrell State Recreation Area is in the county.

17057.description: Fulton County had 33,609 residents in the 2020 census, with Lewistown as its county seat and Canton as its largest city. Dickson Mounds Museum in the county focuses on Native American life in the Illinois River valley.

17059.description: Gallatin County had 4,946 residents in the 2020 census, making it Illinois’ third-least populous county. The Wabash and Ohio rivers meet in its northeast, while the Saline River is a major drainage.

17061.description: Greene County had 11,843 residents in the 2020 census, with Carrollton as its county seat. It also contains a notable archaeological area.

17063.description: Grundy County counted 52,533 residents in the 2020 census, with Morris as its county seat. The county is part of the Chicago metropolitan area.

17065.description: Hamilton County is in southern Illinois, with McLeansboro as its county seat. It had 7,993 residents in the 2020 census.

17067.description: Hancock County is part of the Burlington, Iowa–Illinois micropolitan area. Carthage is its county seat and Hamilton its largest city; the county counted 17,620 residents in 2020.

17069.description: Elizabethtown is the county seat of Hardin County, in Illinois’s Little Egypt region. It is the state’s second-smallest county by area and had 3,649 residents in 2020.

17071.description: Oquawka is the county seat of this Illinois county, which is part of the Burlington, Iowa–Illinois micropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 6,387 residents.

17073.description: Henry County counted 49,284 residents in the 2020 census, with Cambridge as its county seat. It lies in northwestern Illinois.

17075.description: Iroquois County is in northeastern Illinois and is the state’s fifth-largest county by total area. Watseka is its county seat.

17077.description: Jackson County had 52,974 residents in the 2020 census and is located 98 miles south of St. Louis. Murphysboro is its county seat.

17079.description: Jasper County counted 9,287 residents in the 2020 census, with Newton as its county seat.

17081.description: Jefferson County is in southern Illinois, with Mount Vernon as its county seat. It had 37,113 residents in the 2020 census.

17083.description: Jersey County is bordered by the Mississippi River to the south and west, and by the Illinois River and Macoupin Creek to the east. Jerseyville is its county seat and largest community.

17085.description: Jo Daviess County is Illinois’ northwesternmost county, and Charles Mound is the state’s highest natural point. Galena is its county seat.

17087.description: Johnson County had 13,308 residents in the 2020 census, with Vienna as its county seat. The county is in southern Illinois.

17089.description: Kane County had 516,522 residents in the 2020 census and is one of Illinois’ most populous counties. Its largest cities are along the Fox River.

17091.description: Kankakee County counted 107,502 residents in the 2020 census, with Kankakee as its county seat.

17093.description: Kendall County is part of the Chicago metropolitan area and was among the nation’s fastest-growing counties from 2010 to 2020. Yorkville is its county seat.

17095.description: Knox County had 49,967 residents in the 2020 census, with Galesburg as its county seat.

17097.description: Lake County lies along Lake Michigan in northeastern Illinois. Water accounts for more than two-thirds of its total area.

17099.description: LaSalle County is part of the Fox Valley and Illinois River Valley regions. It is Illinois’ second-largest county by land area; Ottawa is its county seat.

17101.description: Lawrence County is Illinois’ easternmost county, with Lawrenceville as its county seat. It had 15,280 residents in the 2020 census.

17103.description: Lee County counted 34,145 residents in the 2020 census, with Dixon as its county seat. The county is in north-central Illinois.

17105.description: Livingston County is Illinois’ fourth-largest county by land area. Pontiac is its county seat; the 2020 population was 35,815.

17107.description: Logan County had 27,987 residents in the 2020 census, with Lincoln as its county seat. It lies in central Illinois.

17109.description: McDonough County forms a near-perfect square, with Macomb as its county seat and largest city. It had 27,238 residents in the 2020 census.

17111.description: McHenry County counted 310,229 residents in the 2020 census, making it Illinois’ sixth-most populous county. Woodstock is its county seat.

17113.description: McLean County is Illinois’ largest county by land area and third-largest by total area. Bloomington is its county seat and largest city.

17115.description: Macon County counted 103,998 residents in the 2020 census, with Decatur as its county seat and largest city.

17117.description: Carlinville is the county seat of Macoupin County, Illinois. Agriculture is its primary industry, including corn, soybeans and some wheat.

17119.description: Madison County is part of the Metro East region of Greater St. Louis, along the Mississippi River. Edwardsville is the county seat; the county had 264,776 residents in 2020.

17121.description: Marion County is in southern Illinois, in the area sometimes called Little Egypt. Salem is its county seat; its southwest corner is where the baseline meets the third principal meridian.

17123.description: The Illinois River bisects Marshall County into eastern and western parts. Lacon is its county seat; the 2020 population was 11,742.

17125.description: Mason County is bordered by the Sangamon River to the south and the Illinois River to the west. Havana is its county seat.

17127.description: Massac County had 14,169 residents in the 2020 census, with Metropolis as its county seat. It lies in southern Illinois.

17129.description: Menard County counted 12,297 residents in the 2020 census, and Petersburg is its county seat. It is part of the Springfield metropolitan area.

17131.description: Mercer County had 15,699 residents in the 2020 census, with Aledo as its county seat. The county is part of the Davenport–Moline–Rock Island metropolitan area.

17133.description: Monroe County’s western Mississippi River area is part of the American Bottom. Waterloo is both its county seat and largest city.

17135.description: Montgomery County had 28,288 residents in the 2020 census, with Hillsboro as its county seat. It is in central Illinois.

17137.description: Morgan County had 32,915 residents in the 2020 census, with Jacksonville as its county seat. The 90th meridian passes through the county.

17139.description: Moultrie County counted 14,526 residents in the 2020 census, with Sullivan as its county seat.

17141.description: Ogle County had 51,788 residents in the 2020 census, with Oregon as its county seat.

17143.description: Peoria is the county seat in this Illinois metropolitan county. The county is drained by the Spoon River and Kickapoo, Elbow and Copperas creeks.

17145.description: Perry County is in southern Illinois, with Pinckneyville as its county seat. It had 20,945 residents in the 2020 census.

17147.description: Piatt County had 16,673 residents in the 2020 census, with Monticello as its county seat and largest city.

17149.description: Pike County lies between the Mississippi and Illinois rivers, with highlands between the river valleys. Pittsfield is its county seat.

17151.description: Pope County is Illinois’ southeasternmost county, and its terrain is hilly. Golconda is its county seat; population was 3,763 in 2020.

17153.description: Pulaski County had 5,193 residents in the 2020 census, with Mound City as its county seat. It is Illinois’ third-smallest county by area.

17155.description: Putnam County is Illinois’ smallest county by area, with Hennepin as its county seat. It had 5,637 residents in the 2020 census.

17157.description: The Kaskaskia River joins the Mississippi River in Randolph County. Chester is its county seat; the 2020 population was 30,163.

17159.description: Richland County counted 15,813 residents in the 2020 census, with Olney as its county seat.

17161.description: Rock Island County is bounded on the west by the Mississippi River. The county had 144,672 residents in 2020, and Rock Island is its county seat.

17163.description: St. Clair County lies directly east of St. Louis and is part of the Metro East region. Belleville is its county seat; the county is among Illinois’ most populous.

17165.description: Saline County is in southern Illinois, with Harrisburg as its largest city and county seat. It had 23,768 residents in the 2020 census.

17167.description: Sangamon County is in central Illinois, with Springfield as its county seat and largest city. It had 196,343 residents in the 2020 census.

17169.description: Schuyler County had 6,902 residents in the 2020 census, with Rushville as its county seat. It is in western Illinois.

17171.description: Scott County is a small rural county west of Springfield, with the Illinois River forming its western boundary. Winchester is the county seat among open farmland and river lowlands.

17173.description: Shelby County had 20,990 residents in the 2020 census, with Shelbyville as its county seat.

17175.description: Stark County is a small north-central Illinois county of open prairie farmland. Toulon is its county seat, with small communities spaced across the agricultural landscape.

17177.description: Stephenson County counted 44,630 residents in the 2020 census, with Freeport as its county seat.

17179.description: Pekin is the county seat and largest city of Tazewell County, part of the Peoria metropolitan area. Most of the population lives along the county’s western border.

17181.description: Union County counted 17,244 residents in the 2020 census, with Jonesboro as its county seat. It is in southern Illinois.

17183.description: Vermilion County lies in eastern Illinois between the Indiana border and Champaign County. Danville is its county seat.

17185.description: Wabash County had 11,361 residents in the 2020 census, with Mount Carmel as its county seat.

17187.description: Monmouth is the county seat of Warren County, Illinois. The county had 16,835 residents in 2020, and water accounts for about 0.1 percent of its total area.

17189.description: Washington County contains many lakes, rivers, streams and creeks. Nashville is its county seat; the 2020 population was 13,761.

17191.description: Wayne County had 16,179 residents in the 2020 census, with Fairfield as its county seat.

17193.description: White County counted 13,877 residents in the 2020 census, with Carmi as its county seat.

17195.description: Whiteside County had 55,691 residents in the 2020 census, with Morrison as its county seat.

17197.description: Will County is in northeastern Illinois, crossed by the Kankakee, DuPage and Des Plaines rivers. It had 696,355 residents in the 2020 census.

17199.description: Marion is the largest city and county seat in this southern Illinois county, part of the Metro Lakeland area. The 2020 census counted 67,153 residents.

17201.description: Winnebago County counted 285,350 residents in the 2020 census, making it the state’s seventh-most populous county. Rockford is its county seat.

17203.description: Woodford County had 38,467 residents in the 2020 census, with Eureka as its county seat.

18001.description: Adams County lies in northeastern Indiana along the Ohio border, centered on Decatur. The landscape is mostly level agricultural land with small streams and scattered towns.

18003.description: Allen County is Indiana’s largest county by area, centered on Fort Wayne at the meeting of the St. Marys, St. Joseph and Maumee rivers. The city and its transportation network anchor a broad surrounding agricultural plain.

18005.description: Columbus is the county seat of Bartholomew County, which forms the Columbus metropolitan area. Camp Atterbury occupies the county’s northwestern corner.

18007.description: Benton County lies along Indiana’s western border, where level prairie and farmland extend toward Illinois. Fowler and small towns serve an agricultural landscape with few wooded areas.

18009.description: Blackford County is a small east-central Indiana county of level farmland, centered on Hartford City. Its modest streams and rural communities cross the former prairie landscape.

18011.description: Boone County lies near the center of Indiana, with Lebanon as its county seat. About two-thirds of the county is cultivated, according to the geographic description.

18013.description: Brown County had 15,475 residents in 2020, and Nashville is its only incorporated town and county seat. Its terrain is rugged and hilly, with brush and trees in drainage areas.

18015.description: Carroll County is crossed by the Wabash and Tippecanoe rivers, which flow through its agricultural plain. Delphi is the county seat amid fields, river corridors and small towns.

18017.description: Cass County is centered on Logansport, where the Wabash and Eel rivers meet. River valleys and surrounding farmland shape this north-central Indiana county.

18019.description: Clark County lies across the Ohio River from Louisville, Kentucky. Jeffersonville is its county seat; the county had 121,093 residents in 2020 and is part of the Louisville metropolitan area.

18021.description: Brazil is the county seat of Clay County, part of the Terre Haute metropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 26,466 residents.

18023.description: Clinton County had 33,190 residents in the 2020 census, with Frankfort as its county seat.

18025.description: Crawford County had 10,526 residents in the 2020 census, with English as its county seat. Its terrain is primarily wooded.

18027.description: Daviess County is a gently rolling agricultural county in southwestern Indiana, centered on Washington. The White River and its tributaries cross the region’s fields and low hills.

18029.description: Dearborn County lies on Indiana’s Ohio border near the state’s southeast corner. It had 50,679 residents in the 2020 census.

18031.description: Decatur County lies in southeastern Indiana, where low rolling hills are largely farmed or developed. Greensburg is the county seat amid a network of small towns and wooded drainage corridors.

18033.description: DeKalb County is a rolling agricultural county in northeastern Indiana along the Ohio border. Auburn is its county seat, with farms and small communities spread across the uplands.

18035.description: Delaware County is part of the Muncie metropolitan area, which is itself within a larger metropolitan region. Muncie is the county seat; the 2020 population was 111,903.

18037.description: Dubois County had 43,637 residents in the 2020 census, with Jasper as its county seat. It is the sole county in the Jasper micropolitan area.

18039.description: Elkhart County is part of the Elkhart–Goshen metropolitan area. Goshen is the county seat; the St. Joseph River runs through Elkhart.

18041.description: Fayette County is mostly rural, with farms, pasture and unincorporated woodland described as its land uses. Connersville is the county seat; the 2020 population was 23,398.

18043.description: New Albany is the county seat in this Louisville metropolitan county, which has Indiana’s second-smallest land area. The Georgetown area includes rolling farmland, fields and woods.

18045.description: Fountain County lies along the Wabash River in west-central Indiana. Covington and smaller river towns sit among steep, wooded bluffs and broad farm fields.

18047.description: Franklin County lies on Indiana’s eastern border, and much of its former woodland has been cleared and leveled for agriculture. Brookville is the county seat; it is part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area.

18049.description: Fulton County had 20,480 residents in the 2020 census, with Rochester as its county seat.

18051.description: Gibson County lies in southwestern Indiana near the Wabash and Ohio rivers, with much of its landscape in the Ohio River Valley. Princeton and smaller towns are surrounded by farmland and wooded stream corridors.

18053.description: Grant County consists of low rolling hills used for vegetation, agriculture or urban development. Marion is its county seat; the county had 66,674 residents in 2020.

18055.description: Greene County had 30,803 residents in the 2020 census, with Bloomfield as its county seat. The U.S. Census Bureau identified the county as the mean center of U.S. population in 1930.

18057.description: Hamilton County is part of the Indianapolis metropolitan area and had 347,467 residents in the 2020 census. Noblesville is its county seat.

18059.description: Hancock County is in the Indianapolis metropolitan area, with Greenfield as its county seat. Its terrain is described as low rolling hills, and the 2020 population was 79,840.

18061.description: Harrison County lies in southern Indiana along the Ohio River. Corydon is its county seat; the county had 39,654 residents in 2020.

18063.description: Hendricks County is among the most populous counties in the Indianapolis metropolitan area. Danville is its county seat; the 2020 population was 174,788.

18065.description: Henry County is centered on New Castle, its county seat and only city. It counted 48,914 residents in the 2020 census.

18067.description: Howard County had 83,658 residents in the 2020 census, with Kokomo as its county seat.

18069.description: Huntington County is crossed by the Wabash River, which flows west through the center of the county. Huntington is the main town amid rolling farmland and rural communities.

18071.description: Jackson County had 46,428 residents in the 2020 census, with Brownstown as its county seat.

18073.description: Jasper County lies in northwestern Indiana, where the Iroquois River and its tributaries cross broad agricultural plains. Rensselaer is the county seat in a rural farming region.

18075.description: Jay County is a rural eastern Indiana county along the Ohio border. Portland and smaller towns are surrounded by flat to gently rolling farmland and small streams.

18077.description: Madison is the county seat of Jefferson County, Indiana. The county had 33,147 residents in 2020; water accounts for about 0.62 percent of its total area.

18079.description: Jennings County had 27,613 residents in the 2020 census, with Vernon as its county seat.

18081.description: Franklin is the county seat of this Indiana county, part of the Indianapolis metropolitan area. Its population was 161,765 in 2020.

18083.description: Knox County is centered on Vincennes along the Wabash River, which forms its western boundary. The river bottoms and broad agricultural plain define this southwestern Indiana county.

18085.description: Kosciusko County had 80,240 residents in the 2020 census, with Warsaw as its county seat and only incorporated city.

18087.description: LaGrange County is a largely rural northern Indiana county of lakes, farms and small towns. LaGrange and Shipshewana serve a landscape of agricultural communities and wetlands.

18089.description: Lake County is Indiana’s second-most populous county, with 498,700 residents in the 2020 census. Crown Point is the county seat, and the county is part of the Chicago metropolitan area.

18091.description: LaPorte County is part of Northwest Indiana and the Michigan City metropolitan area. La Porte is the county seat, and Michigan City is the largest city.

18093.description: Lawrence County is a south-central Indiana county of limestone hills, caves and forested valleys. Bedford is the county seat, surrounded by rural farmland and wooded uplands.

18095.description: Madison County’s mostly level terrain is broken by hills along the White River and Fall Creek. Anderson is the county seat; the 2020 population was 130,129.

18097.description: Marion County contains Indianapolis and its surrounding urban neighborhoods, forming Indiana’s largest metropolitan center. The White River and Fall Creek wind through a highly developed landscape with parks and wooded corridors.

18099.description: Marshall County had 46,095 residents in the 2020 census, with Plymouth as its only city and county seat. Its low, rolling hills are mainly used for agriculture, with wooded drainage areas.

18101.description: Martin County is a hilly, heavily wooded county in southern Indiana, with much of its land under federal management. Shoals and the White River valley sit among forested ridges and secluded hollows.

18103.description: Peru is the county seat of Miami County, part of the Kokomo–Peru combined statistical area. The 2020 population was 35,962.

18105.description: Monroe County was identified as the nation’s mean population center in 1910. Bloomington is its county seat; the 2020 population was 139,718.

18107.description: Montgomery County is a gently rolling agricultural county in west-central Indiana, with Crawfordsville as its county seat. Sugar Creek winds through the farmland and wooded stream valleys.

18109.description: Morgan County combines flat glacial plains with rolling hills where the glaciers stopped in central Indiana. Martinsville is its county seat, amid expanding communities and rural land south of Indianapolis.

18111.description: Newton County lies near Indiana’s northwestern corner and is part of the Chicago metropolitan area. Kentland is its county seat; the 2020 population was 13,830.

18113.description: Noble County is a northeastern Indiana county of lakes and wetlands set among rolling farmland. Kendallville and Albion are local centers in a rural landscape with abundant small waterways.

18115.description: Ohio County is Indiana’s smallest county by land area, tucked along the Ohio River southeast of Cincinnati. Rising Sun and a steep river bluff dominate its compact landscape.

18117.description: Orange County is a hilly southern Indiana county, much of its southern area within Hoosier National Forest. Paoli and French Lick sit among wooded ridges, springs and Patoka Lake.

18119.description: Owen County is still largely wooded, with the White River crossing its low hills and wooded valleys. Spencer is its county seat, surrounded by a mix of forest, farms and small towns.

18121.description: Parke County lies along the Wabash River in western Indiana, with Rockville as its county seat. Sugar Creek also crosses the county.

18123.description: Perry County is described as Indiana’s hilliest and one of its most forested counties. Tell City is its county seat; the population was 19,170 in the 2020 census.

18125.description: Pike County is a rural southwestern Indiana county of low hills, wooded drainages and farmland. The Patoka River and its reservoir shape the local landscape around Petersburg.

18127.description: Porter County reaches Lake Michigan, with the Kankakee River marking its southern edge. The county includes the Indiana Dunes, urban communities and broad stretches of farmland and wetlands.

18129.description: Posey County occupies Indiana’s southwestern tip between the Ohio and Wabash rivers. New Harmony and Mount Vernon sit among wooded stream valleys, river bottoms and agricultural land.

18131.description: Pulaski County had 12,514 residents in the 2020 census, with Winamac as its county seat.

18133.description: Putnam County had 36,726 residents in the 2020 census, with Greencastle as its county seat. Its northern terrain is mostly flat, with more rolling hills in the center and southwest.

18135.description: Randolph County is the origin point of the White River and Whitewater River. Winchester is its county seat; the 2020 population was 24,502.

18137.description: Ripley County had 28,995 residents in the 2020 census, with Versailles as its county seat.

18139.description: Rush County had 16,752 residents in the 2020 census, with Rushville as its county seat and only city. The county was once known as a leading maple syrup producer.

18141.description: St. Joseph County centers on South Bend and the St. Joseph River in northern Indiana. The river corridor, universities and urban development contrast with agricultural land toward the county’s edges.

18143.description: Scott County is a small south-central Indiana county of low hills and wooded creek valleys. Scottsburg is its county seat, with farms and small towns across the interior.

18145.description: Shelby County is mostly devoted to agriculture or urban development, with the western edge drained by Sugar Creek. Shelbyville is its county seat and only incorporated city.

18147.description: Spencer County had 19,810 residents in the 2020 census, with Rockport as its county seat. It is outside the Owensboro metropolitan area, though its riverfront faces Owensboro, Kentucky.

18149.description: Starke County is a northwestern Indiana county of low rolling hills, lakes and wetlands. Knox is its county seat amid farmland and wooded patches.

18151.description: Steuben County is in Indiana’s northeastern corner, with Angola as its county seat and only incorporated city. The county contains a state park and more than 100 lakes.

18153.description: Sullivan County lies along Indiana’s western edge, with the Wabash River forming the Illinois border. Sullivan and smaller towns are surrounded by farmland and stream valleys.

18155.description: Switzerland County follows the Ohio River along Indiana’s southeastern tip, opposite Kentucky. Vevay and riverfront communities sit beneath steep wooded hills and winding valleys.

18157.description: Tippecanoe County is in west-central Indiana, about 22 miles east of Illinois. Lafayette is its county seat, and the county is part of its metropolitan area.

18159.description: Tipton County lies north of Indianapolis and consists mostly of level till plain. Tipton is its county seat; its population was 15,359 in the 2020 census.

18161.description: Union County lies on Indiana’s eastern side, bordering Ohio. Liberty is its county seat; the 2020 population was 7,087.

18163.description: Vanderburgh County had 180,136 residents in the 2020 census, with Evansville as its county seat. It was the eighth-largest Indiana county by population in 2020 and also among the smallest by area.

18165.description: Vermillion County is a narrow north-to-south county along the Wabash River and Illinois border. The river and its wooded valley contrast with the agricultural land around Clinton.

18167.description: Vigo County is centered on Terre Haute along the Wabash River and Illinois border. The river corridor, industrial city and surrounding farmland define this west-central Indiana county.

18169.description: Wabash County had 30,976 residents in the 2020 census, with Wabash as its county seat.

18171.description: Warren County fronts the Wabash River in west-central Indiana, with wooded bluffs in the southeast and flat prairie farmland to the northwest. Williamsport is its county seat.

18173.description: Warrick County had 63,898 residents in the 2020 census, with Boonville as its county seat.

18175.description: Washington County is part of the Louisville metropolitan area. Salem is its county seat and only incorporated city; the county had 28,182 residents in 2020.

18177.description: Wayne County lies on Indiana’s eastern border with Ohio and includes the state’s highest natural elevation, Hoosier Hill. Richmond is its county seat; the county is part of the Richmond micropolitan area.

18179.description: Wells County is drained by the Wabash and Salamonie rivers, which cross its agricultural interior. Bluffton is the county seat in northeastern Indiana.

18181.description: White County is a northwestern Indiana farm county, with the Tippecanoe River flowing south through its center. Monticello and small towns sit amid gently rolling fields.

18183.description: Whitley County is a northern Indiana agricultural county dotted with lakes and small streams. Columbia City is its county seat amid rolling fields and wooded drainage corridors.

19001.description: Greenfield is the county seat of Adair County, which had 7,496 residents in the 2020 census.

19003.description: Adams County was Iowa’s least-populous county in the 2020 census, with 3,704 residents. Corning is its county seat.

19005.description: Allamakee County is Iowa’s northeasternmost county, where the Upper Iowa and Yellow rivers cross the Driftless Area before reaching the Mississippi River. Waukon is the county seat; the 2020 population was 14,061.

19007.description: Appanoose County includes Rathbun Reservoir, created by damming the Chariton River. Centerville is its county seat; the county had 12,317 residents in the 2020 census.

19009.description: Audubon County had 5,674 residents in the 2020 census, making it Iowa’s third-least populous county. Audubon is its county seat.

19011.description: Benton County had 25,575 residents in the 2020 census. Vinton is both the county seat and largest city.

19013.description: The Cedar River crosses Black Hawk County from northwest to southeast, and much of the land lies on its floodplain. Waterloo is the county seat; the 2020 population was 131,144.

19015.description: Boone County had 26,715 residents in the 2020 census, with Boone as its county seat. It forms the Boone micropolitan area within the wider Des Moines region.

19017.description: The Cedar and Wapsipinicon rivers cross Bremer County in northeastern Iowa. Waverly is the county seat; its 2020 population was 24,988.

19019.description: Buchanan County had 20,565 residents in the 2020 census, with Independence as its county seat. It lies in Iowa’s northeast.

19021.description: The North Raccoon River begins in Buena Vista County, north of Marathon. Storm Lake is its county seat; the county had 20,823 residents in the 2020 census.

19023.description: Butler County counted 14,334 residents in the 2020 census, with Allison as its county seat. The county lies in north-central Iowa.

19025.description: Calhoun County had 9,927 residents in the 2020 census, and Rockwell City is both its county seat and largest city.

19027.description: Carroll County had 20,760 residents in the 2020 census, with Carroll as its county seat. The county lies in western Iowa.

19029.description: Cass County counted 13,127 residents in the 2020 census, with Atlantic as its county seat. It is in southwestern Iowa.

19031.description: Rock Creek flows through Cedar County, which had 18,505 residents in the 2020 census. Tipton is its county seat.

19033.description: Cerro Gordo County centers on Mason City, its county seat, and had 43,127 residents in the 2020 census. The county’s total area includes a small share of water.

19035.description: Cherokee County had 11,658 residents in the 2020 census, with Cherokee as its county seat. The county is in northwest Iowa.

19037.description: Chickasaw County counted 12,012 residents in the 2020 census, with New Hampton as its county seat. The county lies in northeast Iowa.

19039.description: Clarke County had 9,748 residents in the 2020 census, with Osceola as its county seat. The county is in southern Iowa.

19041.description: Clay County had 16,384 residents in the 2020 census, with Spencer as its county seat. Barringer Slough is a notable wetland in the county.

19043.description: Clayton County lies in Iowa’s Driftless Area, where streams have cut deep valleys above the Mississippi River. Elkader is the county seat, and Guttenberg is its largest city.

19045.description: Clinton County includes Iowa’s easternmost point on the Mississippi River. Clinton is the county seat; the county had 46,460 residents in the 2020 census.

19047.description: Crawford County had 16,525 residents in the 2020 census, with Denison as its county seat. It is the 13th-largest county in Iowa by area.

19049.description: Dallas County counted 99,678 residents in the 2020 census, with Adel as its county seat. It is one of Iowa’s more populous counties and part of the Des Moines metropolitan region.

19051.description: Davis County had 9,110 residents in the 2020 census, and Bloomfield is its county seat. The county is part of the Ottumwa micropolitan area.

19053.description: Decatur County counted 7,645 residents in the 2020 census, with Leon as its county seat. The county’s communities are spread across southern Iowa.

19055.description: Delaware County had 17,488 residents in the 2020 census, and Manchester is its county seat. Its surface is described as rough and hilly.

19057.description: Des Moines County counted 38,910 residents in the 2020 census, with Burlington as both its county seat and largest city. It is one of Iowa’s two counties on the Mississippi River.

19059.description: Dickinson County had 17,703 residents in the 2020 census, and Spirit Lake is its county seat. The Iowa Great Lakes make the county a popular vacation destination.

19061.description: Dubuque County had 99,266 residents in the 2020 census, with Dubuque as its county seat. Manufacturing remains important, alongside a more diversified economy that includes healthcare and education.

19063.description: Emmet County counted 9,388 residents in the 2020 census, with Estherville as both its county seat and largest city. It is among Iowa’s smallest counties by area.

19065.description: Fayette County had 19,509 residents in the 2020 census, and West Union is its county seat. The county lies in northeastern Iowa.

19067.description: Floyd County counted 15,627 residents in the 2020 census, with Charles City as its county seat and largest city. The city is the principal community in north-central Iowa.

19069.description: Franklin County had 10,019 residents in the 2020 census, with Hampton as its county seat. The county lies in north-central Iowa.

19071.description: Fremont County counted 6,605 residents in the 2020 census, with Sidney as its county seat and largest city. It is among Iowa’s least populous counties.

19073.description: Greene County had 8,771 residents in the 2020 census, and Jefferson is its county seat. The county lies in west-central Iowa.

19075.description: Grundy County counted 12,329 residents in the 2020 census, with Grundy Center as its county seat and largest city. It ranks among Iowa’s larger counties by area.

19077.description: Guthrie County had 10,623 residents in the 2020 census, with Guthrie Center as its county seat. The county is in west-central Iowa.

19079.description: Hamilton County counted 15,039 residents in the 2020 census, with Webster City as its county seat and largest city. The county is in central Iowa.

19081.description: Hancock County had 10,795 residents in the 2020 census, and Garner is its county seat. It lies in north-central Iowa.

19083.description: Hardin County counted 16,878 residents in the 2020 census, with Eldora as its county seat. The county is located in central Iowa.

19085.description: Harrison County had 14,582 residents in the 2020 census, and Logan is its county seat. It lies in western Iowa.

19087.description: Henry County counted 20,482 residents in the 2020 census, with Mount Pleasant as its county seat. The county lies in southeastern Iowa.

19089.description: Howard County had 9,469 residents in the 2020 census, with Cresco as both its county seat and largest city. It is in northeastern Iowa.

19091.description: Humboldt County counted 9,597 residents in the 2020 census. Dakota City is the county seat, and Humboldt is its largest city.

19093.description: Ida County had 7,005 residents in the 2020 census, with Ida Grove as its county seat. It is one of Iowa’s least populous counties.

19095.description: Iowa County counted 16,662 residents in the 2020 census, with Marengo as its county seat and Williamsburg as its largest city. It is one of the larger counties in the state by area.

19097.description: Jackson County had 19,485 residents in the 2020 census, and Maquoketa is its county seat. The county’s eastern border follows the Mississippi River.

19099.description: Jasper County counted 37,813 residents in the 2020 census, with Newton as its county seat. The North and South Skunk rivers flow through the county.

19101.description: Jefferson County had 15,663 residents in the 2020 census, with Fairfield as its county seat. The Skunk River runs south through the county.

19103.description: Johnson County counted 152,854 residents in the 2020 census, with Iowa City as its county seat and largest city. It is among Iowa’s most populous counties and includes the University of Iowa.

19105.description: Jones County had 20,646 residents in the 2020 census, with Anamosa as its county seat and largest city. The county is in eastern Iowa.

19107.description: Keokuk County counted 10,033 residents in the 2020 census, with Sigourney as its county seat and largest city. The South Branch of the Skunk River crosses the county.

19109.description: Kossuth County is Iowa’s largest county by area, with Algona as both its county seat and largest city. Farms growing corn and soybeans are part of its agricultural economy.

19111.description: Lee County is Iowa’s southernmost county and had 33,555 residents in the 2020 census. Fort Madison and Keokuk are both county seats, a distinction unique in Iowa.

19113.description: Linn County counted 230,299 residents in the 2020 census, with Cedar Rapids as its county seat and largest city. It is Iowa’s second-most populous county.

19115.description: Louisa County had 10,837 residents in the 2020 census, with Wapello as both its county seat and largest city. The county is part of the Muscatine micropolitan area.

19117.description: Lucas County counted 8,634 residents in the 2020 census, with Chariton as its county seat. It lies in southern Iowa.

19119.description: Lyon County is Iowa’s northwesternmost county, with Rock Rapids as its county seat. It had 11,934 residents in the 2020 census.

19121.description: Madison County had 16,548 residents in the 2020 census, with Winterset as its county seat. It is part of the Des Moines–West Des Moines metropolitan area.

19123.description: Mahaska County counted 22,190 residents in the 2020 census, with Oskaloosa as its county seat. Oskaloosa is also the center of the county’s micropolitan area.

19125.description: Marion County had 33,414 residents in the 2020 census, with Knoxville as its county seat. The county lies in south-central Iowa.

19127.description: Marshall County counted 40,105 residents in the 2020 census, with Marshalltown as both its county seat and largest city. It ranks among Iowa’s larger counties by area.

19129.description: Mills County had 14,484 residents in the 2020 census, with Glenwood as its county seat. The county is in southwestern Iowa.

19131.description: Mitchell County counted 10,565 residents in the 2020 census, with Osage as its county seat. The county is in northeastern Iowa.

19133.description: Monona County had 8,751 residents in the 2020 census, and Onawa is its county seat. The county is in western Iowa.

19135.description: Monroe County lies in south-central Iowa and was once a center of bituminous coal mining. Its population reached more than 25,000 in 1910 before declining as mining diminished.
