19137.description: Red Oak is the county seat of Montgomery County in southwestern Iowa. The largely rural county is devoted to agriculture and had 10,330 residents in 2020.

19139.description: Muscatine County counted 43,235 residents in the 2020 census, with Muscatine as its county seat. Its southeastern border follows the Mississippi River.

19141.description: O’Brien County had 14,182 residents in the 2020 census, with Primghar as its county seat. It is located in northwest Iowa.

19143.description: Osceola County counted 6,192 residents in the 2020 census, making it one of Iowa’s least populous counties. Sibley is its county seat.

19145.description: Page County had 15,211 residents in the 2020 census, with Clarinda as its county seat. It is in southwestern Iowa.

19147.description: Palo Alto County counted 8,996 residents in the 2020 census, with Emmetsburg as its county seat. It is a rural north-central Iowa county.

19149.description: Plymouth County is Iowa’s westernmost county and the fourth-largest by area. Le Mars is both its county seat and largest city; its population was 25,698 in 2020.

19151.description: Pocahontas County had 7,078 residents in the 2020 census, making it one of Iowa’s least populous counties. Pocahontas is its county seat.

19153.description: Polk County is Iowa’s most populous county, with 492,401 residents in the 2020 census. Des Moines is both its county seat and the state capital.

19155.description: Pottawattamie County counted 93,667 residents in the 2020 census and is Iowa’s second-largest county by area. Council Bluffs is its county seat and largest city.

19157.description: Poweshiek County is drained by the North Fork of the Skunk River. Montezuma is the county seat; the county had 18,662 residents in the 2020 census.

19159.description: Ringgold County had 4,663 residents in the 2020 census, making it Iowa’s second-least populous county. Mount Ayr is its county seat.

19161.description: Sac County counted 9,814 residents in the 2020 census. Sac City is both its county seat and largest city.

19163.description: Scott County is Iowa’s third-most populous county, with 174,669 residents in the 2020 census. Davenport is both the county seat and largest city.

19165.description: Shelby County had 11,746 residents in the 2020 census, with Harlan as both its county seat and largest city.

19167.description: Sioux County counted 35,872 residents in the 2020 census. Orange City is its county seat, while Sioux Center is its largest city.

19169.description: Story County had 98,537 residents in the 2020 census and is the ninth-most populous county in Iowa. Nevada is its county seat, and the geographic center of Iowa lies within the county.

19171.description: Tama County counted 17,135 residents in the 2020 census. Toledo is its county seat, while Tama is its largest city.

19173.description: Taylor County had 5,896 residents in the 2020 census, making it one of Iowa’s least populous counties. Bedford is its county seat.

19175.description: Union County is in southern Iowa and had 12,138 residents in the 2020 census. Creston is its county seat.

19177.description: Van Buren County counted 7,203 residents in the 2020 census, placing it among Iowa’s least populous counties. Keosauqua is its county seat.

19179.description: Wapello County had 35,437 residents in the 2020 census, with Ottumwa as both its county seat and largest city.

19181.description: Warren County counted 52,403 residents in the 2020 census. Indianola is its county seat and largest city; the county is part of the Des Moines metropolitan area.

19183.description: Washington County had 22,565 residents in the 2020 census, with Washington as both its county seat and largest city.

19185.description: Wayne County counted 6,497 residents in the 2020 census, making it one of Iowa’s least populous counties. Corydon is its county seat and largest city.

19187.description: Webster County had 36,999 residents in the 2020 census, with Fort Dodge as its county seat.

19189.description: Winnebago County counted 10,679 residents in the 2020 census. Forest City is its county seat.

19191.description: Winneshiek County had 20,070 residents in the 2020 census, with Decorah as its county seat.

19193.description: Woodbury County counted 105,941 residents in the 2020 census and borders the Missouri River on Iowa’s western edge. Sioux City is its county seat and largest city.

19195.description: Worth County had 7,443 residents in the 2020 census and is among Iowa’s smallest counties by area. Northwood is its county seat.

19197.description: Wright County counted 12,943 residents in the 2020 census, with Clarion as its county seat. Its terrain is described as generally undulating.

20001.description: Allen County is in southeastern Kansas, with Iola as both its county seat and most populous city. Its population was 12,526 in the 2020 census.

20003.description: Anderson County lies in east-central Kansas, with Garnett as both its county seat and most populous city. It counted 7,836 residents in the 2020 census.

20005.description: Atchison County is a small northeastern Kansas county, with Atchison as both its county seat and most populous city. It had 16,348 residents in the 2020 census.

20007.description: Barber County lies in south-central Kansas, with Medicine Lodge as both its county seat and most populous city. It had 4,228 residents in the 2020 census.

20009.description: Barton County is square in outline, centered on Great Bend, which is both its county seat and largest city. The county counted 25,493 residents in the 2020 census.

20011.description: Bourbon County is in southeast Kansas, with Fort Scott as its county seat and most populous city. Its population was 14,360 in the 2020 census.

20013.description: Brown County lies in northeastern Kansas, where the Wolf River has its source. Hiawatha is both the county seat and most populous city; the county had 9,508 residents in 2020.

20015.description: Butler County is Kansas’ largest county by total area, with El Dorado as its county seat. Andover is the most populous city; the county counted 67,380 residents in 2020.

20017.description: Chase County is in the eastern half of central Kansas, with Cottonwood Falls as its county seat and largest city. It had 2,572 residents in the 2020 census.

20019.description: Chautauqua County is in southeast Kansas, with Sedan as its county seat and most populous city. It counted 3,379 residents in the 2020 census.

20021.description: Cherokee County lies in southeastern Kansas, with Columbus as its county seat and Baxter Springs as its most populous city. The county had 19,362 residents in 2020 and is part of the Joplin metropolitan area.

20023.description: Cheyenne County occupies Kansas’ northwestern corner and is crossed by the South Fork of the Republican River. St. Francis is both its county seat and most populous city; population was 2,616 in 2020.

20025.description: Clark County lies in southwestern Kansas, with Ashland as its county seat and most populous city. The county counted 1,991 residents in the 2020 census.

20027.description: Clay County is centered on Clay Center, which is both its county seat and most populous city. The county had 8,117 residents in the 2020 census.

20029.description: Cloud County is centered on Concordia, its county seat and most populous city. It counted 9,032 residents in the 2020 census.

20031.description: Coffey County lies in eastern Kansas, with Burlington as its county seat and most populous city. Its population was 8,360 in the 2020 census.

20033.description: Comanche County is a small south-central Kansas county, with Coldwater as its county seat and most populous city. It had 1,689 residents in the 2020 census.

20035.description: Cowley County is centered on Winfield, its county seat, and Arkansas City, its most populous city. The county had 34,549 residents in the 2020 census.

20037.description: Crawford County is in southeast Kansas, with Girard as its county seat and Pittsburg as its most populous city. It counted 38,972 residents in the 2020 census.

20039.description: Decatur County is in northwest Kansas, crossed by Beaver Creek and Long Branch Creek. Oberlin is both its county seat and most populous city; population was 2,764 in 2020.

20041.description: Dickinson County is in central Kansas, with Abilene as its county seat and most populous city. It had 18,402 residents in the 2020 census.

20043.description: Doniphan County is Kansas’ northeasternmost county, bordered by Nebraska to the north and Missouri to the east. Troy is the county seat; Wathena is the largest city.

20045.description: Douglas County centers on Lawrence, its county seat and most populous city, and the University of Kansas. The county counted 118,785 residents in the 2020 census.

20047.description: Edwards County is a small south-central Kansas county, with Kinsley as its county seat and most populous city. It had 2,907 residents in the 2020 census.

20049.description: Elk County is in southeastern Kansas, with Howard as its county seat and most populous city. Its population was 2,483 in the 2020 census.

20051.description: Ellis County is crossed by the Saline River and centered on Hays, its county seat and most populous city. It counted 28,934 residents in the 2020 census.

20053.description: Ellsworth County is crossed by the Smoky Hill River. Ellsworth is both its county seat and most populous city; the county had 6,376 residents in the 2020 census.

20055.description: Finney County is Kansas’ second-largest county by area, centered on Garden City, its county seat and largest city. It counted 38,470 residents in the 2020 census.

20057.description: Ford County is centered on Dodge City, its county seat and most populous city. The county had 34,287 residents in the 2020 census.

20059.description: Franklin County lies in eastern Kansas, with Ottawa as its county seat and most populous city. It had 25,996 residents in the 2020 census.

20061.description: Geary County is a small county in Kansas, with Junction City as its county seat and most populous city. The county counted 36,739 residents in the 2020 census.

20063.description: Gove County is centered on Gove City, its county seat, while Quinter is its most populous city. It counted 2,718 residents in the 2020 census.

20065.description: Graham County is centered on Hill City, its county seat and most populous city. The county had 2,415 residents in the 2020 census.

20067.description: Grant County’s only city is Ulysses, which is also its county seat. It counted 7,352 residents in the 2020 census.

20069.description: Gray County includes a wind farm near Montezuma with 170 turbines and 110 megawatts of generating capacity; Cimarron is the county seat. The county had 5,653 residents in the 2020 census.

20071.description: Greeley County has a predominantly prairie landscape between 3,000 and 4,000 feet in elevation; its county seat is Tribune. The county had 1,284 residents in the 2020 census.

20073.description: Greenwood County lies in southeastern Kansas and is the state’s fifth-largest county by area; Eureka is its county seat. The county had 6,016 residents in the 2020 census.

20075.description: The Arkansas River crosses Hamilton County, where limestone and gypsum deposits are also found; Syracuse is the county seat. The county had 2,518 residents in the 2020 census.

20077.description: Anthony is the county seat of Harper County, Kansas. The county had 5,485 residents in the 2020 census.

20079.description: The Little Arkansas River flows through Harvey County, whose county seat and most populous city is Newton. The county had 34,024 residents in the 2020 census.

20081.description: Haskell County’s landscape includes circular crop fields; Sublette is its county seat and most populous city. The county had 3,780 residents in the 2020 census.

20083.description: Jetmore is the county seat of Hodgeman County, Kansas. The county had 1,723 residents in the 2020 census.

20085.description: The Prairie Band Potawatomi Indian Reservation occupies about 18.5 percent of Jackson County near its center; Holton is the county seat. The county had 13,232 residents in the 2020 census.

20087.description: Oskaloosa is the county seat of Jefferson County, Kansas. The county had 18,368 residents in the 2020 census.

20089.description: Mankato is the county seat of Jewell County, Kansas. The county had 2,932 residents in the 2020 census.

20091.description: Johnson County lies along the Missouri border and contains Kansas City suburbs, including Overland Park; Olathe is the county seat. The county had 609,863 residents in the 2020 census.

20093.description: Lakin is the county seat of Kearny County, Kansas. The county had 3,983 residents in the 2020 census.

20095.description: Kingman is the county seat of Kingman County, Kansas. The county had 7,470 residents in the 2020 census.

20097.description: Kiowa County contains iron-rich meteorites from the Brenham meteor fall; Greensburg is its county seat and largest city. The county had 2,460 residents in the 2020 census.

20099.description: Labette County lies in southeastern Kansas, with Oswego as county seat and Parsons as its most populous city. The county had 20,184 residents in the 2020 census.

20101.description: Dighton is both Lane County’s seat and its only incorporated city; the county is Kansas’s third-least populous. The county had 1,574 residents in the 2020 census.

20103.description: Leavenworth County is part of the Kansas City metropolitan area, with a watershed connected to the Kansas River basin through Stranger Creek. The county had 81,881 residents in the 2020 census.

20105.description: Lincoln Center is the county seat of Lincoln County, Kansas. The county had 2,939 residents in the 2020 census.

22041.description: Winnsboro is the parish seat of Franklin Parish, Louisiana. The parish had 19,774 residents in the 2020 census.

22043.description: Grant Parish lies in north-central Louisiana’s Red River Valley and belongs to the Alexandria metropolitan area; Colfax is the parish seat. The parish had 22,169 residents in the 2020 census.

22045.description: Iberia Parish includes Marsh Island and the Port of Iberia’s waterway connection to the Gulf Coast; New Iberia is the parish seat. The parish had 69,929 residents in the 2020 census.

22047.description: Iberville Parish lies south of Baton Rouge and belongs to its metropolitan area; Plaquemine is the parish seat. The parish had 30,241 residents in the 2020 census.

22049.description: Jackson Parish lies in northern Louisiana, with Jonesboro as parish seat and Caney Lake Reservoir in Jimmie Davis State Park to its east. The parish had 15,031 residents in the 2020 census.

22051.description: Jefferson Parish combines northern New Orleans suburbs with extensive southern marshland and Grand Isle; Gretna is the parish seat. The parish had 440,781 residents in the 2020 census.

22059.description: Jena is the parish seat of LaSalle Parish, Louisiana. The parish had 14,791 residents in the 2020 census.

22061.description: Ruston is Lincoln Parish’s seat, and the parish forms the Ruston micropolitan statistical area. The parish had 48,396 residents in the 2020 census.

22063.description: Livingston Parish is part of the Baton Rouge metropolitan area and contains a LIGO gravitational wave observatory; the town of Livingston is its parish seat. The parish had 142,282 residents in the 2020 census.

22065.description: Madison Parish lies in Mississippi River delta lowlands on Louisiana’s northeastern border; its economy remains primarily agricultural, and Tallulah is the parish seat. The parish had 10,017 residents in the 2020 census.

22067.description: Bastrop is Morehouse Parish’s seat; the parish forms the Bastrop micropolitan statistical area. The parish had 25,629 residents in the 2020 census.

22069.description: Natchitoches Parish is Louisiana’s fourth-largest parish by land area and lies within the Cane River National Heritage Area; Natchitoches is its parish seat. The parish had 37,515 residents in the 2020 census.

22071.description: Orleans Parish shares its boundaries and consolidated government with New Orleans. Lake Pontchartrain lies to its north and Lake Borgne to its east.

22073.description: The Ouachita River separates Monroe, Ouachita Parish’s seat, from West Monroe; the parish is part of the Monroe metropolitan area. The parish had 160,368 residents in the 2020 census.

22075.description: Plaquemines Parish has low-lying communities and Gulf of Mexico boundaries to the south and southeast; seafood exports and citrus production are significant industries. The parish had 23,515 residents in the 2020 census.

22077.description: Pointe Coupee Parish has prairie and backswamp terrain and an economy heavily reliant on agriculture, including sugarcane; New Roads is the parish seat. The parish had 20,758 residents in the 2020 census.

22079.description: Rapides Parish contains Alexandria, its parish seat and largest city, on the Red River; the parish belongs to the Alexandria metropolitan area. The parish had 130,023 residents in the 2020 census.

22081.description: Coushatta is the parish seat of Red River Parish, Louisiana. The parish had 7,620 residents in the 2020 census.

22083.description: Richland Parish has flat, fertile farmland in Louisiana’s Delta Country, with the Boeuf River crossing its center and Bayou Macon flowing through the east. The parish had 20,043 residents in the 2020 census.

22085.description: Many is the parish seat of Sabine Parish, Louisiana. The parish had 22,155 residents in the 2020 census.

22087.description: St. Bernard Parish lies southeast of New Orleans and includes the Chandeleur Islands and Chandeleur Sound; Chalmette is its parish seat. The parish had 43,764 residents in the 2020 census.

22089.description: The Mississippi River splits St. Charles Parish between east and west banks; its economic base is the energy industry, and Hahnville is the parish seat. The parish had 52,549 residents in the 2020 census.

22091.description: St. Helena Parish lies in the northern tier of Louisiana’s Florida Parishes and belongs to the Baton Rouge metropolitan area; Greensburg is its parish seat. The parish had 10,920 residents in the 2020 census.

22093.description: St. James Parish sits on the Mississippi River between New Orleans and Baton Rouge, with Convent as its parish seat. The parish had 20,192 residents in the 2020 census.

22099.description: Iberia Parish separates St. Martin Parish into two noncontiguous areas; St. Martin lies in the Atchafalaya Basin, with Bayou Teche running through it. The parish had 51,767 residents in the 2020 census.

22103.description: St. Tammany Parish lies north of Lake Pontchartrain and forms the Slidell–Mandeville–Covington metropolitan area; Covington is its parish seat. The parish had 264,570 residents in the 2020 census.

22107.description: Tensas Parish’s eastern boundary follows the Mississippi River; St. Joseph is the parish seat, near Lake Bruin, an oxbow lake. The parish had 4,147 residents in the 2020 census.

22109.description: Terrebonne Parish borders the Gulf of Mexico and averages about six feet above sea level, with extensive flood protection works; Houma is the parish seat. The parish had 109,580 residents in the 2020 census.

22111.description: Union Parish lies in north-central Louisiana and belongs to the Monroe metropolitan area; Farmerville is its parish seat. The parish had 21,107 residents in the 2020 census.

22113.description: Vermilion Parish lies in southern Acadiana along the Gulf of Mexico, where parts of its southern land have been lost to erosion; Abbeville is its parish seat. The parish had 57,359 residents in the 2020 census.

22117.description: Washington Parish’s agriculture includes watermelon production, following a long history of timber and paper industries; Franklinton is the parish seat and Bogalusa its largest city. The parish had 45,463 residents in the 2020 census.

22119.description: Webster Parish lies in northwestern Louisiana and has long depended on petroleum and natural gas employment; Minden is its parish seat. The parish had 36,967 residents in the 2020 census.

22121.description: West Baton Rouge Parish lies along the Mississippi River, with heavy industry supported by river and rail transportation; Port Allen is the parish seat. The parish had 27,199 residents in the 2020 census.

22123.description: Oak Grove is the parish seat of West Carroll Parish, Louisiana. The parish had 9,751 residents in the 2020 census.

22125.description: West Feliciana Parish lies on the Mississippi River and contains the River Bend Nuclear Generating Station; St. Francisville is its parish seat. The parish had 15,310 residents in the 2020 census.

22127.description: Saline Bayou separates Winn Parish from Natchitoches Parish along U.S. Highway 71; Winnfield is the parish seat. The parish had 13,755 residents in the 2020 census.

23001.description: The Androscoggin River crosses Androscoggin County’s center; Auburn is the county seat and Lewiston its most populous city. The county had 111,139 residents in the 2020 census.

23003.description: Aroostook County is Maine’s northernmost and largest county by area, along the Canadian border; Houlton is its county seat. The county had 67,105 residents in the 2020 census.

23005.description: Cumberland County includes most of Casco Bay and Sebago Lake, which supplies much of its tap water; Portland is the county seat. The county had 303,069 residents in the 2020 census.

23007.description: Franklin County includes Appalachian mountain terrain, Rangeley Lake and part of Mooselookmegantic Lake; Farmington is the county seat. The county had 29,456 residents in the 2020 census.

23009.description: Hancock County includes Acadia National Park on Mount Desert Island and extends inland from the coast; Ellsworth is the county seat. The county had 55,478 residents in the 2020 census.

23011.description: The Kennebec River nearly bisects Kennebec County, whose landscape also includes lakes, ponds and the Kennebec Highlands; Augusta, Maine’s capital, is its county seat. The county had 123,642 residents in the 2020 census.

23013.description: Knox County contains Mount Megunticook in Camden Hills State Park, its highest point at 1,381 feet; Rockland is the county seat. The county had 40,607 residents in the 2020 census.

23015.description: Lincoln County is Maine’s third-smallest county by area, with Wiscasset as its county seat and Crummett Mountain among its geographic features. The county had 35,237 residents in the 2020 census.

23017.description: Oxford County borders Quebec in Maine, with Paris as its county seat. The county had 57,777 residents in the 2020 census.

23019.description: Penobscot County forms the Bangor metropolitan area and is home to the University of Maine; Bangor is its county seat. The county had 152,199 residents in the 2020 census.

23021.description: Piscataquis County contains Mount Katahdin, Maine’s highest natural point, and Moosehead Lake, the state’s largest lake; Dover-Foxcroft is its county seat. The county had 16,800 residents in the 2020 census.

23023.description: Sagadahoc County is Maine’s smallest county by area and part of the Portland–South Portland metropolitan area; Bath is the county seat. The county had 36,699 residents in the 2020 census.

23025.description: Somerset County is Maine’s third-largest county by area, with Skowhegan as the county seat. The county had 50,477 residents in the 2020 census.

23027.description: Belfast is the county seat of Waldo County, Maine. The county had 39,607 residents in the 2020 census.

23029.description: Washington County borders New Brunswick and contains the easternmost point in the contiguous United States; fishing and coastal tourism support local communities. The county had 31,095 residents in the 2020 census.

23031.description: York County lies in southern Maine along New Hampshire, separated from Strafford County by the Salmon Falls and Piscataqua rivers; Alfred is its county seat. The county had 211,972 residents in the 2020 census.

24001.description: Allegany County lies mainly in Appalachian Ridge-and-Valley terrain, with the Allegheny Front in its western portion and the Potomac River along its southern boundary. The county had 68,106 residents in the 2020 census.

24003.description: Anne Arundel County lies along Chesapeake Bay’s western shore, with tidal tributaries forming prominent peninsulas; Annapolis is its county seat and Maryland’s capital. The county had 588,261 residents in the 2020 census.

24005.description: Baltimore County combines suburban development with rural, wooded hills in the north and partly surrounds the independent city of Baltimore. Education, government and health care are major economic sectors.

24009.description: Calvert County occupies a peninsula between Chesapeake Bay and the Patuxent River; Prince Frederick is the county seat. The county had 92,783 residents in the 2020 census.

24011.description: Caroline County is rural and contains the Choptank River and Tuckahoe Creek; it is the only Eastern Shore county touching neither Chesapeake Bay nor the Atlantic Ocean. The county had 33,293 residents in the 2020 census.

24013.description: Carroll County lies on the Piedmont Plateau, with rolling hills and deciduous forest; Parr’s Ridge crosses it from southwest to northeast, and Westminster is the county seat. The county had 172,891 residents in the 2020 census.

24015.description: Cecil County straddles the rolling Piedmont and flat Atlantic Coastal Plain, with the Susquehanna River and upper Chesapeake Bay along its western boundary. The county had 103,725 residents in the 2020 census.

24017.description: Charles County is part of Southern Maryland, with La Plata as its county seat. The county had 166,617 residents in the 2020 census.

24019.description: Dorchester County is Maryland’s largest county by total area and lies on the Eastern Shore, with Cambridge as its county seat. The county had 32,531 residents in the 2020 census.

24021.description: Frederick County spans the Piedmont and Appalachian Mountains, with the Middletown Valley between Catoctin and South mountains; Frederick is the county seat. The county had 271,717 residents in the 2020 census.

24023.description: Garrett County lies entirely in the Appalachian highlands, with deep river valleys and forested recreation lands; tourism includes Deep Creek Lake and winter skiing. The county had 28,806 residents in the 2020 census.

24025.description: Harford County spans Piedmont hills and Atlantic Coastal Plain flatlands along Chesapeake Bay, combining rural and suburban areas with denser development around Aberdeen and Bel Air. The county had 260,924 residents in the 2020 census.

24027.description: Howard County has rolling Piedmont hills bounded largely by the Patapsco and Patuxent rivers; Ellicott City is its county seat and Columbia a major planned community. The county had 334,529 residents in the 2020 census.

24029.description: Kent County lies between the Sassafras and Chester rivers, with Chesapeake Bay to the west; Chestertown is its county seat. The county had 19,198 residents in the 2020 census.

24031.description: Montgomery County adjoins Washington, D.C., on rolling Piedmont terrain; its economy includes biotechnology and research, and Rockville is the county seat. The county had 1,062,061 residents in the 2020 census.

24033.description: Prince George’s County borders Washington, D.C., and has gently rolling coastal-plain hills and valleys, with the Patuxent River along its eastern boundary. The county had 967,201 residents in the 2020 census.

24035.description: Queen Anne’s County lies on Maryland’s Eastern Shore and belongs to the Baltimore metropolitan area; Centreville is its county seat. The county had 49,874 residents in the 2020 census.

24037.description: St. Mary’s County occupies a peninsula bordered largely by the Patuxent and Potomac rivers and Chesapeake Bay, with wooded hills, agricultural fields and tidal shores. The county had 113,777 residents in the 2020 census.

24039.description: Somerset County is Maryland’s southernmost county and part of the Lower Eastern Shore; Princess Anne is its county seat. The county had 24,620 residents in the 2020 census.

24041.description: Talbot County’s economy includes tourism, maritime activity and financial services on Maryland’s Eastern Shore; Easton is its county seat. The county had 37,526 residents in the 2020 census.

24043.description: Washington County includes much of the broad Hagerstown Valley between Appalachian ridges, with the Potomac River along its southern boundary; Hagerstown is its county seat. The county had 154,705 residents in the 2020 census.

24045.description: Wicomico County has mostly flat terrain on the Delmarva Peninsula; Salisbury, its county seat, hosts the headquarters of poultry and grain company Perdue Farms. The county had 103,588 residents in the 2020 census.

24047.description: Worcester County has mostly level coastal terrain and is Maryland’s only county bordering the Atlantic Ocean; Snow Hill is the county seat. The county had 52,460 residents in the 2020 census.

24510.description: Baltimore is an independent city on the Patapsco River near Chesapeake Bay, crossing the fall line between the Piedmont and Atlantic Coastal Plain. It had 585,708 residents in the 2020 census.

25001.description: Barnstable County comprises Cape Cod and associated islands, with Barnstable as the county seat. The county had 228,996 residents in the 2020 census.

25003.description: Berkshire County contains the Hoosac Range, Taconic Mountains and Mount Greylock, Massachusetts’s highest natural point; Pittsfield is its largest city and traditional county seat. The county had 129,026 residents in the 2020 census.

25005.description: Bristol County borders Rhode Island and is part of the Providence metropolitan area; Taunton is its shire town. The county had 579,200 residents in the 2020 census.

25007.description: Dukes County consists of about 40 named islands, including Martha’s Vineyard and Chappaquiddick; Edgartown is its county seat. The county had 20,600 residents in the 2020 census.

25009.description: Essex County includes Massachusetts’s North Shore, Cape Ann and lower Merrimack Valley within Greater Boston. It had 809,829 residents in the 2020 census.

25011.description: Franklin County includes the northern Pioneer Valley, with steep hills rising beside the Connecticut River; Greenfield is its traditional county seat. The county had 71,029 residents in the 2020 census.

25013.description: Hampden County lies in the Pioneer Valley, with Springfield, its traditional county seat, serving as a regional economic and cultural center. The county had 465,825 residents in the 2020 census.

25015.description: Hampshire County occupies the middle Pioneer Valley and northern Hartford–Springfield Knowledge Corridor; Northampton is its traditional county seat. The 2020 census counted 162,308 residents.

25017.description: Middlesex County includes much of MetroWest and is drained by the Merrimack, Nashua and Concord rivers, with the Charles River along its southeastern boundary. It had 1,632,002 residents in 2020.

25019.description: Nantucket County comprises Nantucket, Tuckernuck and Muskeget islands south of Cape Cod under a consolidated town-county government. Tourism and seasonal residents greatly expand the island’s summer population.

25021.description: Norfolk County is part of Greater Boston, with Dedham as its county seat and the separated towns of Brookline and Cohasset forming exclaves. The county had 725,981 residents in the 2020 census.

25023.description: Plymouth County lies south of Boston within its metropolitan area; Plymouth and Brockton are the county seats. The county had 530,819 residents in the 2020 census.

25025.description: Suffolk County consists of Boston, Chelsea, Revere and Winthrop; Boston is Massachusetts’s capital and the county’s traditional seat. The county had 797,936 residents in the 2020 census.

25027.description: Worcester County spans central Massachusetts from the northern to the southern state boundary and is the state’s largest county by area. Worcester is its largest city and traditional shire town.

26003.description: Alger County lies on Lake Superior in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula and contains Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore, with rock formations, waterfalls and sand dunes. The county had 8,842 residents in the 2020 census.

26005.description: Allegan County is primarily agricultural and forms the Holland micropolitan area; Allegan is its county seat. The county had 120,502 residents in the 2020 census.

26007.description: Alpena County lies beside Lake Huron and Thunder Bay, with extensive state forest and drainage through the Thunder Bay River; Alpena is its county seat. The county had 28,907 residents in the 2020 census.

26009.description: Antrim County lies beside Grand Traverse Bay and contains Torch Lake and much of the Chain of Lakes watershed; Bellaire is its county seat. The county had 23,431 residents in the 2020 census.

26011.description: Arenac County is Michigan’s third-smallest county by land area, with Standish as its county seat. The county had 15,002 residents in the 2020 census.

26013.description: Baraga County lies on Lake Superior’s Keweenaw Bay and includes much of the Huron Mountains, including Michigan’s highest natural point, Mount Arvon. The county had 8,158 residents in the 2020 census.

26015.description: Hastings is the county seat of Barry County, Michigan. The county had 62,423 residents in the 2020 census.

26017.description: Bay County lies beside Saginaw Bay, with the Saginaw River crossing Bay City and the Kawkawlin River draining much of its center. The county had 103,856 residents in the 2020 census.

26019.description: Benzie County lies along Lake Michigan and includes part of Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore and Crystal Lake; Beulah is the county seat. The county had 17,970 residents in the 2020 census.

26021.description: Berrien County occupies Michigan’s southwestern corner along Indiana and Lake Michigan, with the St. Joseph River flowing through it to the lake. The county had 154,316 residents in the 2020 census.

26023.description: Branch County forms the Coldwater micropolitan area and is Michigan’s third-smallest county by total area; Coldwater is its county seat. The county had 44,862 residents in the 2020 census.

26025.description: Calhoun County forms the Battle Creek metropolitan area, with Marshall as its county seat. The county had 134,310 residents in the 2020 census.

26027.description: Cass County is Michigan’s smallest county by total area and belongs to the South Bend-Mishawaka metropolitan area; Cassopolis is its county seat. The county had 51,589 residents in the 2020 census.

26029.description: Charlevoix County is bisected by Lake Charlevoix and includes Beaver Island in Lake Michigan; Charlevoix is its county seat and Boyne City its largest city. The county had 26,054 residents in the 2020 census.

26031.description: Cheboygan County is part of Northern Michigan, with Cheboygan as its county seat. The county had 25,579 residents in the 2020 census.

26033.description: Chippewa County occupies the eastern Upper Peninsula with shorelines on Lake Huron and Lake Superior; Sault Ste. Marie is its county seat. The county had 36,785 residents in the 2020 census.

26035.description: Clare County is considered part of both Northern and Central Michigan, with Harrison as its county seat. The county had 30,856 residents in the 2020 census.

26037.description: Clinton County is included in the Lansing-East Lansing metropolitan area; St. Johns is the county seat. The county had 79,128 residents in the 2020 census.

26039.description: Crawford County contains parts of the Au Sable, Manistee and Muskegon watersheds, with 75 percent of its area publicly owned; Grayling is the county seat. The county had 12,988 residents in the 2020 census.

26041.description: Recreation and forest products are major industries in Delta County in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula; Escanaba is its county seat. The county had 36,903 residents in the 2020 census.

26043.description: Dickinson County is one of two landlocked counties in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula and belongs to the Iron Mountain micropolitan area; Iron Mountain is its county seat. The county had 25,947 residents in the 2020 census.

26045.description: Eaton County lies in Central Michigan within the Lansing-East Lansing metropolitan area; Charlotte is its county seat. The county had 109,175 residents in the 2020 census.

26047.description: Emmet County lies at the top of Michigan’s Lower Peninsula between Lake Michigan and the Straits of Mackinac; Petoskey is its county seat. The county had 34,112 residents in the 2020 census.

26049.description: The Flint River drains most of Genesee County and feeds Mott Lake and Holloway Reservoir; Flint is the county seat and largest city. The county had 406,211 residents in the 2020 census.

26051.description: Gladwin County is Michigan’s second-smallest county by total area, with Gladwin as its county seat. The county had 25,386 residents in the 2020 census.

26053.description: Gogebic County lies in Michigan’s western Upper Peninsula between Wisconsin and Lake Superior; Bessemer is its county seat. The county had 14,380 residents in the 2020 census.

26055.description: Grand Traverse County includes the Old Mission Peninsula extending into Grand Traverse Bay and numerous inland lakes; Traverse City is its county seat. The county had 95,238 residents in the 2020 census.

26057.description: Gratiot County lies in Central Michigan, with Ithaca as county seat and Alma as its most populous city. The county had 41,761 residents in the 2020 census.

26059.description: Hillsdale County borders both Indiana and Ohio and contains the headwaters of two separate St. Joseph rivers; Hillsdale is its county seat. The county had 45,746 residents in the 2020 census.

26061.description: Houghton County includes the Portage Lift Bridge, which connects Houghton and Hancock across the waterway dividing the Keweenaw Peninsula. The county had 37,361 residents in the 2020 census.

26063.description: Huron County occupies the northern Thumb between Saginaw Bay and Lake Huron, with generally flat, heavily agricultural terrain; Bad Axe is the county seat. The county had 31,407 residents in the 2020 census.

26065.description: Ingham County has gently rolling hills crossed by the Red Cedar River and bordered by the Grand River to the west; Mason is its county seat. The county had 284,900 residents in the 2020 census.

26067.description: Ionia County belongs to the Grand Rapids-Kentwood metropolitan area, with Ionia as its county seat. The county had 66,804 residents in the 2020 census.

26069.description: Lake Huron forms Iosco County’s eastern boundary; Tawas City is the county seat in this Northern Michigan county. The county had 25,237 residents in the 2020 census.

26071.description: Iron County is one of two landlocked counties in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula; Crystal Falls is its county seat. The county had 11,631 residents in the 2020 census.

26073.description: Isabella County contains the Isabella Indian Reservation and Central Michigan University; Mount Pleasant is its county seat. The county had 64,394 residents in the 2020 census.

26075.description: Jackson County forms the Jackson metropolitan area in Michigan, with the city of Jackson as its county seat. It had 160,366 residents in the 2020 census.

26077.description: Kalamazoo County is part of the Kalamazoo–Portage metropolitan area, with Kalamazoo as its county seat. The county had 261,670 residents in 2020.

26079.description: Kalkaska County includes more than 80 lakes, extensive marshland and much of the Pere Marquette State Forest; Kalkaska is its county seat. The county had 17,939 residents in the 2020 census.

26081.description: Kent County contains Grand Rapids, Michigan’s second-largest city and the county seat, alongside company headquarters including Amway in Ada and Bissell in Walker. The county had 657,974 residents in the 2020 census.

26083.description: Keweenaw County includes Isle Royale, the northeastern Keweenaw Peninsula and intervening Lake Superior waters; Eagle River is its county seat. The county had 2,046 residents in the 2020 census.

26085.description: Baldwin is the county seat of Lake County, Michigan. The county had 12,096 residents in the 2020 census.

26087.description: Lapeer County lies in Michigan’s Thumb and contains the Flint River’s headwaters at Columbiaville; Lapeer is its county seat. The county had 88,619 residents in the 2020 census.

26089.description: Leelanau County occupies the Leelanau Peninsula between Lake Michigan and Grand Traverse Bay; its county seat is in Suttons Bay Township east of Lake Leelanau.

26091.description: Lenawee County lies in southeastern Michigan and forms the Adrian micropolitan area; Adrian is the county seat. The county had 99,423 residents in the 2020 census.

26093.description: Livingston County belongs to the Detroit metropolitan area, with Howell as its county seat and most populous city. The county had 193,866 residents in the 2020 census.

26095.description: Luce County lies in the Upper Peninsula and has a Canadian water boundary across Lake Superior; Newberry is its county seat and only incorporated community. The county had 5,339 residents in the 2020 census.

26097.description: Mackinac County lies at the boundary of Lake Huron and Lake Michigan and includes Mackinac Island; St. Ignace is the county seat and northern end of the Mackinac Bridge. The county had 10,834 residents in the 2020 census.

26099.description: Macomb County combines rural and agricultural communities in the north with suburban and urban development to the south, bordering Canada across Lake St. Clair. The county had 881,217 residents in the 2020 census.

26101.description: Manistee County lies in Northern Michigan along Lake Michigan, with Manistee as the county seat. The county had 25,032 residents in the 2020 census.

26103.description: Marquette County lies beside Lake Superior and contains part of the Huron Mountains; Marquette is the county seat of Michigan’s largest county by land area. The county had 66,017 residents in the 2020 census.

26105.description: Mason County forms the Ludington micropolitan statistical area, with Ludington as its county seat. The county had 29,052 residents in the 2020 census.

26107.description: Mecosta County’s major employers include Ferris State University, Haworth and Spectrum Health in Big Rapids, the county seat. The county had 39,714 residents in the 2020 census.

26109.description: Menominee is the county seat of Menominee County, Michigan. The county had 23,502 residents in the 2020 census.

26111.description: Midland is the county seat of Midland County, Michigan. The county had 83,494 residents in the 2020 census.

26113.description: Missaukee County lies in Northern Michigan within the Cadillac micropolitan area; Lake City is its county seat. The county had 15,052 residents in the 2020 census.

26115.description: Monroe County lies along Lake Erie and is crossed by the River Raisin and Sandy Creek; Monroe is its county seat and largest city. The county had 154,809 residents in the 2020 census.

26117.description: Montcalm County lies in West Michigan, with Stanton as county seat and Greenville as its largest city. The county had 66,614 residents in the 2020 census.

26119.description: Montmorency County is largely state forest, with numerous lakes and Thunder Bay River drainage; tourism-related services and retail support its economy. The county had 9,153 residents in the 2020 census.

26121.description: Muskegon County contains river-fed Muskegon, White and Mona lakes, each linked to Lake Michigan; Muskegon Lake also provides access for large commercial vessels. The county had 175,824 residents in 2020.

26123.description: Newaygo County has more than 230 natural lakes and extensive Manistee National Forest land; tourism is its most important economic activity, alongside agriculture and small manufacturing. The county had 49,978 residents in the 2020 census.

26125.description: Oakland County contains much of Detroit’s northern suburbs, with Pontiac as county seat and Troy as its largest city. The county had 1,274,395 residents in the 2020 census.

26127.description: Oceana County lies along Lake Michigan in West Michigan, supporting agriculture and tourism; Hart is its county seat. The county had 26,659 residents in the 2020 census.

26129.description: Ogemaw County lies in Northern Michigan, with West Branch as its county seat. The county had 20,770 residents in the 2020 census.

26131.description: Ontonagon County lies on Lake Superior in Michigan’s western Upper Peninsula; Ontonagon is its county seat. The county had 5,816 residents in the 2020 census.

26133.description: Osceola County has low rolling hills, with about half its land converted to agricultural or urban use and drainage through the Muskegon and Manistee river systems. The county had 22,891 residents in the 2020 census.

26135.description: Oscoda County lies in Northern Michigan, with the unincorporated community of Mio serving as its county seat. The county had 8,219 residents in the 2020 census.

26137.description: Otsego County contains more than 370 lakes, many formed by glacial ice, with most concentrated in its southern portion; Gaylord is the county seat. The county had 25,091 residents in the 2020 census.

26139.description: The Grand River bisects Ottawa County and empties into Lake Michigan at Grand Haven, the county seat; agriculture is a major local activity. It had 296,200 residents in 2020.

26141.description: Presque Isle County lies in Northern Michigan’s Lower Peninsula, with Rogers City as its county seat. The county had 12,982 residents in the 2020 census.

26143.description: Roscommon County contains Houghton Lake, Michigan’s largest inland lake, and part of the Au Sable State Forest; Roscommon is the county seat. The county had 23,459 residents in the 2020 census.

26145.description: Saginaw County is part of Mid-Michigan’s Flint/Tri-Cities region; major employers include Nexteer Automotive and Covenant HealthCare. The county had 190,124 residents in the 2020 census.

26147.description: St. Clair County follows the St. Clair River in Michigan’s Thumb region; Port Huron, its county seat, stands where the river meets Lake Huron. The county had 160,383 residents in the 2020 census.

26149.description: St. Joseph County lies on Michigan’s border with Indiana and entirely within the St. Joseph River watershed; Centreville is its county seat. The county had 60,939 residents in the 2020 census.

26151.description: Sanilac County lies in Michigan’s Thumb and is the Lower Peninsula’s largest county by land area; Sandusky is the county seat. The county had 40,611 residents in the 2020 census.

26153.description: Schoolcraft County lies in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula, with its county seat, Manistique, on Lake Michigan’s northern shore. The county had 8,047 residents in the 2020 census.

26155.description: The Shiawassee River flows through Corunna, Shiawassee County’s seat, and Owosso, its largest city, before continuing north into Saginaw County. The county had 68,094 residents in the 2020 census.

26157.description: Tuscola County lies in Michigan’s Thumb region, with Caro as its county seat. The county had 53,323 residents in the 2020 census.

26159.description: Van Buren County combines farmland and small towns with lakefront homes, tourism and suburban development near Kalamazoo County; Paw Paw is its county seat. The county had 75,587 residents in the 2020 census.

26161.description: Washtenaw County forms the Ann Arbor metropolitan area and contains the University of Michigan and Eastern Michigan University; Ann Arbor is its county seat. The county had 372,258 residents in the 2020 census.

26163.description: Wayne County contains Detroit, its county seat, and borders Ontario across the Detroit River and Lake St. Clair, with bridge and tunnel connections to Canada. The county had 1,793,561 residents in the 2020 census.

26165.description: Wexford County has largely wooded rolling hills, much within Manistee National Forest, and the Manistee River crossing its northern portion; Cadillac is the county seat. The county had 33,673 residents in the 2020 census.

27001.description: Aitkin County has wooded rolling hills dotted with lakes and ponds, with the Mississippi River crossing its west-central portion; Aitkin is the county seat. The county had 15,697 residents in the 2020 census.

27003.description: Anoka County has low wooded hills, with the Rum River crossing its west and joining the Mississippi along its southwestern boundary; Anoka is the county seat. The county had 363,887 residents in the 2020 census.

27005.description: Becker County combines forested hills, hundreds of lakes and fertile farmland, with part of the White Earth Indian Reservation; Detroit Lakes is the county seat. The county had 35,183 residents in the 2020 census.

27007.description: Beltrami County includes much of Red Lake and rolling wooded terrain, with the Mississippi River crossing its southern portion; Bemidji is the county seat. The county had 46,228 residents in the 2020 census.

27009.description: The Mississippi River forms Benton County’s western boundary, beside low rolling hills used for agriculture or covered with woodland; Foley is the county seat. The county had 41,379 residents in the 2020 census.

27011.description: Big Stone County lies on Minnesota’s South Dakota boundary, with Big Stone Lake and the Minnesota River along its southwest and south; Ortonville is the county seat. The county had 5,166 residents in the 2020 census.

27013.description: Blue Earth County has low rolling hills largely devoted to agriculture, with the Blue Earth River joining the Minnesota River along its northern boundary. The county had 69,112 residents in the 2020 census.

27015.description: Brown County has rolling agricultural hills, with the Minnesota River along its northern boundary and the Cottonwood River crossing its center; New Ulm is the county seat. The county had 25,912 residents in the 2020 census.

27017.description: Carlton County lies along Wisconsin, with heavily wooded rolling hills drained by the Saint Louis, Moose Horn and Nemadji rivers; Carlton is the county seat. The county had 36,207 residents in the 2020 census.

27019.description: Carver County combines agricultural rolling hills and eastern lakes, with the Minnesota River along its southern boundary; Chaska is its county seat. The county had 106,922 residents in the 2020 census.

27021.description: Cass County has wooded rolling hills heavily dotted with lakes and ponds, with the Crow Wing River along its southern boundary; Walker is the county seat. The county had 30,066 residents in the 2020 census.

27023.description: Chippewa County has low rolling agricultural hills, with the Minnesota River along its southwestern boundary and the Chippewa River crossing its west. The county had 12,598 residents in the 2020 census.

27025.description: Chisago County lies along the St. Croix River opposite Wisconsin, with agricultural rolling hills and numerous lakes; Center City is its county seat. The county had 56,621 residents in the 2020 census.

27027.description: Clay County lies along the Red River opposite North Dakota, with rolling hills and lakes in the east; Moorhead is the county seat. The county had 65,318 residents in the 2020 census.

27029.description: Clearwater County includes Lake Itasca, the Mississippi River’s source, amid wooded rolling hills and numerous lakes; Bagley is its county seat. The county had 8,524 residents in the 2020 census.

27031.description: Cook County occupies Minnesota’s rugged, heavily wooded northeastern tip between Canada and Lake Superior and contains Eagle Mountain, the state’s highest natural point. The county had 5,600 residents in the 2020 census.

27033.description: Cottonwood County has low rolling agricultural hills, with the Heron Lake Outflow crossing its southern portion; Windom is its county seat. The county had 11,517 residents in the 2020 census.

27035.description: Crow Wing County forms the Brainerd micropolitan area, with Brainerd as its county seat. The county had 66,123 residents in the 2020 census.

27037.description: Dakota County has low rolling hills descending toward river valleys, with Buck Hill in Burnsville its highest point; Hastings is the county seat. The county had 439,882 residents in the 2020 census.

27039.description: Dodge County has rolling agricultural terrain drained by the Zumbro River system and belongs to the Rochester metropolitan area; Mantorville is its county seat. The 2020 census counted 20,867 residents.

27041.description: Douglas County has rolling hills and more than 250 lakes, with prairie, savanna and deciduous forest landscapes; Alexandria is its county seat. The county had 39,006 residents in the 2020 census.

27043.description: Faribault County lies along Minnesota’s border with Iowa, with the Blue Earth River flowing north through its west-central portion; Blue Earth is the county seat. The county had 13,921 residents in the 2020 census.

27045.description: Fillmore County lies along Iowa, with rolling hills cut by gullies and drainage through the Root River system; Preston is its county seat. The county had 21,228 residents in the 2020 census.

27047.description: Freeborn County lies along Iowa, with hilly terrain and the Shell Rock River flowing south from Albert Lea Lake; Albert Lea is its county seat. The county had 30,895 residents in the 2020 census.

27049.description: Goodhue County lies along Lake Pepin opposite Wisconsin, with high river-valley bluffs and rolling hills; Red Wing is its county seat. The county had 47,582 residents in the 2020 census.

27051.description: Grant County has low rolling agricultural hills dotted with lakes, drained by the Chippewa and Mustinka rivers; Elbow Lake is its county seat. The county had 6,074 residents in the 2020 census.

27053.description: Hennepin County contains Minneapolis, its county seat, and Saint Anthony Falls on the Mississippi River; savanna soils cover more than three-quarters of its area. The county had 1,281,565 residents in the 2020 census.

27055.description: Houston County occupies Minnesota’s southeastern corner between Iowa and the Mississippi River, with hills deeply cut by drainage toward the east. The county had 18,843 residents in the 2020 census.

27057.description: Hubbard County has hilly, largely wooded terrain dotted with lakes and ponds; Park Rapids is its county seat. The county had 21,344 residents in the 2020 census.

27059.description: The Rum River flows through central Isanti County, whose hilly terrain includes gullies, lakes and ponds; Cambridge is the county seat. The county had 41,135 residents in the 2020 census.

27061.description: Itasca County has extensive forest, wetlands and more than 1,400 lakes; forestry and logging are major economic sectors, and Grand Rapids is its county seat. The county had 45,014 residents in the 2020 census.

27063.description: Jackson County lies along Iowa, with agricultural hills and the Des Moines River crossing its center toward the state boundary; Jackson is its county seat. The county had 9,989 residents in the 2020 census.

27065.description: Kanabec County has partly wooded agricultural hills cut by drainage channels, with the Snake River crossing its center; Mora is the county seat. The county had 16,032 residents in the 2020 census.

27067.description: Kandiyohi County has partly wooded rolling hills mostly devoted to agriculture, with prairie and savanna soils; Willmar is the county seat. The county had 43,732 residents in the 2020 census.

27069.description: Kittson County occupies Minnesota’s northwestern corner beside Canada and North Dakota, with agricultural low hills and the Red River along its western boundary. The county had 4,207 residents in the 2020 census.

27071.description: Koochiching County lies along the Rainy River opposite Canada, with several northward-flowing tributaries draining into it; International Falls is the county seat. The county had 12,062 residents in the 2020 census.

27073.description: Lac qui Parle County borders South Dakota, with the Minnesota River forming Marsh Lake and Lac qui Parle Reservoir along its northeastern boundary. The county had 6,719 residents in the 2020 census.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lac qui Parle County, Minnesota

27075.description: Lake County extends from Lake Superior to Ontario through heavily wooded hills and rugged terrain in the Superior National Forest; Two Harbors is the county seat. The county had 10,905 residents in the 2020 census.

27077.description: Lake of the Woods County includes the Northwest Angle, separated from the rest of the county by the lake, with land access through Manitoba; Baudette is the county seat. The county had 3,763 residents in the 2020 census.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lake of the Woods County, Minnesota

27079.description: Le Sueur County has low rolling hills dotted with lakes and ponds, with the Minnesota River along its western boundary; Le Center is the county seat. The county had 28,674 residents in the 2020 census.

27081.description: Lincoln County lies along South Dakota, with rolling hills mostly devoted to agriculture and the Lac qui Parle River crossing its northeast; Ivanhoe is the county seat. The county had 5,640 residents in the 2020 census.

27083.description: Lyon County has low rolling hills crossed by the Yellow Medicine, Redwood and Cottonwood rivers; Marshall is the county seat. The county had 25,269 residents in the 2020 census.

27085.description: McLeod County has low rolling agricultural hills and lakes, with the South Fork Crow River and Buffalo Creek flowing east through it; Glencoe is its county seat. The county had 36,771 residents in the 2020 census.

27087.description: Mahnomen County lies entirely within the White Earth Indian Reservation, with wooded, lake-dotted land in the east and agriculture elsewhere; Mahnomen is the county seat. The county had 5,411 residents in the 2020 census.

27089.description: Marshall County has low agricultural hills beside the Red River on Minnesota’s North Dakota boundary; Warren is its county seat. The county had 9,040 residents in the 2020 census.

27091.description: Martin County lies along Iowa and has low agricultural hills dotted with lakes and ponds; Fairmont is its county seat. The county had 20,025 residents in the 2020 census.

27093.description: Meeker County has low, lightly wooded hills dotted with lakes and ponds, with available land devoted to agriculture; Litchfield is the county seat. The county had 23,400 residents in the 2020 census.

27095.description: The Rum River flows south from Mille Lacs Lake through Mille Lacs County, whose wooded rolling hills include agricultural clearings; Milaca is the county seat. The county had 26,459 residents in the 2020 census.

27097.description: The Mississippi River crosses west-central Morrison County, while Camp Ripley occupies a significant area to the north; Little Falls is the county seat. The county had 34,010 residents in the 2020 census.

27099.description: Mower County lies along Iowa, with the Cedar River crossing its west and the Upper Iowa River rising within it; Austin is the county seat. The county had 40,029 residents in the 2020 census.

27101.description: Murray County has rolling agricultural hills and Buffalo Ridge, which divides Mississippi and Missouri river drainage; Slayton is its county seat. The county had 8,179 residents in the 2020 census.

27103.description: The Minnesota River defines Nicollet County’s southern boundary, beside low rolling agricultural hills; St. Peter is the county seat. The county had 34,454 residents in the 2020 census.

27105.description: Nobles County lies along Iowa on Buffalo Ridge, a divide between the Mississippi and Missouri watersheds; agriculture drives much of its economy. The county had 22,290 residents in the 2020 census.

27107.description: Norman County has agricultural low hills along the Red River opposite North Dakota, with the Wild Rice River crossing its south; Ada is the county seat. The county had 6,441 residents in the 2020 census.

27109.description: Olmsted County combines Rochester’s urban area in the Zumbro River valley with surrounding farmland and small agricultural communities; Rochester is its county seat. The county had 162,847 residents in the 2020 census.

27111.description: Otter Tail County has rolling hills, central woodland and numerous lakes, with the Otter Tail River crossing its central and western areas; Fergus Falls is the county seat. The county had 60,081 residents in the 2020 census.

27113.description: The Thief River joins the Red Lake River near Thief River Falls, Pennington County’s seat; surrounding low hills are largely agricultural. The county had 13,992 residents in the 2020 census.

27115.description: Pine County lies along the St. Croix River opposite Wisconsin, with partly wooded agricultural hills drained by the Kettle and Snake rivers. The county had 28,876 residents in the 2020 census.

27117.description: Pipestone County lies along South Dakota, with rolling agricultural hills and the Rock River rising within it; Pipestone is the county seat. The county had 9,424 residents in the 2020 census.

27119.description: Polk County lies along the Red River opposite North Dakota, with low rolling agricultural hills; Crookston is its county seat and East Grand Forks its largest city. The county had 31,192 residents in the 2020 census.

27121.description: Pope County has low rolling agricultural hills dotted with lakes, with the Chippewa River and its branches draining southward; Glenwood is the county seat. The county had 11,308 residents in the 2020 census.

27123.description: Ramsey County is Minnesota’s smallest county by area and is fully urbanized; Saint Paul, the state capital, is its county seat. The county had 552,352 residents in the 2020 census.

27125.description: The Clearwater River joins the Red Lake River near Red Lake Falls, Red Lake County’s seat; surrounding low rolling hills are devoted to agriculture. The county had 3,935 residents in the 2020 census.

27127.description: Redwood County has rolling terrain largely devoted to corn and soybeans, with the Minnesota River along its northeastern boundary and the Redwood River crossing its north. The county had 15,425 residents in the 2020 census.

27129.description: Renville County has rolling agricultural hills and scattered lakes, with the Minnesota River along its southwestern boundary; Olivia is its county seat. The county had 14,723 residents in the 2020 census.

27131.description: The Cannon River crosses central Rice County and meets the Straight River at Faribault, its county seat; surrounding terrain has low agricultural hills and lakes. The county had 67,097 residents in the 2020 census.

27133.description: Rock County occupies Minnesota’s southwestern corner between South Dakota and Iowa, with low rolling hills predominantly used for agriculture; Luverne is the county seat. The county had 9,704 residents in the 2020 census.

27135.description: Roseau County lies along Canada, with agricultural low hills, lakes and extensive southeastern woodland; the Roseau River drains its north, and Roseau is the county seat. The county had 15,331 residents in the 2020 census.

27137.description: Lake Superior, Rainy Lake, and the Canada–U.S. border shape St. Louis County’s northern landscape, while Duluth anchors its southern end. Mining and iron-ore shipping remain part of the Iron Range economy alongside forestry and tourism.

27139.description: The Minnesota River traces Scott County’s north and west edges through a broad valley that was once oak savanna and is now largely farmland. Shakopee and Prior Lake are among the county’s cities within the Minneapolis–St. Paul metropolitan area.

27141.description: The Mississippi marks Sherburne County’s southern edge, while the Rum, Elk, and St. Francis rivers cross its rolling, lake-dotted terrain. Elk River and other communities sit within the Minneapolis–St. Paul metropolitan area, alongside wooded and open landscapes.

27143.description: The Minnesota River borders Sibley County to the east, with the Rush River and its branches draining the lower county. Rolling, lake-dotted hills and a landscape devoted largely to agriculture define this south-central Minnesota county.

27145.description: The Sauk River drains central Stearns County toward the Mississippi, which follows its northeastern edge; the terrain is gently rolling, lightly wooded, and dotted with lakes. St. Cloud is the county’s largest city and seat, amid a landscape largely used for farming or development.

27147.description: The Straight River runs north through Steele County’s gently rolling, drainage-cut landscape, which is largely farmed where possible. Owatonna, the county seat, serves the surrounding agricultural area in southern Minnesota.

27149.description: The Pomme de Terre River runs south through Stevens County’s rolling, mostly agricultural terrain toward the Minnesota River. Morris, the county seat, is the main community in this sparsely populated west-central Minnesota county.

27151.description: The Minnesota River skirts Swift County’s southwest, while the Pomme de Terre and Chippewa rivers cross its rolling, largely agricultural landscape. Benson serves as the county seat, and the county also has farm-equipment manufacturing and an ethanol plant.

27153.description: The Long Prairie River crosses Todd County eastward toward the Crow Wing, which follows the county’s northeastern edge. Rolling hills, lakes, and drainage corridors make up a largely agricultural central Minnesota landscape.

27155.description: The Red River follows Traverse County’s western edge between Minnesota and North and South Dakota, and the Mustinka River drains its northern portion. Low rolling land is largely cultivated, with Wheaton serving as the county seat.

27157.description: The Mississippi River forms Wabasha County’s Wisconsin boundary, and the Zumbro and Whitewater rivers descend through its rolling terrain toward the main river. Wabasha is the county seat in this southeastern Minnesota county within the Rochester metropolitan area.

27159.description: The Crow Wing River crosses Wadena County and helps define its eastern edge, joined by the Leaf and Partridge rivers. Rolling, drainage-cut land is farmed where possible, with Wadena as the county’s principal community.

27161.description: Rivers including the Le Sueur and Little Cobb drain Waseca County westward across rolling, lake-dotted country. Agriculture occupies much of the available land, and the city of Waseca is both the county seat and a local center.

27163.description: Washington County lies between the Mississippi and St. Croix rivers, with the latter marking its Wisconsin border. Gently rolling terrain slopes toward the rivers, while Woodbury and other Minneapolis–St. Paul suburbs form a growing urban landscape alongside lakes.

27165.description: The Watonwan River and its tributaries drain Watonwan County’s gently rolling hills, dotted with small lakes and ponds. The land is largely cultivated where possible, and St. James is the county seat.

27167.description: The Bois de Sioux River marks Wilkin County’s North Dakota boundary and meets the Otter Tail River at Breckenridge to form the Red River. The low, rolling land is extensively cultivated across this western Minnesota county.

27169.description: The Mississippi River forms Winona County’s eastern border with Wisconsin. Winona is the county seat in this part of southeastern Minnesota’s Driftless Area.

27171.description: The Mississippi borders Wright County to the northeast, and numerous small lakes interrupt its gently undulating terrain. Buffalo is the county seat; the county’s Twin Cities connection and rapid population growth accompany a landscape of savanna soils and expanding communities.

27173.description: The Minnesota River follows Yellow Medicine County’s northeastern side, where the Yellow Medicine River and other streams cut through rolling land. Agriculture dominates much of the county, while the Upper Sioux Indian Reservation is located within its boundaries.

28001.description: Natchez is the county seat of Adams County, part of a micropolitan area shared with Concordia Parish, Louisiana. The county was organized in 1799, making it the first in the former Mississippi Territory.

28003.description: Alcorn County lies in northeastern Mississippi, with Corinth as its county seat and the central city of its micropolitan area. The Tuscumbia and Hatchie rivers cross the county.

28005.description: Amite County lies along Mississippi’s Louisiana boundary, with the Amite River running through it. Liberty, the county seat, serves a largely rural area connected to the McComb metropolitan region.

28007.description: The Big Black River bounds Attala County on the west, in central Mississippi. Kosciusko, the county seat, anchors a rolling inland area away from the state’s major river lowlands.

28009.description: The headwaters of the Wolf River wind across Benton County’s northern reaches, through a landscape that includes bottomland hardwood swamp. Ashland is the county seat, and the county lies within the Memphis metropolitan region.

28011.description: Bolivar County occupies the flat Mississippi Delta, or Yazoo Basin, along the state’s western edge. Its two county seats, Rosedale and Cleveland, serve a landscape historically shaped by cotton and now also by large-scale soybean, corn, and rice farming.

28013.description: Calhoun County had 13,266 residents in the 2020 census, with Pittsboro as its county seat. It lies in north-central Mississippi, with county government centered in Pittsboro.

28015.description: Carroll County spans the Mississippi Delta and wooded hill country, with the Yazoo and Big Black rivers marking its western and eastern sides. Carrollton and Vaiden are its county seats within the Greenwood regional area.

28017.description: Chickasaw County lies in north-central Mississippi and has two county seats, Houston and Okolona. Its name reflects the Chickasaw people, whose homeland included this region before forced removal in the 1830s; some Chickasaw families remained.

28019.description: The Big Black River marks Choctaw County’s northern edge as it flows toward the Mississippi. Ackerman is the county seat in this central Mississippi county, where the river forms a prominent geographic boundary.

28021.description: The Mississippi River borders Claiborne County to the west, while the Big Black River marks its northern side. Port Gibson is the county seat in a region south of the Delta, historically shaped by cotton plantations and African American communities.

28023.description: The Chickasawhay River flows north to south through eastern Clarke County on its way to the Pascagoula River system. Quitman, the county seat, is part of the Meridian metropolitan region in southeastern Mississippi.

28025.description: Clay County is part of northeastern Mississippi’s Golden Triangle, with West Point as its county seat. It was formerly designated a micropolitan area, though the federal designation ended in 2013.

28027.description: Coahoma County lies in the Mississippi Delta, a flat, fertile lowland in the state’s northwest. Clarksdale is its county seat and the center of a regional area that joined the larger Memphis-Clarksdale region in 2023.

28029.description: Copiah County lies in central Mississippi, with the Pearl River forming its eastern border. Hazlehurst, the county seat, is included in the Jackson metropolitan area.

28031.description: Covington County had 18,340 residents in the 2020 census, with Collins as its county seat.

28033.description: DeSoto County occupies Mississippi’s northwest corner and is part of the Memphis metropolitan area. Its landscape shifts from lowland once used for cotton plantations in the west to hill country in the east, with Hernando as county seat.

28035.description: Hattiesburg, the county seat and largest city, anchors Forrest County in south-central Mississippi. The county is part of the Hattiesburg metropolitan area, with urban and suburban development around the city.

28037.description: The Homochitto River bisects Franklin County diagonally from northeast to southwest, crossing an otherwise inland landscape. Meadville is the county seat in this southwestern Mississippi county.

28039.description: George County had 24,350 residents in the 2020 census, with Lucedale as its county seat. The county sits beside the Alabama state line in southeastern Mississippi.

28041.description: Greene County had 13,530 residents in the 2020 census, with Leakesville as its county seat. It occupies Mississippi’s southeastern border.

28043.description: Grenada County combines contrasting landscapes: its western half reaches into the Mississippi Delta, while the rest lies farther inland. Grenada is the county seat, and cotton was a major crop well into the twentieth century.

28045.description: Hancock County lies on the Gulf of Mexico at the Louisiana state line, with Bay St. Louis as county seat. The coast, NASA’s Stennis Space Center, and the wider Gulfport-Biloxi metropolitan area shape this southernmost county.

28047.description: Harrison County stretches along the Gulf Coast, with Gulfport and Biloxi as county seats and the Tchoutacabouffa River entering Biloxi Bay. Gulfport is Mississippi’s chief port, linking the coastal cities to the Gulf of Mexico.

28049.description: Jackson, Mississippi’s capital, and Raymond are the county seats of Hinds County, a center for the state’s professional, educational, business, and industrial activity. The Big Black and Pearl rivers frame its northwest and east sides within the Jackson metropolitan area.

28051.description: The Yazoo and Big Black rivers bound Holmes County, whose western portion lies in the Mississippi Delta and whose land was long devoted to cotton. Lexington is the county seat in this rural area between the two river systems.

28053.description: Humphreys County sits in the flat Mississippi Delta, where Belzoni is the county seat and farm-raised catfish production is a defining industry. Extensive aquaculture ponds share the county’s agricultural landscape.

28055.description: The Mississippi River forms Issaquena County’s entire western boundary, and river ports shaped its early communities. The county had 1,338 residents in the 2020 census, among the fewest east of the Mississippi.

28057.description: Itawamba County had 23,863 residents in the 2020 census, with Fulton as its county seat. The county forms part of the Tupelo micropolitan area in northeastern Mississippi.

28059.description: Jackson County occupies Mississippi’s southeastern tip, with sandy soils and Piney Woods landscapes. Pascagoula is the county seat, and 31% of the county’s area is water.

28061.description: Jasper County’s two historic county centers, Paulding in the east and Bay Springs in the west, reflect its divided settlement pattern. Timber, cattle, poultry, and oil and gas production feature in this still largely rural county within the Laurel region.

28063.description: The Mississippi River forms Jefferson County’s western border, across a largely rural county whose economy and population have declined as agriculture mechanized and people moved to cities. Fayette is the county seat.

28065.description: Jefferson Davis County had 11,321 residents in the 2020 census, with Prentiss as its county seat. It is part of the Brookhaven micropolitan area.

28067.description: Laurel and Ellisville serve as the two county seats of Jones County in southeastern Mississippi. Its rural economy draws on timber and agriculture, alongside major employers in manufacturing and other sectors.

28069.description: Kemper County lies along Mississippi’s eastern border, with De Kalb as its county seat. Scooba is home to East Mississippi Community College, linking this rural county to the Meridian regional area.

28071.description: Oxford, the county seat, anchors Lafayette County’s micropolitan area in north Mississippi. The county is also associated with the hill-country setting that inspired William Faulkner’s fictional Yoknapatawpha County.

28073.description: Lamar County is largely rural, with its northeastern quarter more developed and tied to the Hattiesburg metropolitan area. Purvis is the county seat in this south Mississippi county.

28075.description: Meridian is the county seat and largest city of Lauderdale County, part of the Meridian micropolitan area in eastern Mississippi.

28077.description: Lawrence County had 12,016 residents in the 2020 census, with Monticello as its county seat. The county lies in south-central Mississippi.

28079.description: Leake County lies near the geographic center of Mississippi, with Carthage as its county seat. The state’s 2010 population center was near Lena, within this inland county.

28081.description: Lee County had 83,343 residents in the 2020 census, with Tupelo as its county seat. Tupelo anchors the county’s micropolitan area in northeastern Mississippi.

28083.description: Leflore County lies in the Mississippi Delta, where the Yazoo River forms its southern border. Greenwood is the county seat and center of the Greenwood micropolitan area.

28085.description: Brookhaven is the county seat of Lincoln County, southwest of Jackson in Mississippi. The county had 34,907 residents in the 2020 census.

28087.description: The Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway flows through Lowndes County, with a lock and dam near Columbus. Columbus is the county seat in Mississippi’s Golden Triangle region.

28089.description: The old course of the Pearl River forms part of Madison County’s southeastern border, now altered by the Ross Barnett Reservoir. Canton is the county seat within the Jackson metropolitan area.

28091.description: Columbia is the county seat of Marion County in southern Mississippi. The county had 24,441 residents in the 2020 census.

28093.description: Holly Springs is the county seat of Marshall County in north-central Mississippi, part of the Memphis metropolitan area. The county borders Tennessee.

28095.description: Monroe County borders Alabama in northeastern Mississippi, with Aberdeen as its county seat. The county had 34,180 residents in the 2020 census.

28097.description: The Big Black River crosses the southern part of Montgomery County on its way toward the Mississippi. Winona is the county seat in this small central Mississippi county.

28099.description: Philadelphia is the county seat of Neshoba County, which is also home to the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians. The county hosts the Neshoba County Fair and harness horse races.

28101.description: Decatur is the county seat of Newton County in east-central Mississippi. The county had 21,291 residents in the 2020 census.

28103.description: Macon is the county seat of Noxubee County in east-central Mississippi. The county had 10,285 residents in the 2020 census.
