28105.description: Starkville is the county seat of Oktibbeha County and home to Mississippi State University. The county includes parts of the Black Belt and Flatwoods geological regions within the Golden Triangle.

28107.description: The Tallahatchie River bisects Panola County, just east of the Mississippi Delta. Sardis and Batesville share the county seat, a division that reflects the river’s effect on travel.

28109.description: Pearl River County includes the Picayune micropolitan area, which connects to the New Orleans region across the Louisiana state line. Poplarville is the county seat.

28111.description: New Augusta is the county seat of Perry County, moved there from Old Augusta in 1906 when the railroad arrived. The county is part of the Hattiesburg metropolitan area.

28113.description: Magnolia is the county seat of Pike County in southwestern Mississippi, on the Louisiana border. The county forms part of the McComb micropolitan area.

28115.description: The Natchez Trace Parkway crosses the southeast corner of Pontotoc County, with Pontotoc as county seat. The county is part of the Tupelo micropolitan area.

28117.description: Booneville is the county seat of Prentiss County in northeastern Mississippi. The county had 25,008 residents in the 2020 census.

28119.description: Quitman County lies in the Mississippi Delta, with Marks as its county seat. The county had 6,176 residents in the 2020 census.

28121.description: The Pearl River forms Rankin County’s western border, with several eastern Jackson suburbs within its boundaries. Brandon is the county seat, and Pearl is its largest city.

28123.description: Scott County lies within the Jackson metropolitan area, about a 45-minute drive from the state capital. Forest serves as its county seat in this central Mississippi county.

28125.description: Sharkey County lies in the Mississippi Delta, with the Yazoo River forming part of its eastern boundary. Rolling Fork is the county seat in this sparsely populated western Mississippi landscape.

28127.description: The Pearl River forms Simpson County’s western boundary, once an important transportation route in the nineteenth century. Mendenhall is the county seat, and the county is part of the Jackson metropolitan area.

28129.description: Smith County had 14,209 residents in the 2020 census, with Raleigh as its county seat. It is an inland county in central Mississippi.

28131.description: Wiggins is the county seat of Stone County, which is part of the Gulfport-Biloxi metropolitan area in southern Mississippi. The county had 18,333 residents in the 2020 census.

28133.description: Sunflower County extends lengthwise across the Mississippi Delta, with Indianola as its county seat and largest city. The flat agricultural county also contains Mississippi State Penitentiary at Parchman.

28135.description: The Tallahatchie River runs north to south through Tallahatchie County before joining the Yazoo River system farther south. Charleston and Sumner are its county seats in the Mississippi Delta.

28137.description: Tate County lies east of the Mississippi River in a fertile river valley that was developed for cotton cultivation. Senatobia is the county seat, about 40 miles south of Memphis within its metropolitan area.

28139.description: Tippah Creek crosses Tippah County from northeast to southwest toward the Tallahatchie River, with ridges alongside it shaping local divisions. Ripley is the county seat near Mississippi’s northern border.

28141.description: Woodall Mountain, Mississippi’s highest natural point, rises in Tishomingo County, which also has natural limestone outcrops. Iuka is the county seat in the state’s northeastern corner.

28143.description: Tunica County lies in the Mississippi Delta and forms part of the Memphis metropolitan area. Tunica Resorts, an unincorporated community, is known for its casino resorts.

28145.description: Union County had 27,777 residents in the 2020 census, with New Albany as its county seat. It was assembled from parts of Tippah, Pontotoc, and Lee counties in the 1870s.

28147.description: Walthall County lies in southwestern Mississippi, with Tylertown as its county seat. Magee’s Creek runs through the Holmes Water Park there and is designated an eligible state scenic stream.

28149.description: The Mississippi River borders Warren County, where Vicksburg grew as an important river port and remains the county seat. The county includes both Delta lowlands and a narrow marshy strip along the Yazoo River delta.

28151.description: Washington County occupies the Mississippi Delta beside Arkansas, with Greenville as its county seat. The county forms the Greenville micropolitan area.

28153.description: Wayne County had 19,779 residents in the 2020 census, with Waynesboro as its county seat. It is one of Mississippi’s larger counties by land area.

28155.description: The Big Black River borders Webster County on the south, in central Mississippi. Walthall is the county seat, and the county had 9,926 residents in the 2020 census.

28157.description: Wilkinson County occupies Mississippi’s southwest corner along the Mississippi River, with Woodville as its county seat. The river defines the county’s western edge across from Louisiana.

28159.description: Winston County is home to Nanih Waiya, an ancient mound long venerated by the Choctaw people and now owned by the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians. Louisville is the county seat in east-central Mississippi.

28161.description: Yalobusha County had 12,481 residents in the 2020 census and has two county seats, Water Valley and Coffeeville. The county is in north-central Mississippi.

28163.description: The Yazoo River forms Yazoo County’s western border. Yazoo City is the county seat of this Mississippi county, the state’s largest by total area.

29001.description: Adair County lies in northeastern Missouri, with Kirksville as its county seat and principal city. The county forms the Kirksville micropolitan area in a largely rural part of the state.

29003.description: Andrew County lies in northwestern Missouri near St. Joseph, with Savannah as its county seat. Its communities are linked to the St. Joseph metropolitan area and the broader Kansas City region.

29005.description: The Missouri River forms most of Atchison County’s western boundary with Nebraska, including the unusual reach around McKissick Island. Rock Port is the county seat in Missouri’s northwest corner.

29007.description: Mexico, Missouri, serves as the county seat of Audrain County in the state’s central region. The county is an inland rural area between the larger metropolitan centers of central Missouri.

29009.description: Roaring River State Park lies in the southern part of Barry County amid the Mark Twain National Forest. Cassville is the county seat in southwestern Missouri.

29011.description: Lamar is the county seat of Barton County in southwestern Missouri. The rural county’s local identity also includes the birthplace of Harry S. Truman, near Lamar.

29013.description: Bates County lies west of the Missouri River and within the Kansas City metropolitan area, with Butler as its county seat. It remains mostly rural, though its population has declined as residents moved to cities.

29015.description: Benton County had 19,394 residents in the 2020 census, with Warsaw as its county seat. It lies in west-central Missouri.

29017.description: Bollinger County spans a transition from Mississippi Delta flatlands in the south to Ozark hills in the north. Marble Hill is its only city and county seat, in a largely rural area where agriculture and construction support the economy.

29019.description: The Missouri River traces Boone County’s southern boundary, with Columbia serving as the county seat and home of the University of Missouri. Columbia anchors a growing metropolitan area in the state’s central region.

29021.description: St. Joseph is the county seat of Buchanan County in northwest Missouri, within the Kansas City combined statistical area. The county’s northern urban center and surrounding communities form part of this wider regional network.

29023.description: Butler County lies in the southeastern Ozark foothills, with Poplar Bluff as its largest city and county seat. The county forms a micropolitan area centered on this regional hub.

29025.description: Caldwell County is part of the Kansas City metropolitan area, with Kingston as its county seat. It had 8,815 residents in the 2020 census.

29027.description: The Missouri River forms Callaway County’s southern boundary, where forested hills and valleys contrast with flatter northern terrain. Fulton is the county seat, and vineyards and wineries have a history dating to German immigrants in the nineteenth century.

29029.description: Camdenton is the county seat of Camden County, Missouri. Water covers about 7.4 percent of the county’s total area, and the population was 42,745 in 2020.

29031.description: Cape Girardeau County borders the Mississippi River in southeastern Missouri, with Jackson as county seat and Cape Girardeau as its largest city. Floodplain lowlands near the river contrast with wooded, hilly terrain to the west and north.

29033.description: Carrollton is the county seat of Carroll County, Missouri. The county was organized from part of Ray County in 1833 and had 8,495 residents in 2020.

29035.description: The Current River cuts through Carter County’s rugged Ozark plateau, where wooded hills and valleys define the landscape. Van Buren is the county seat, and timber remains a major local resource.

29037.description: Cass County borders the Kansas City metropolitan area and includes part of Kansas City, Missouri. Harrisonville is the county seat, amid western Missouri communities increasingly connected to the urban region.

29039.description: Stockton Lake and several rivers contribute to Cedar County’s substantial water area in southwestern Missouri. Stockton is the county seat, and the county had 14,188 residents in the 2020 census.

29041.description: The Chariton River runs through Chariton County in north-central Missouri. Keytesville is the county seat, and the county had 7,408 residents in the 2020 census.

29043.description: Christian County’s rolling and hilly surface is drained by the James River and branches of the White River. Ozark is the county seat, and the county has grown rapidly as the Springfield metropolitan area expanded.

29045.description: Kahoka is the county seat of Clark County in Missouri’s northeastern corner. The county is part of the Fort Madison–Keokuk, Iowa–Illinois–Missouri micropolitan area.

29047.description: Clay County contains northern Kansas City suburbs and part of Kansas City itself, with Liberty as its county seat. Its metropolitan landscape also includes the Midwest National Air Center near Excelsior Springs.

29049.description: Plattsburg is the county seat of Clinton County, part of the Kansas City metropolitan area. The county had 21,184 residents in 2020.

29051.description: Jefferson City, Missouri’s capital and Cole County’s largest city, lies south of the Missouri River. The county forms part of the Jefferson City metropolitan area and contains the state’s 2010 population center near Wardsville.

29053.description: Boonville is the county seat of Cooper County in central Missouri. Part of the Columbia metropolitan area, the county had 17,103 residents in 2020.

29055.description: Steelville is the county seat of Crawford County in east-central Missouri, where the U.S. population’s mean center was located in 1990. A portion of Sullivan also falls within the St. Louis metropolitan area.

29057.description: Dade County had 7,569 residents in the 2020 census, with Greenfield as its county seat. It is located in southwestern Missouri.

29059.description: Dallas County had 17,071 residents in the 2010 census, with Buffalo as its county seat. The county is part of the Springfield metropolitan area.

29061.description: Gallatin is the county seat of Daviess County in north-central Missouri. The town of Jamesport is home to the state’s largest Amish community, adding a distinctive settlement pattern to the rural county.

29063.description: Maysville is the county seat of DeKalb County in northwest Missouri, part of the St. Joseph metropolitan area. The county’s communities connect this rural landscape to the wider Kansas City region.

29065.description: Salem, the county seat, grew as a center for producing and shipping railroad ties from the surrounding Ozark forests. Timber remains an important local resource in Dent County, east-central Missouri.

29067.description: Ava is the county seat and only incorporated community in Douglas County, in south-central Missouri. The county had 11,578 residents in the 2020 census.

29069.description: Dunklin County occupies Missouri’s Bootheel, a low-lying southeastern extension of the state. The St. Francis River reaches Missouri’s lowest point here before flowing into Arkansas, and Kennett is the county seat.

29071.description: Franklin County lies along the south side of the Missouri River within the St. Louis metropolitan area. The Bourbeuse River cuts a winding valley through the county, where wineries are part of the Missouri Rhineland.

29073.description: Gasconade County lies south of the Missouri River in the Missouri Rhineland, with Hermann as its county seat. The area includes the Hermann and Ozark Highlands American Viticultural Areas, known for vineyards and wineries.

29075.description: Gentry County had 6,162 residents in the 2020 census, with Albany as its county seat. It lies in northwestern Missouri.

29077.description: Springfield, the county seat and largest city, anchors Greene County in the Ozark Mountains and foothills. The county is the state’s largest population center outside the Kansas City and St. Louis metropolitan areas.

29079.description: Trenton is the county seat of Grundy County, Missouri. The county was organized in 1841 from part of Livingston County and had 9,808 residents in 2020.

29081.description: Bethany is the county seat of Harrison County in northwestern Missouri. The county had 8,157 residents in the 2020 census.

29083.description: Clinton is the county seat of Henry County in western Missouri. The county had 21,946 residents in the 2020 census.

29085.description: The Pomme de Terre Dam forms Lake Pomme de Terre just south of Hermitage, and Truman Reservoir extends from the county’s northern border to the city. Hermitage is the county seat.

29087.description: Oregon is the county seat of Holt County in northwestern Missouri. The county had 4,223 residents in 2020, and water covers about 1.6 percent of its total area.

29089.description: The Missouri River forms Howard County’s southern boundary, with Fayette as the county seat. The area is part of Little Dixie, a historic settlement region, and the Columbia metropolitan area.

29091.description: West Plains is the largest city and county seat of Howell County in southern Missouri. The county forms a micropolitan area and is among the state’s largest by land area.

29093.description: Ironton and the surrounding Arcadia Valley sit within Iron County, encircled by the Saint Francois Mountains of the Ozarks. Taum Sauk Mountain, Missouri’s highest point, and several state parks make this a notably mountainous county.

29095.description: Kansas City and Independence are Jackson County’s two county seats, and the Missouri River forms much of its northern edge. This highly urbanized western county includes a large part of the Kansas City metropolitan area.

29097.description: Joplin is Jasper County’s largest city, while Carthage is its county seat in southwestern Missouri. The county forms part of the Joplin metropolitan area.

29099.description: The Mississippi River marks Jefferson County’s eastern border, where St. Louis suburbs extend southward. Hillsboro is the county seat in this eastern Missouri metropolitan county.

29101.description: Warrensburg is the county seat of Johnson County in western Missouri. The county forms a micropolitan area that is also included in the broader Kansas City combined region.

29103.description: Edina is the county seat of Knox County in northeastern Missouri, one of the state’s least populous counties. Its population was 3,744 in the 2020 census.

29105.description: Lebanon is the county seat of Laclede County, which forms its own micropolitan area in southern Missouri. The county had 36,039 residents in the 2020 census.

29107.description: Lexington is the county seat of Lafayette County in western Missouri, part of the Kansas City metropolitan area. The county had 32,984 residents in 2020.

29109.description: Mount Vernon is the county seat of Lawrence County in the Ozarks of southwestern Missouri. The county also contains the Ozark Cavefish National Wildlife Refuge.

29111.description: Monticello is the county seat of Lewis County in northeastern Missouri, part of the Quincy metropolitan area across the Mississippi. Agriculture, government services, and higher education contribute to its diversified rural economy.

29113.description: The Mississippi River forms Lincoln County’s eastern border with Illinois, and Troy is its county seat. The county lies within the St. Louis metropolitan area, where rural communities meet the region’s outer suburbs.

29115.description: Linneus is the county seat of Linn County in northern Missouri. The county had 11,874 residents in 2020.

29117.description: Chillicothe is the county seat of Livingston County in northwestern Missouri. The county had 14,557 residents in 2020.

29119.description: Pineville is the county seat of McDonald County in the southwestern corner of Missouri. The county had 23,303 residents in the 2020 census.

29121.description: Macon is the county seat of Macon County in northern Missouri. The county had 15,209 residents in 2020.

29123.description: Fredericktown is both the county seat and largest city in Madison County, part of Missouri’s Lead Belt. Mining has long shaped this area, which includes one of the oldest lead mines west of the Mississippi.

29125.description: Vienna is the county seat of Maries County in central Missouri. The county takes its name from the Maries and Little Maries rivers, whose French-derived name refers to marshes, lakes, or ponds.

29127.description: Marion County has two courthouses, in Palmyra and Hannibal, and is part of the Hannibal micropolitan area. Palmyra is the county seat in northeastern Missouri.

29129.description: Princeton is the county seat of Mercer County in northwestern Missouri. The county is among the state’s least populous, with 3,538 residents in the 2020 census.

29131.description: Tuscumbia is the county seat of Miller County in Missouri’s northern Ozarks. The county’s communities occupy an inland setting within the Ozark region.

29133.description: The Mississippi River forms the eastern border of Mississippi County, the easternmost county in Missouri. Charleston is its largest city and county seat, with 12,577 residents in 2020.

29135.description: California is the county seat of Moniteau County within the Jefferson City metropolitan area. The county takes its name from Moniteau Creek in central Missouri.

29137.description: Paris is the county seat of Monroe County in northeastern Missouri. The county is also known as the birthplace of Mark Twain.

29139.description: Montgomery County lies in east-central Missouri, about midway between Columbia and St. Louis. Montgomery City is the county seat in a portion of the Missouri Rhineland.

29141.description: Versailles is the county seat of Morgan County in central Missouri. The county is an inland part of the state’s central region.

29143.description: New Madrid County occupies the Bootheel, with Portageville as its largest city and New Madrid as county seat. A Mississippi River oxbow wraps around Kentucky Bend, an unusual border feature along the county’s eastern side.

29145.description: Neosho is the county seat of Newton County in southwestern Missouri, within the Joplin metropolitan area. The county had 58,648 residents in the 2020 census.

29147.description: Nodaway River divides western Nodaway County, while rolling hills and several rivers shape the surrounding landscape. Maryville is the county seat in northwest Missouri, near the Iowa border.

29149.description: Oregon County contains more Mark Twain National Forest land than any other Missouri county, along with the state’s largest federally protected wilderness area. The Eleven Point River, Missouri’s only National Wild and Scenic River, runs through this Ozark county.

29151.description: Linn is the county seat of Osage County, within the Jefferson City metropolitan area. The county’s geography and vineyards connect it to the Missouri Rhineland along the river valley.

29153.description: Gainesville is the county seat of Ozark County in southern Missouri, with Arkansas along its southern edge. The county takes its name from the Ozark Mountains that define the region.

29155.description: The Mississippi River forms Pemiscot County’s eastern border in Missouri’s southeastern Bootheel. Caruthersville is the county seat, and the lowland landscape has supported cotton and other commodity crops.

29157.description: Perry County spans Mississippi River lowlands and higher uplands, with the low-lying area including productive farmland near the river. Perryville is the county seat in southeastern Missouri.

29159.description: Sedalia is the county seat of Pettis County and home to the Missouri State Fair. The Lamine River and its branches drain this west-central Missouri county, which forms the Sedalia micropolitan area.

29161.description: Rolla is the largest city and county seat of Phelps County in central Missouri. Vineyards and wineries in the county are part of the Ozark Highlands wine region, and Rolla anchors its micropolitan area.

29163.description: The Mississippi River borders Pike County to the east, with Bowling Green as the county seat. The county is part of Missouri’s eastern river corridor.

29165.description: The Missouri River forms part of Platte County’s southwestern border with Kansas, while Kansas City International Airport lies within the county. Platte City is the county seat in the Kansas City metropolitan area.

29167.description: Bolivar is the county seat of Polk County in southwestern Missouri, within the Springfield metropolitan area. The county’s communities are linked to Springfield, the region’s largest urban center.

29169.description: Fort Leonard Wood occupies part of Pulaski County, where it accounts for nearly one-third of the micropolitan area’s population. Waynesville is the county seat in central Missouri.

29171.description: Unionville is the county seat of Putnam County in north-central Missouri. The county had 4,681 residents in the 2020 census.

29173.description: New London is the county seat of Ralls County in northeastern Missouri, within the Hannibal micropolitan area. The county is part of the wider Quincy-Hannibal regional area.

29175.description: Huntsville is the county seat of Randolph County in northern Missouri. The county forms the Moberly micropolitan area, which is part of the larger Columbia regional area.

29177.description: Richmond is the county seat of Ray County in northwestern Missouri, within the Kansas City metropolitan area. The county lies in the state’s western region.

29179.description: Johnson’s Shut-Ins State Park is a major destination in Reynolds County, part of the Ozark foothills and Lead Belt. Centerville is the county seat in this southeastern Missouri county.

29181.description: The Current River and Mark Twain National Forest are among the main outdoor destinations in Ripley County’s Ozark landscape. Doniphan is the county seat in southern Missouri.

29183.description: St. Charles County includes northwestern St. Louis suburbs and a rural edge along the Missouri River bluffs. St. Charles is the county seat, and vineyards in the county are part of the Augusta wine region.

29185.description: Osceola is the county seat and Appleton City the largest city of St. Clair County in western Missouri. Water covers about 4.6 percent of its total area.

29186.description: Ste. Genevieve County borders Illinois across the Mississippi River and includes one of the oldest French colonial settlements west of that river. Ste. Genevieve is the largest city and county seat.

29187.description: Farmington is the largest city and county seat of St. Francois County in Missouri’s Lead Belt. The county forms the Farmington micropolitan area, linked to the wider St. Louis region.

29189.description: St. Louis County wraps around the independent City of St. Louis, bounded by the Mississippi, Missouri, and Meramec rivers. Clayton is the county seat and Florissant its largest city within the St. Louis metropolitan area.

29195.description: The Missouri River forms Saline County’s northern border, joined there by the Grand River. Marshall is the county seat in this Little Dixie county, part of the region settled by migrants from the Upper South.

29197.description: Lancaster is the county seat of Schuyler County on the Iowa border in northeastern Missouri. It is part of the Kirksville micropolitan area.

29199.description: Memphis is the county seat of Scotland County in northeastern Missouri, along the Iowa border. The county had 4,716 residents in the 2020 census.

29201.description: The Mississippi River forms Scott County’s eastern border with Illinois, while Benton is the county seat. Scott County forms the Sikeston micropolitan area in southeastern Missouri.

29203.description: Shannon County is Missouri’s second-largest county by area, with Eminence as its county seat. It had 7,031 residents in the 2020 census.

29205.description: Shelbyville is the county seat of Shelby County in northeastern Missouri. The county had 6,103 residents in 2020.

29207.description: Bloomfield is the county seat of Stoddard County in southeastern Missouri. The county had 28,672 residents in the 2020 census.

29209.description: Galena is the county seat of Stone County in southwestern Missouri. The county was part of the Branson micropolitan area until 2023.

29211.description: Medicine, Locust, East Locust, Yellow, and Spring creeks drain Sullivan County in northern Missouri. Milan is the county seat near the divide between the Chariton and Grand river watersheds.

29213.description: Taney County includes Branson and Table Rock, well-known tourism destinations in southwestern Missouri. Forsyth is the county seat, and the county forms the Branson micropolitan area.

29215.description: Texas County is Missouri’s largest county by area, with Houston as its county seat. The county is in southern Missouri and contains the 2010 center of the U.S. population.

29217.description: Vernon County lies on Missouri’s western border with Kansas, with Nevada as its county seat. The Four Rivers Conservation Area includes restored wetland in the county’s northern part.

29219.description: Warren County sits north of the Missouri River within the St. Louis metropolitan area, with Warrenton as county seat. Vineyards along Route 94 are part of the Missouri Rhineland.

29221.description: Potosi is the largest city and county seat of Washington County in southeastern Missouri. The county lies inland within the state’s southeastern region.

29223.description: Greenville is the county seat of Wayne County in Missouri’s Ozark foothills. Piedmont is the county’s most populous community, followed by Greenville and Williamsville.

29225.description: Webster County straddles the divide between the Missouri and White river watersheds, with headwaters of four rivers rising there. Marshfield is the county seat within the Springfield metropolitan area.

29227.description: Worth County lies along the Iowa border in northwestern Missouri, with Grant City as its county seat. It had 1,973 residents in the 2020 census, the fewest in the state.

29229.description: Wright County lies in the Salem Plateau of the Ozarks, with moderately hilly terrain drained by the Gasconade and North Fork rivers. Hartville is the county seat and near the 2020 U.S. population center.

29510.description: The independent City of St. Louis lies near the confluence of the Mississippi and Missouri rivers. Its 2020 population was 301,578, and the city anchors a metropolitan region extending into Illinois.

30001.description: Beaverhead County is Montana’s largest county by area, with Dillon as its county seat. The Continental Divide traces much of its perimeter and all of its Idaho border, while the Big Hole River crosses the county.

30003.description: Most of Big Horn County lies within the Crow and Northern Cheyenne reservations, beneath the Big Horn, Pryor, and Wolf mountain ranges. Hardin is the county seat, and coal mining and agriculture shape its economy.

30005.description: The Milk River and the Bears Paw and Little Rocky mountains mark Blaine County’s landscape along Montana’s border with Saskatchewan. Chinook is the county seat, and agriculture is its main industry.

30007.description: Canyon Ferry Lake lies between the Big Belt and Elkhorn mountains in Broadwater County, with Townsend as county seat. Agriculture is a primary industry, while the lake supports recreation and local irrigation.

30009.description: Granite Peak, Montana’s highest mountain, rises in the Beartooth Mountains of Carbon County, while the Pryor Mountains and Big Horn River mark its eastern side. Red Lodge is the county seat within the Billings metropolitan area.

30011.description: Medicine Rocks State Park lies north of Ekalaka, where weathering has shaped distinctive rock formations. Ekalaka is the county seat in southeastern Montana.

30013.description: The Missouri and Sun rivers meet at Great Falls in Cascade County, framed by the Rocky, Little Belt, and Highwood mountains. Great Falls is the county seat and center of the county’s metropolitan area.

30015.description: Fort Benton stands on the Missouri River in north-central Montana, where it was once an important port. Chouteau County also includes part of the Lewis and Clark National Forest and produces more winter wheat than any other county in Montana.

30017.description: Miles City is the county seat and largest town of Custer County in southeastern Montana. Agriculture, including dryland farming and cattle raising, is the main part of the local economy.

30019.description: Rolling plains and the Poplar River characterize Daniels County along Montana’s northern border with Saskatchewan. Scobey is the county seat, and cattle and dryland wheat are major income sources.

30021.description: Glendive is the county seat of Dawson County in eastern Montana. Dryland grain, coal, and oil and gas production feature in the county’s economy.

30023.description: Anaconda is the county seat of Deer Lodge County, whose consolidated city-county government dates to 1977. The county includes the Anaconda Mountain Range, Georgetown Lake, and the Mount Haggin Wildlife Management Area.

30025.description: Baker is the county seat of Fallon County, which had 3,049 residents in the 2020 census.

30027.description: Lewistown is the county seat of Fergus County, in a region that developed around agriculture and mining. The county had 11,446 residents in the 2020 census.

30029.description: Flathead County includes much of Flathead Lake, Flathead Valley, and the Flathead River, features shaped by glacial activity. Kalispell is the county seat and center of the county’s micropolitan area near the Canadian border.

30031.description: Bozeman is the county seat of Gallatin County, set between the Bridger Range and the Gallatin Range and River. The county also includes the West Yellowstone entrance to Yellowstone National Park and Big Sky Resort.

30033.description: Jordan is the county seat of Garfield County, whose low population density reflects its wide-open eastern Montana setting. The county is notable for discoveries of several major Tyrannosaurus rex specimens.

30035.description: Glacier County spans the transition from the Great Plains to the Rocky Mountains and includes Glacier National Park, Lewis and Clark National Forest, and the Blackfeet Indian Reservation. Its northern border meets Alberta, with several international crossings.

30037.description: Ryegate is the county seat of Golden Valley County, one of Montana’s least populous counties. It had 823 residents in the 2020 census.

30039.description: Philipsburg is the county seat of Granite County in western Montana. The county had 3,309 residents in the 2020 census.

30041.description: Hill County lies along Montana’s northern border with Alberta and Saskatchewan, with Havre as its county seat. Part of the Rocky Boy Indian Reservation and the nation’s largest county park are within its boundaries.

30043.description: Boulder is the county seat of Jefferson County, part of the Helena micropolitan area. The county had 12,085 residents in the 2020 census.

30045.description: Judith Basin County sits in a basin between the Highwood, Big Snowy, and Little Belt mountains. Stanford is the county seat, and agriculture is the main basis of the economy.

30047.description: More than two-thirds of Lake County’s land lies within the Flathead Indian Reservation. Polson is the county seat in northwestern Montana.

30049.description: Helena, Montana’s capital and Lewis and Clark County’s largest city, is also its county seat. The county forms the Helena micropolitan area in central Montana.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lewis and Clark County, Montana

30051.description: Liberty County borders Alberta along Montana’s northern line, and Tiber Dam is a recreation destination in its southwest corner. Chester is the county seat.

30053.description: Lincoln County is heavily wooded and mountainous, sharing Montana’s northern border with British Columbia. Libby is the county seat, and the Kootenai River reaches the state’s lowest point where it flows into Idaho.

30055.description: Circle is the county seat of McCone County in eastern Montana. The county had 1,729 residents in the 2020 census.

30057.description: Virginia City is the county seat of Madison County in southwestern Montana. The county had 8,623 residents in the 2020 census.

30059.description: White Sulphur Springs is the county seat of Meagher County in central Montana. The state’s 2010 population center was located within the county.

30061.description: Superior is the county seat of Mineral County in western Montana. The county’s seat and administrative center lie in a sparsely populated part of the state.

30063.description: Missoula is both the county seat and largest city of Missoula County, a growing regional trade center in western Montana. The county’s economy includes the University of Montana, regional hospitals, and the U.S. Forest Service.

30065.description: Roundup is the county seat of Musselshell County in south-central Montana. The county had 4,730 residents in 2020, and water covers about 0.1 percent of its total area.

30067.description: Livingston is the county seat of Park County, where a small part of Yellowstone National Park lies. Granite Peak, Montana’s highest natural point, is also within the county.

30069.description: The Musselshell River forms the eastern boundary of Petroleum County, within the Missouri Plateau of the Great Plains. Winnett is the county seat, and petroleum and cattle raising are principal economic activities.

30071.description: Phillips County stretches from the Canadian border with Saskatchewan to the Missouri River, which forms its southern edge. Malta is the county seat, and the county is Montana’s second largest by land area.

30073.description: Conrad is the county seat of Pondera County, Montana. The county had 5,898 residents in 2020, and water covers about 1 percent of its total area.

30075.description: Broadus is the county seat of Powder River County in southeastern Montana. The county’s very low water area reflects a predominantly land-based landscape.

30077.description: Deer Lodge is the county seat of Powell County in western Montana. Avon and nearby communities are set in the county’s countryside.

30079.description: Terry is the county seat of Prairie County, whose name reflects the region’s predominant landscape. The county had 1,088 residents in the 2020 census.

30081.description: Hamilton is the county seat of Ravalli County in the Bitterroot Valley, between the Sapphire Mountains to the east and Bitterroot Mountains to the west. Agriculture and timber form much of the local economy.

30083.description: Sidney is the county seat of Richland County in eastern Montana. Ranching remains widespread, while oil production grew after the discovery of the Elm Coulee field in 2000.

30085.description: Three-fourths of Roosevelt County lies within the Fort Peck Indian Reservation, with Wolf Point as county seat. The county had 10,794 residents in the 2020 census.

30087.description: Forsyth is the county seat of Rosebud County in southeastern Montana, which includes part of Custer National Forest. It is among Montana’s largest counties by land area.

30089.description: The Clark Fork River crosses Sanders County between the Bitterroot and Cabinet mountains, part of the Coeur d’Alene Mountains. Thompson Falls is the county seat in western Montana along the Idaho border.

30091.description: Plentywood is the county seat of Sheridan County on Montana’s northern border with Saskatchewan. The county’s 2020 population was 3,539.

30093.description: Butte is the county seat of Silver Bow County, whose city and county governments consolidated in 1977 as Butte-Silver Bow. The county forms a micropolitan area and is Montana’s smallest by area.

30095.description: Columbus is the county seat of Stillwater County in southern Montana. The county had 8,963 residents in the 2020 census.

30097.description: Big Timber is the county seat of Sweet Grass County in south-central Montana. The county had 3,678 residents in the 2020 census.

30099.description: Choteau is the county seat of Teton County in northwestern Montana. The county had 6,226 residents in the 2020 census.

30101.description: Shelby is the county seat of Toole County, which shares Montana’s northern border with Canada. The Marias River runs through the county’s southern part, including a stretch designated as Marias River State Park.

30103.description: Hysham is the county seat of Treasure County in eastern Montana. The county had 762 residents in the 2020 census.

30105.description: Glasgow is the county seat of Valley County, on Montana’s border with Saskatchewan. Agriculture is its main economic activity, and it is the state’s fourth-largest county by total area.

30107.description: Harlowton is the county seat of Wheatland County in central Montana. The county had 2,069 residents in the 2020 census.

30109.description: Wibaux County shares Montana’s eastern border region and is among the state’s smallest counties by area. The town of Wibaux is its county seat.

30111.description: The Yellowstone River runs diagonally across Yellowstone County, with Billings as both county seat and largest city. The county forms the Billings metropolitan area and is Montana’s most populous county.

31001.description: Hastings is the county seat and largest city of Adams County in south-central Nebraska. The county forms its own micropolitan area.

31003.description: Neligh is the county seat and largest city of Antelope County, which also contains the Ashfall Fossil Beds National Natural Landmark. The county is in northeastern Nebraska.

31005.description: Arthur County is one of Nebraska’s least populous counties, with 434 residents in the 2020 census. Arthur is both its county seat and only incorporated community.

31007.description: Harrisburg is the county seat and largest community of Banner County, where no incorporated municipalities exist. The county lies in the Great Plains and includes buttes and Pumpkin Creek Valley.

31009.description: Brewster is the county seat of Blaine County, while Dunning is its largest village. The county had 431 residents in the 2020 census.

31011.description: Albion is the county seat and largest city of Boone County in north-central Nebraska. Its population was 5,386 in the 2020 census.

31013.description: Alliance is the county seat and largest city of Box Butte County in western Nebraska. The county had 10,842 residents in the 2020 census.

31015.description: Butte is the county seat of Boyd County, while Spencer is its largest village. The county’s 2020 population was 1,810.

31017.description: Ainsworth is the county seat and largest city of Brown County, in Nebraska’s Outback region. The county had 2,903 residents in the 2020 census.

31019.description: Kearney is the county seat and largest city of Buffalo County in central Nebraska. The county forms the Kearney micropolitan area.

31021.description: The Missouri River forms much of Burt County’s eastern boundary with Iowa, though shifts in the river have left small portions of the county east of its channel. Tekamah is the county seat and largest city.

31023.description: David City is the county seat and largest city of Butler County in eastern Nebraska. The county also contains the state’s 2020 center of population near Garrison.

31025.description: Cass County lies along Nebraska’s eastern edge across the Missouri River from Iowa, with Plattsmouth as county seat and largest city. It is part of the Omaha–Council Bluffs metropolitan area.

31027.description: Cedar County borders South Dakota across the Missouri River at Nebraska’s northern edge. Hartington is the county seat, and the county’s name reflects the cedar groves in the area.

31029.description: Frenchman Creek crosses Chase County from west to southeast, exposing limestone outcrops between Enders and Wauneta. Imperial is the county seat on Nebraska’s western edge beside Colorado.

31031.description: Cherry County is Nebraska’s largest county by area and borders South Dakota to the north. Valentine is its county seat and largest city.

31033.description: Sidney is the county seat of Cheyenne County on Nebraska’s southern border with Colorado. The county is in the state’s southwest.

31035.description: Clay Center is the county seat of Clay County in south-central Nebraska. The county had 6,104 residents in the 2020 census.

31037.description: Schuyler is the county seat and largest city of Colfax County in eastern Nebraska. The county had 10,582 residents in the 2020 census.

31039.description: West Point is the county seat of Cuming County in eastern Nebraska. The county’s 2020 census population was 9,013.

31041.description: Broken Bow is the county seat of Custer County, Nebraska’s second-largest county by area. The county had 10,545 residents in the 2020 census.

31043.description: The Missouri River forms Dakota County’s northeastern boundary with Iowa and South Dakota, beside rolling prairies and bottomlands. Dakota City is the county seat, and South Sioux City is its largest city.

31045.description: Dawes County shares Nebraska’s northern border with South Dakota, with Chadron as its county seat and largest city. Residents use Mountain Time, unlike most of the state.

31047.description: Lexington is the county seat and largest city of Dawson County near the center of Nebraska. The county forms a micropolitan area.

31049.description: Chappell is the county seat of Deuel County on Nebraska’s southern border with Colorado. Residents use Mountain Time, unlike eastern parts of the state.

31051.description: Ponca is the county seat of Dixon County on Nebraska’s northeastern edge across the Missouri River from South Dakota. The county is part of the Sioux City metropolitan area.

31053.description: The Elkhorn River crosses northeastern Dodge County, while the Platte River follows its southern boundary. Fremont is the county seat and largest city in a micropolitan area tied to Omaha.

31055.description: Omaha is both the county seat and largest city of Douglas County on Nebraska’s eastern border across the Missouri River from Iowa. The county anchors the Omaha–Council Bluffs metropolitan area.

31057.description: Dundy County occupies Nebraska’s southwest corner, between Colorado and Kansas. Benkelman is the county seat, and the county had 1,654 residents in the 2020 census.

31059.description: The Big Blue River watershed drains Fillmore County through the West Fork of the Big Blue, Turkey Creek, and Little Blue. Geneva is the county seat in the eastern portion of Nebraska.

31061.description: The Republican River flows east through the southern part of Franklin County along Nebraska’s border with Kansas. Franklin is the county seat.

31063.description: Stockville is the county seat of Frontier County in south-central Nebraska. The county’s 2020 population was 2,519.

31065.description: The Republican River crosses Furnas County in southern Nebraska near the Kansas border. Beaver City is the county seat.

31067.description: The Big Blue River runs south through Gage County toward Kansas, with Beatrice as county seat and largest city. The county forms the Beatrice micropolitan area.

31069.description: The North Platte River crosses the southern part of Garden County, whose residents use Mountain Time. Oshkosh is the county seat.

31071.description: The North Loup River crosses the southwest corner of Garfield County in central Nebraska. Burwell is the county seat.

31073.description: The Platte River flows through the northern part of Gosper County, which is part of the Lexington micropolitan area. Elwood is the county seat.

31075.description: Grant County lies in the Sandhills, with rolling hillocks and small lakes and reservoirs. Hyannis is its county seat and largest village.

31077.description: The Cedar and North Loup rivers cross opposite corners of Greeley County in central Nebraska. Greeley Center is the county seat.

31079.description: The Platte and South Loup rivers cross Hall County, whose county seat and largest city is Grand Island. The county forms the Grand Island metropolitan area.

31081.description: The Platte River follows Hamilton County’s northwestern edge, beside Merrick County. Aurora is the county seat within the Grand Island metropolitan area.

31083.description: The Republican River crosses Harlan County, where it is impounded by Harlan County Lake at the southeastern corner. Alma is the county seat amid gently rolling low hills.

31085.description: Hayes County has hilly terrain with flattened hilltops used for center-pivot irrigation, and Red Willow Creek drains its upper elevations. Hayes Center is the county seat.

31087.description: The Republican River flows east through Hitchcock County’s rolling low hills, whose flatter tops are used for agriculture. Trenton is the county seat.

31089.description: The Niobrara River follows Holt County’s northern line, while the Elkhorn River crosses its upper center. O’Neill is the county seat and largest city in this large north-central county.

31091.description: The Middle Loup River flows east across Hooker County’s low rolling hills. Mullen is both its county seat and largest village.

31093.description: The Upper and Middle Loup rivers meet near the center of Howard County, where rolling hilltops are used for agriculture. St. Paul is the county seat within the Grand Island metropolitan area.

31095.description: The Little Blue River crosses Jefferson County’s rolling hills toward Kansas, with flatter hilltops used largely for agriculture. Fairbury is the county seat on the state’s southern line.

31097.description: The Big Nemaha River flows southeast through Johnson County’s low rolling hills, whose level tops are mostly farmed. Tecumseh is the county seat.

31099.description: The Platte River follows the northern boundary of Kearney County, whose gently rolling low hills are mostly used for agriculture. Minden is the county seat, and the county is part of the Kearney micropolitan area.

31101.description: Lake McConaughy and the North and South Platte rivers mark Keith County’s landscape of low rolling hills. Ogallala is the county seat, with agricultural land concentrated in flatter areas.

31103.description: The Keya Paha River flows east through Keya Paha County’s low rolling hills, where level ground is used for agriculture. Springview is the county seat and largest village near South Dakota.

31105.description: Kimball County’s rolling hills slope east, with drier farming and some center-pivot irrigation on flatter land. Kimball is the county seat and largest city in western Nebraska.

31107.description: The Missouri River borders Knox County to the northeast, where Lewis and Clark Lake lies below Gavins Point Dam. Center is the county seat, and most of the flatter land is used for agriculture.

31109.description: Lincoln, Nebraska’s capital and largest city, is also the county seat of Lancaster County. The county is part of the Lincoln metropolitan area.

31111.description: The North and South Platte rivers join near North Platte, then continue east through Lincoln County. North Platte is the county seat in a county of mixed-grass prairie, dunes, agriculture, irrigation, and cattle ranching.

31113.description: Stapleton is the county seat and largest village of Logan County in central Nebraska. The county’s runoff drains east-northeast toward the Dismal River.

31115.description: The Calamus and North Loup rivers cross Loup County, whose low corrugated flatland is sparsely used for agriculture. Taylor is the county seat.

31117.description: Tryon is the county seat and largest city of McPherson County in central Nebraska. The county had 399 residents in the 2020 census, the fewest in the state.

31119.description: The Elkhorn River runs east across Madison County’s gently rolling landscape, much of which is farmed. Madison is the county seat, and Norfolk is the largest city.

31121.description: The Platte River borders Merrick County on the southeast, while Prairie Creek crosses its center and drains into the Platte. Central City is the county seat in the Grand Island metropolitan area.

31123.description: The North Platte River crosses Morrill County and passes Bridgeport, its county seat. Chimney Rock, a prominent rock formation, is also within the county’s rolling hills.

31125.description: The Loup River crosses Nance County northeastward, joined near Fullerton by the Cedar River. Fullerton is the county seat amid rolling hills.

31127.description: The Missouri River forms most of Nemaha County’s eastern boundary with Missouri. Auburn is the county seat in this eastern Nebraska county.

31129.description: The Republican River crosses Nuckolls County’s southwest corner, while smaller streams drain its upper part toward Crooked Creek. Nelson is the county seat along Nebraska’s southern border with Kansas.

31131.description: Otoe County’s rolling hills descend toward the Missouri River basin, with Nebraska City as county seat. The river forms the county’s eastern boundary, and fertile soils support crops and fruit orchards.

31133.description: Pawnee County lies along Nebraska’s southern border with Kansas, with rolling hills and local drainages. Pawnee City is the county seat.

31135.description: Perkins County’s arid, low rolling hills slope southeast toward Colorado. Grant is the county seat, and flatter land is used for agriculture, often with center-pivot irrigation.

31137.description: The Platte River follows the northern boundary of Phelps County, where the low rolling hills slope toward its basin. Holdrege is the county seat in an agricultural county in south-central Nebraska.

31139.description: The North Fork of the Elkhorn River crosses Pierce County’s low rolling hills, while Dry Fork drains its western part. Pierce is the county seat, and the county is part of the Norfolk micropolitan area.

31141.description: The Platte River borders Platte County on the south, and the Loup River crosses its lower section toward Columbus. Columbus is the county seat and largest city, anchoring a micropolitan area.

31143.description: The Platte River follows the northwestern edge of Polk County, where rolling hills descend toward the river valley. Osceola is the county seat in this agricultural county.

31145.description: The Republican River crosses Red Willow County’s rolling hills, with McCook as the county seat. The county lies along Nebraska’s southern border with Kansas.

31147.description: Richardson County occupies Nebraska’s southeast tip between the Missouri River, Missouri, and Kansas. Falls City is the county seat, and parts of the Ioway and Sac and Fox reservations lie in the county.

31149.description: The Niobrara River follows Rock County’s northern boundary, across rolling hills dotted with small lakes. Bassett is the county seat and largest city.

31151.description: The Big Blue River flows south through Saline County’s gently rolling, agricultural landscape, with tributaries draining the center and south. Wilber is the county seat.

31153.description: Sarpy County lies between the Missouri and Platte rivers, with rolling hills and small drainages descending toward them. Papillion is the county seat, and Bellevue is the largest city within the Omaha–Council Bluffs metropolitan area.

31155.description: The Platte River borders Saunders County to the north and east, with rolling hills sloping toward its valley. Wahoo is the county seat and largest city in the Omaha–Council Bluffs metropolitan area.

31157.description: The North Platte River crosses Scotts Bluff County, where Gering is the county seat and Scottsbluff the largest city. Agriculture, including sugar beets, corn, and beans, is the county’s economic base.

31159.description: The Big Blue River crosses Seward County’s gently rolling farmland, which includes center-pivot irrigation. Seward is the county seat and largest city within the Lincoln metropolitan area.

31161.description: The Niobrara River crosses Sheridan County’s arid rolling terrain in northern Nebraska, beside South Dakota. Rushville is the county seat, and Gordon is the largest city.

31163.description: The Middle Loup River crosses Sherman County’s rolling hills toward the southeast, with tributary creeks draining its west. Loup City is the county seat.

31165.description: The Niobrara River winds through Sioux County in Nebraska’s northwest corner, between South Dakota and Wyoming. Harrison is the county seat and largest village in the Scottsbluff micropolitan area.

31167.description: The Elkhorn River flows east across Stanton County’s low rolling hills. Stanton is the county seat in the Norfolk micropolitan area.

31169.description: Rolling hills slope east across Thayer County toward the Big Sandy and Rose creeks. Hebron is the county seat on Nebraska’s southern border with Kansas.

31171.description: The Middle Loup and Dismal rivers flow east through Thomas County’s rolling hills. Thedford is the county seat in this Sandhills county.

31173.description: The Omaha and Winnebago reservations together cover all of Thurston County’s land area. Pender is the county seat, and the county borders Iowa across the Missouri River.

31175.description: The North and Middle Loup rivers cross Valley County’s rolling hills, with agriculture concentrated in the flatter river valleys. Ord is the county seat.

31177.description: Washington County lies across the Missouri River from Iowa, with the Elkhorn River along its southwestern boundary. Blair is the county seat and largest city within the Omaha–Council Bluffs metropolitan area.

31179.description: South Logan Creek drains Wayne County’s gently rolling, mostly agricultural land toward the northeast. Wayne is the county seat in northeastern Nebraska.

31181.description: The Republican River crosses Webster County’s low rolling hills in southern Nebraska. Red Cloud is the county seat, and flatter land is used for agriculture, including center-pivot irrigation.

31183.description: Beaver Creek drains Wheeler County’s low rolling hills toward the east. Bartlett is the county seat and largest village in this central Nebraska county.

31185.description: York County’s rolling prairie slopes toward the Platte River to the northwest, and much of the land is agricultural. York is the county seat and largest city.

32001.description: Churchill County’s rugged ridges enclose an intermediate valley, with lakes and ponds across the terrain. Fallon is the county seat in northwestern Nevada.

32003.description: Clark County spans a mountainous basin around Las Vegas and includes Henderson, North Las Vegas, Hoover Dam, and the Colorado River. Las Vegas is the county seat and largest city in Nevada.

32005.description: Carson Valley rises toward the Sierra Nevada in Douglas County, with Minden as county seat. The county forms the Gardnerville Ranchos micropolitan area, included in the Reno–Carson City–Fernley combined area.

32007.description: Elko County is Nevada’s second-largest county by area, with Elko as county seat in the northeast. The county includes 49.8% of the Duck Valley Indian Reservation and sagebrush steppe across much of its landscape.

32009.description: The Silver Peak and Monte Cristo ranges dominate Esmeralda County, which also includes part of Death Valley National Park. Goldfield is the county seat, and the county has no incorporated communities.

32011.description: Diamond Peak rises along Eureka County’s border with White Pine County, while Eureka is the county seat. The county forms part of the Elko micropolitan area.

32013.description: The Santa Rosa Range and Granite Peak rise in eastern Humboldt County, while Winnemucca anchors its transport crossroads. The county is largely rural and is Nevada’s fourth largest by area.

32015.description: Battle Mountain is the county seat of Lander County, where the Toiyabe and Shoshone mountain ranges include its highest and most prominent peaks. The county had 5,734 residents in the 2020 census.

32017.description: Lincoln County includes the highly restricted Groom Lake military installation known as Area 51. Pioche is the county seat in this large, sparsely settled county in southeastern Nevada.

32019.description: Yerington is the county seat of Lyon County, which forms part of the Reno metropolitan area. The county lies in western Nevada near the California border.

32021.description: Mount Grant is the highest point in Mineral County, whose county seat is Hawthorne. The county had 4,554 residents in the 2020 census.

32023.description: Nye County is Nevada’s largest county by area, with Tonopah as county seat and Pahrump as its micropolitan area. It includes the Nevada Test Site and proposed Yucca Mountain repository.

32027.description: The Black Rock Desert, site of the annual Burning Man event, extends into Pershing County. Lovelock is the county seat, and north-south mountain ranges alternate with dry Great Basin valleys.

32029.description: Virginia City is the county seat of Storey County in the Reno-Sparks metropolitan area. Technology, manufacturing, and logistics are key sectors in this small county.

32031.description: Reno is the county seat of Washoe County, which includes the Massacre Rim Wilderness Study Area, an International Dark Sky Sanctuary. Mount Rose is the county’s highest point.

32033.description: White Pine County is a mountain region of eastern Nevada, with Great Basin National Park and numerous federally designated wilderness areas. Ely is the county seat, and the area includes parts of several national forests and state parks.

32510.description: Carson City is Nevada’s capital and an independent city, most of whose residents live in Eagle Valley along the Carson Range. The Carson River crosses the city’s southwestern edge, and the city limits extend into the Sierra Nevada.

33001.description: Belknap County lies in New Hampshire’s Lakes Region, with the southwestern half of Lake Winnipesaukee within its boundaries. Laconia is the county seat, surrounded by other lakes and the Belknap Mountains.

33003.description: Northern Carroll County is mountainous, with several ski areas and part of Crawford Notch. Ossipee is the county seat in eastern New Hampshire.

33005.description: Mount Monadnock, the highest point in Cheshire County, rises in its northwestern corner. Keene is the county seat in southwestern New Hampshire.

33007.description: Coös County occupies New Hampshire’s northern reaches along the Quebec border, with much of the White Mountains and other protected lands within its boundaries. Lancaster is the county seat, and forestry and tourism are major industries.

33009.description: About half of Grafton County lies in White Mountain National Forest, alongside Squam Lake and the Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest. Haverhill is the county seat, and the county also includes Dartmouth College and Plymouth State University.

33011.description: Manchester and Nashua are the two county seats of Hillsborough County and the largest cities in New Hampshire. The county forms the state’s most populous and densely settled area within the Manchester-Nashua metropolitan region.

33013.description: Mount Kearsarge rises along the boundary between Warner and Wilmot in Merrimack County. Concord, the state capital, is the county seat and center of a micropolitan area.

33015.description: Rockingham County occupies New Hampshire’s southeastern corner and contains the state’s entire Atlantic coastline. Brentwood is the county seat, and the county is part of the Boston metropolitan area.

33017.description: The Salmon Falls River separates Strafford County from Maine and joins the Piscataqua River near Dover. Dover is the county seat in southeastern New Hampshire.

33019.description: Newport is the county seat of Sullivan County in western New Hampshire. The county forms part of the Claremont-Lebanon micropolitan area.

34001.description: Atlantic County lies along New Jersey’s Atlantic Coastal Plain, with barrier islands including Absecon Island and Brigantine. Mays Landing is its county seat, and the county is part of the Jersey Shore region.

34003.description: Bergen County occupies New Jersey’s northeastern corner along the Hudson River, across from Manhattan and the Bronx. It is a densely developed part of the New York metropolitan area.

34005.description: Burlington County is New Jersey’s largest by land area, with Mount Holly as county seat. Coastal and alluvial plains cover most of the county, interrupted by a few isolated hills.

34007.description: Camden County is a flat, low-lying coastal and alluvial plain in southern New Jersey, reaching the Delaware River. Camden is the county seat, and Cherry Hill is the county’s largest community.

34009.description: Cape May County occupies the Cape May peninsula between Delaware Bay and the Atlantic, with barrier islands and beaches along its coast. Tourism is its largest industry, and Cape May Court House is the county seat.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Cape May County, New Jersey

34011.description: Cumberland County lies on Delaware Bay in New Jersey’s Southern Shore region. The county seat is Bridgeton.

34013.description: Essex County is a densely settled part of northern New Jersey’s New York metropolitan region. Newark is the county seat and largest city.

34015.description: Gloucester County lies in southern New Jersey near the Delaware River and Philadelphia metropolitan area. Woodbury is its county seat.

34017.description: Hudson County occupies New Jersey’s northeastern corner across the Hudson River from Manhattan. Jersey City is the county seat and largest city in this densely urban county.

34019.description: Hunterdon County lies in the western part of New Jersey, with hilly terrain across much of its area. Flemington is the county seat in the Central Jersey region.

34021.description: Mercer County is mostly flat coastal plain in the southeast, rising toward the Piedmont Plateau and Sourlands in the northwest. Trenton is the county seat and state capital, where the Delaware River borders the county.

34023.description: Middlesex County extends from the Raritan Valley inland to the northern Jersey Shore. New Brunswick is the county seat and home to the state’s flagship academic institution.

34025.description: Monmouth County lies between the Raritan Bay, Atlantic Ocean, and neighboring counties, with about 30% of its area covered by water. It is part of both the Jersey Shore and New York metropolitan regions.

34027.description: Morris County rises from the Passaic River valley in the east toward higher and more rugged terrain in the west. Morristown is the county seat in the New York metropolitan area.

34029.description: Ocean County is New Jersey’s largest county by total area, with an extensive shoreline and beaches along the Jersey Shore. Toms River is the county seat in the southern part of the New York metropolitan area.

34031.description: Passaic County includes low, flat terrain along the Passaic and Pompton rivers, Watchung hills, and rugged highlands in the northwest. Paterson is the county seat within the New York metropolitan area.

34033.description: Salem County lies on the Delaware River, with flat coastal plain drained by the Salem River and other creeks. Salem is the county seat in the Philadelphia metropolitan area.

34035.description: Somerset County ranges from low land along the Raritan River to Mine Mountain, its high point near Bernardsville. Somerville is the county seat in the north-central part of New Jersey.

34037.description: Sussex County is New Jersey’s northernmost county, in the Skylands region and the New York metropolitan area. Newton is its county seat, and the county includes the Highlands and Kittatinny Valley.

34039.description: Union County is mostly flat and low-lying, with the Watchung Mountains rising in its northwest corner. Elizabeth is the county seat and most populous municipality.

34041.description: Warren County’s rolling hills include the Kittatinny Ridge and parts of the New Jersey Highlands. The county borders the Delaware River to the west and is part of the North Jersey region.

35001.description: Bernalillo County stretches from the East Mountain area east of the Sandia Mountains to the Volcano Cliffs on the west mesa. Albuquerque is the county seat and New Mexico’s largest city.

35003.description: Catron County is New Mexico’s largest by area and third-least populous, with Reserve as its county seat. It had 3,579 residents in the 2020 census.

35005.description: Roswell is the county seat of Chaves County, which forms a micropolitan area in southeastern New Mexico. The county is one of the largest in the state by area.

35006.description: Grants is the county seat of Cibola County, a mining area with uranium mines. The county also includes El Malpais National Monument.

35007.description: Colfax County reaches from prairies through piñon forests to alpine meadows in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. Raton is the county seat, and Philmont Scout Ranch and the Whittington Center are located there.

35009.description: Curry County lies on New Mexico’s eastern state line beside Texas and forms the Clovis micropolitan area. Clovis is the county seat.

35011.description: Fort Sumner is the county seat of De Baca County, one of New Mexico’s least populous counties. Its population was 1,698 in the 2020 census.

sources.title: Wikipedia: De Baca County, New Mexico

35013.description: The Mesilla Valley, a Rio Grande floodplain, runs north to south through Doña Ana County, with the Organ Mountains along its eastern edge. Las Cruces is the county seat in the Las Cruces metropolitan area.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Doña Ana County, New Mexico

35015.description: Carlsbad Caverns National Park and the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant are both in Eddy County, north of the Texas line. Carlsbad is the county seat and largest city; the Pecos River leaves New Mexico here.

35017.description: Silver City is the county seat of Grant County in southwest New Mexico, and the county forms its micropolitan area. Grant County had 28,185 residents in the 2020 census.

35019.description: Santa Rosa is the county seat of Guadalupe County, which had 4,452 residents in the 2020 census.

35021.description: Harding County’s high prairie and lower semi-desert rangeland are divided by the Canadian Escarpment, with the Canadian River in a deep canyon along part of the west border. Mosquero is the county seat.

35023.description: Hidalgo County is New Mexico’s southernmost county, with Lordsburg as its county seat and largest city. Its southern Bootheel extends between Mexico to the east and south.

35025.description: Lea County lies in New Mexico’s southeast corner along the Texas border, above part of the Permian Basin. Lovington is the county seat, and Hobbs anchors the micropolitan area.

35027.description: Ruidoso is Lincoln County’s largest community, while Carrizozo is its county seat. The county had 20,269 residents in the 2020 census.

35028.description: Los Alamos County is New Mexico’s smallest county by area and includes the communities of Los Alamos and White Rock. The county’s highest point is near Caballo Mountain along its northern border.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Los Alamos County, New Mexico

35029.description: Luna County’s mostly flat lowlands include grassland and desert scrub, with the Florida, Cooke’s Range, and Tres Hermanas mountains. Deming is the county seat near the Mexican border.

35031.description: Gallup is the county seat and center of McKinley County’s micropolitan area in northwestern New Mexico. The county had 72,902 residents in the 2020 census.

35033.description: Truchas Peak is the highest point in Mora County, where Mora is the county seat. Watrous and Wagon Mound are among the county’s other settlements.

35035.description: Otero County borders Texas to the south and is among New Mexico’s largest counties by area. Alamogordo is the county seat and center of its micropolitan area.

35037.description: Quay County borders Texas to the east, with Tucumcari as its county seat. Agriculture and ranching remain major employers, alongside logistics and services concentrated around Interstate 40.

35039.description: Truchas Peak is the highest point in Rio Arriba County, which borders Colorado to the north. Tierra Amarilla is the county seat within the Española micropolitan area.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Rio Arriba County, New Mexico

35041.description: Portales is the county seat of Roosevelt County, which borders Texas to the east. The county forms a micropolitan area included in the wider Clovis-Portales region.

35043.description: Sandoval County includes the summit of Redondo Peak and a geographically separate exclave between Los Alamos and Santa Fe counties. Bernalillo is the county seat within the Albuquerque metropolitan area.

35045.description: San Juan County includes New Mexico’s portion of the Four Corners and extensive Navajo Nation and Ute Mountain Ute reservation lands. Aztec is the county seat in the state’s northwest corner.

sources.title: Wikipedia: San Juan County, New Mexico

35047.description: San Miguel County stretches from the Great Plains to the Rocky Mountains, with Elk Mountain at its highest point. Las Vegas is the county seat and center of its micropolitan area.

sources.title: Wikipedia: San Miguel County, New Mexico

35049.description: The Rio Grande and its tributaries drain Santa Fe County, where Santa Fe Baldy is the highest point. Santa Fe is the county seat and state capital.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Santa Fe County, New Mexico

35051.description: Truth or Consequences is the county seat of Sierra County in southwestern New Mexico. The county had 11,576 residents in the 2020 census.

35053.description: Socorro County ranges from the Rio Grande to South Baldy in the Magdalena Mountains. Socorro is its county seat, and the county is home to several scientific research institutions.

35055.description: Taos County contains Wheeler Peak, New Mexico’s highest natural point, and 17 of the state’s 25 highest peaks. Taos is the county seat in the northern part of the state.

35057.description: Torrance County’s rolling grasslands rise toward the Manzano Mountains on its western edge. Playas and seasonal lakes center on Laguna del Perro southeast of Estancia, the county seat.

35059.description: Union County is New Mexico’s easternmost county, meeting Colorado to the north and Oklahoma and Texas to the east. Clayton is the county seat.

35061.description: Valencia County lies within the Albuquerque metropolitan area and is among New Mexico’s smallest counties by area. Los Lunas is the county seat.

36001.description: Albany County extends south and west from the Mohawk-Hudson confluence, with the Hudson forming its eastern edge. Albany is the county seat and New York’s capital, in the Capital District.

36003.description: The Genesee River bisects Allegany County on its way north to Lake Ontario, and the county borders Pennsylvania. Belmont is the county seat in southwestern New York.

36005.description: The Bronx is New York City’s northernmost borough and the only county in the city located primarily on the mainland. The Bronx River divides hillier western terrain from flatter areas to the east.

36007.description: The Susquehanna River meets the Chenango River at Binghamton, Broome County’s seat. The county is home to Binghamton University, one of the State University of New York’s university centers.

36009.description: Cattaraugus County includes Allegany State Park, part of the Allegany Reservation, and a reach of the Allegheny River. Little Valley is the county seat in rugged southwestern New York.

36011.description: Cayuga County lies in the Finger Lakes region, with Owasco Lake at its center and Cayuga Lake along part of its western edge. Auburn is the county seat and largest city.

36013.description: Chautauqua Lake lies near the center of Chautauqua County, while Lake Erie forms its northern boundary. Mayville is the county seat and Jamestown the largest city in New York’s westernmost county.

36015.description: Chemung County lies along Pennsylvania in New York’s Southern Tier and Finger Lakes regions. Elmira is the county seat; the county forms the Elmira metropolitan area, part of the wider Elmira–Corning combined area.

36017.description: The Chenango River flows south through Chenango County toward the Susquehanna. Norwich is the county seat in the south-central part of New York.

36019.description: The Saranac and Great Chazy rivers flow east across Clinton County into Lake Champlain, which forms its Vermont boundary. Plattsburgh is the county seat near the Canadian border.

36021.description: The Hudson River forms Columbia County’s western boundary, while the Taconic and Berkshire mountains rise to the east. Hudson is the county seat in the Capital District region.

36023.description: Cortland County lies south of Syracuse and north of Binghamton in Central New York. Cortland is the county seat and center of a micropolitan area.

36025.description: Delaware County contains part of the Catskill Mountains and is separated from Pennsylvania by the Delaware River. Delhi is the county seat in New York’s Southern Tier.

36027.description: Dutchess County lies between the Hudson River and the Connecticut border, with hilly terrain across much of the area. Poughkeepsie is the county seat in the Hudson Valley.

36029.description: Erie County borders Lake Erie in western New York, with Buffalo as its county seat. Its northern half is relatively flat, while the Southtowns to the south include the northwesternmost foothills of the Appalachian Mountains.

36031.description: Essex County lies entirely within Adirondack Park in northeastern New York. Lake Champlain forms its eastern boundary, and Mount Marcy, New York’s highest natural point, is in the town of Keene.

36033.description: Franklin County borders Quebec and Ontario in northeastern New York. Its county seat is Malone, and the Upper, Middle and Lower Saranac lakes are within the county.

36035.description: Fulton County is in the central part of the state, northwest of Albany, lying in the southern Adirondack Mountains. Approximately 58% of the county is within the boundaries of Adirondack Park.

36037.description: Genesee County is east of Buffalo and southwest of Rochester in the western portion of New York State. Genesee County had 58,388 residents at the 2020 census.

36039.description: Greene County is located in southeast central New York State, just west of the Hudson River and south of Albany. The northern and eastern regions are mostly low-lying flatlands.

36041.description: Hamilton County is in the state's north central section, northwest of Albany. It lies entirely within Adirondack Park and consists mostly of publicly owned parkland.

36043.description: Herkimer County is part of New York’s Mohawk Valley region and the Utica–Rome metropolitan area. The county is known for the unusually clear, doubly terminated quartz crystals called Herkimer diamonds.

36045.description: Jefferson County lies on New York’s Canadian border, beside the outlet of Lake Ontario into the Saint Lawrence River. It contains part of the Thousand Islands and part of the Tug Hill Plateau; its county seat is Watertown.

36047.description: Kings County is coterminous with Brooklyn, at the western end of Long Island. It shares a land border with Queens and has water borders along Jamaica Bay, the Atlantic Ocean, Upper New York Bay and the East River.

36049.description: Lewis County is located in northwestern New York State, slightly east of due north from Syracuse. The eastern part of the county is in the Adirondack Park.

36051.description: Livingston County is located in the Finger Lakes region, south of Rochester and east of Buffalo. Letchworth State Park is partly in the western part of the county.

36053.description: Madison County is located in central New York State, just east of Syracuse, north of Binghamton, and slightly north of due west from Albany. Madison County contains the geographic center of the state at Pratts Hollow in the Town of Eaton.

36055.description: Monroe County lies along Lake Ontario’s southern shore in western New York. Rochester is its county seat and largest city, and the county forms part of the Rochester metropolitan area.

36057.description: Montgomery County is located in the central part of the state, west of the city of Schenectady and northwest of Albany. Montgomery County had 49,532 residents at the 2020 census.

36059.description: Nassau County borders the Long Island Sound on the north and the open Atlantic Ocean on the south. The highest point in the county is Harbor Hill on the north shore.

36061.description: New York County is coterminous with Manhattan. The borough consists primarily of Manhattan Island, along with Marble Hill and several smaller islands in the East River and New York Harbor.

36063.description: Niagara County lies just north of Buffalo in western New York, bordering Lake Ontario to the north and the Niagara River and Canada to the west.

36065.description: Oneida County is in the central portion of New York State, east of Syracuse, and west of Albany. Oneida Lake is on the northwestern corner of the county, and the Adirondack Park is on the northeast.

36067.description: Onondaga County lies in central New York, west of Albany and Utica, east of Rochester and northeast of Ithaca.
