36069.description: Ontario County is in western New York State, east of Buffalo, southeast of Rochester, and northwest of Ithaca. The county is within the Finger Lakes Region of the state.

36071.description: Orange County is in southeastern New York State, directly north of the New Jersey-New York border, west of the Hudson River, east of the Delaware River and northwest of New York City. It borders the New York counties of Dutchess, Putnam, Rockland, Sullivan, Ulster, and Westchester, as well as Passaic and Sussex counties in New Jersey and Pike County in Pennsylvania.

36073.description: Orleans County extends north into Lake Ontario to the Canada–United States border. Its underwater area is larger than its land area.

36075.description: Oswego County is in northwestern New York State, just north of Syracuse and northwest of Utica, on the eastern shore of Lake Ontario. The Salmon River Falls, a waterfall, is a popular sightseeing destination in the northeastern portion of the county.

36077.description: Otsego County is in central New York State, to the west of Albany, southeast of Utica, and northeast of Binghamton. The county is part of the Central New York Region and Mohawk Valley Region of New York State.

36079.description: Putnam County is situated in the lower Hudson Valley in the southeastern part of New York, between the Hudson River on its west and the New York-Connecticut border on its east. Putnam is southeast of Newburgh, and it is north of White Plains.

36081.description: Queens County is coterminous with the borough of Queens in New York City. Brooklyn lies to its south and west, and Newtown Creek forms part of the border between the two boroughs.

36083.description: Rensselaer County is located in the far eastern part of New York State. The eastern boundary of the county runs along the New York–Vermont and New York–Massachusetts borders.

36085.description: Richmond County is coterminous with Staten Island, New York City’s southernmost borough. The Arthur Kill and Kill Van Kull separate it from New Jersey, and New York Bay separates it from the rest of New York City.

36087.description: Rockland County lies just north of New Jersey on the west side of the Hudson River. About 30% of the county is devoted to parkland.

36089.description: St. Lawrence County is New York’s northernmost county and its largest by area. Part of the county lies within Adirondack Park, and the Port of Ogdensburg is on the St. Lawrence Seaway.

sources.title: Wikipedia: St. Lawrence County, New York

36091.description: Saratoga County lies north of Albany in eastern New York. The Hudson River forms its eastern border, and the Mohawk River forms its southern border.

36093.description: Schenectady County is located in east central New York State, northwest of Albany, an area usually considered "Upstate". Schenectady County had 158,061 residents at the 2020 census.

36095.description: Schoharie County lies west of Albany, with much of its southern portion in the Catskill Mountains. Schoharie Creek flows north toward the Mohawk River, and agriculture is the county’s primary industry.

36097.description: Schuyler County is in the western part of New York State, west of Ithaca at the southern end of Seneca Lake. The Finger Lakes National Forest is in the north part of the county.

36099.description: Seneca County is in the western part of New York in the Finger Lakes Region, bounded on the east by Cayuga Lake and on the west by Seneca Lake. The Finger Lakes National Forest is in the south part of the county.

36101.description: Steuben County lies in southwestern New York immediately north of Pennsylvania. Its county seat is Bath, and Corning, Inc., a manufacturer of specialty glass and related products, is its largest employer.

36103.description: Suffolk County occupies the central and eastern part of Long Island, in the extreme east of the State of New York. The eastern end of the county splits into two peninsulas, known as the North Fork and the South Fork.

36105.description: Sullivan County is in the southern part of New York State, southeast of Binghamton and southwest of Albany. It is separated from Pennsylvania along its southwest boundary by the Delaware River.

36107.description: Tioga County is in southwest New York State, west of Binghamton and directly north of the border with Pennsylvania. The Susquehanna River flows into Pennsylvania from this county.

36109.description: Tompkins County is in the west central part of New York State, south of Syracuse and northwest of Binghamton. It is usually geographically grouped with the Finger Lakes region, but some locals consider themselves to be part of Central New York or the Southern Tier.

36111.description: Ulster County is in southeastern New York State, south of Albany, immediately west of the Hudson River. Much of it is within the Catskill Mountains and the Shawangunk Ridge.

36113.description: Warren County is situated in the eastern portion of New York State in the Adirondack Mountains. The eastern border is Washington County.

36115.description: Washington County is a long narrow county located in the northeastern section of the State. It is known for its rich valley farm land and is part of the Great Appalachian Valley (also known simply as the 'Great Valley') which is a long narrow valley strip often between tall mountain ranges.

36117.description: Wayne County is in the western part of New York State, east of Rochester and northwest of Syracuse, on the south shore of Lake Ontario. Sodus Bay is located on the north shoreline of the county.

36119.description: Westchester County lies north of New York City, bordered by the Hudson River to the west and Long Island Sound to the east. Its county seat is White Plains, and Yonkers is its most populous municipality.

36121.description: Wyoming County is a largely rural, hilly county east of Buffalo in western New York. Agriculture dominates its economy, including dairy production, while wooded areas support timber and maple syrup production.

36123.description: Yates County is in the western part of New York State, northwest of Ithaca and southeast of Rochester. It is in the Finger Lakes Region.

37001.description: Alamance County lies in North Carolina’s Piedmont, with rolling terrain and the Cane Creek Mountains in its south-central area. Textile manufacturing remains important, and many residents commute to work outside the county.

37003.description: Alexander County is located within the Foothills region of western North Carolina. The county's main geographic feature is the Brushy Mountains, a deeply eroded spur of the Blue Ridge Mountains to the west.

37005.description: Alleghany County is located in northwestern North Carolina. The major rivers of Alleghany County are the New River, and the Little River; the latter flows through the town of Sparta, the county seat.

37007.description: Anson County borders Chesterfield County, South Carolina, and four North Carolina counties. Its county seat is Wadesboro, and its population was 22,055 at the 2020 census.

37009.description: Ashe County is located in extreme northwestern North Carolina. The county is bordered by two states: Virginia on the north; and Tennessee to the west.

37011.description: Avery County is a rural, mountainous county entirely within the Appalachian Mountains of North Carolina. Most of Grandfather Mountain lies within the county, and Newland is the county seat.

37013.description: Beaufort County is split in half by the Pamlico River. Beaufort County had 44,652 residents at the 2020 census.

37015.description: Bertie County is in North Carolina. Bertie County had 17,934 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Windsor.

37017.description: Bladen County is North Carolina’s fourth-largest county by land area, with Elizabethtown as its county seat. Agriculture is its largest employer, and the county is the state’s largest blueberry producer.

37019.description: Brunswick County is North Carolina’s southernmost county, with Bolivia as its county seat. The Brunswick and Cape Fear rivers provide access to the Atlantic Ocean.

37021.description: The French Broad River enters the county at its border with Henderson County to the south and flows north into Madison County. The source of the Swannanoa River, which joins the French Broad River in Asheville, is in northeast Buncombe County near Mount Mitchell, a part of the Black Mountains range.

37023.description: Burke County contains portions of two lakes: Lake James along its western border with McDowell County and Lake Rhodhiss along its northeastern border with Caldwell County. Table Rock, a prominent peak in the county in the east rim of Linville Gorge, part of Pisgah National Forest, has been described as "the most visible symbol in the region".

37025.description: Cabarrus County lies in the gently rolling Carolina Piedmont. Its eastern half includes the westernmost foothills of the Uwharrie Mountains, and Concord is the county seat.

37027.description: Caldwell County is divided into three distinct geographic sections: the Blue Ridge Mountains, which dominate the northern and western parts of the county; the gently rolling Piedmont country in the middle and southern parts of the county; and the Brushy Mountains, an isolated remnant of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The "Brushies", as they are often called, run across much of Caldwell County's eastern section.

37029.description: Camden County is included in the Virginia Beach–Chesapeake combined statistical area. Its population was 10,355 at the 2020 census, and Camden is its county seat.

37031.description: Carteret County is in North Carolina. Carteret County had 67,686 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Beaufort.

37033.description: Caswell County is bordered by Person, Orange, Alamance, and Rockingham counties, and the state of Virginia. The Dan River flows through a part of the county.

37035.description: Catawba County is in North Carolina. Catawba County had 160,610 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Newton, and its largest community is Hickory.

37037.description: Chatham County lies totally within the Piedmont physiographic region. The topography of the county is generally gently rolling with several higher hills rising above the general terrain.

37039.description: Cherokee County is North Carolina’s westernmost county, bordering Tennessee to the west and Georgia to the south. Its county seat is Murphy, and the U.S. Forest Service owned 31% of the county as of 2025.

37041.description: Chowan County is in North Carolina. Chowan County had 13,708 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Edenton.

37043.description: Clay County is bordered to the south by the state of Georgia and the Chattahoochee National Forest. The Nantahala River forms part of its northeastern border.

37045.description: Cleveland County is part of the South Mountains, a sub-range of the Blueridge Mountains that runs through the county's northwest corner. In the south east corner of the county is Crowders & Kings Mountains, part of a small narrow ridge that sits above the very near surrounding area.

37047.description: Columbus County lies in southeastern North Carolina along the South Carolina border. It is the state’s third-largest county by land area, with Whiteville as its county seat.

37049.description: Craven County is bordered by Pitt County and Beaufort County to the north, Pamlico County to the east, Carteret County to the south, Jones County to the west, and Lenoir County to the northwest. Craven County lies within the Neuse River Basin.

37051.description: Cumberland County is in North Carolina. As of the 2020 census, the population was 334,728, making it the fifth-most populous county in North Carolina. Its county seat is Fayetteville.

37053.description: Currituck County includes the northern communities of North Carolina's Outer Banks, separated from mainland Currituck County by the Currituck Sound. Currituck County had 28,100 residents at the 2020 census.

37055.description: Dare County includes the middle part of the Outer Banks and contains Roanoke Island. Dare County had 36,915 residents at the 2020 census.

37057.description: Davidson County is located entirely within the Piedmont region of central North Carolina. The Piedmont consists of gently rolling terrain frequently broken by hills or shallow valleys formed by rivers and streams.

37059.description: Davie County is in North Carolina. Davie County had 42,712 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Mocksville.

37061.description: Duplin County is located in the humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification Cfa) zone, with mostly moderate temperatures year round. Winters are mild across Duplin, with the warmest winter temperatures found in the southeastern areas of the county due to the influence of the nearby Atlantic Ocean.

37063.description: Durham County is in North Carolina. As of the 2020 census, the population was 324,833, making it the sixth-most populous county in North Carolina. Its county seat is the city of Durham, which is the only incorporated municipality predominantly located within the county.

37065.description: Edgecombe County is in North Carolina. Edgecombe County had 48,900 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Tarboro.

37067.description: Forsyth County lies in North Carolina’s northwest Piedmont, with Winston-Salem as its county seat. It is part of the Winston-Salem metropolitan area and the Greensboro–Winston-Salem–High Point combined statistical area.

37069.description: Franklin County is in North Carolina. Franklin County had 68,573 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Louisburg.

37071.description: Gaston County belongs to the southern Piedmont physiographic province. Most of Gaston County is in the drainage basin of the Catawba River, except for small areas along the western edge of the county which are in the basin of the Broad River.

37073.description: Gates County is in North Carolina. As of the 2020 census, the population was 10,478, making it the fifth-least populous county in North Carolina. Its county seat is Gatesville.

37075.description: Graham County has mountainous terrain, and two-thirds of the county lies within Nantahala National Forest. Its county seat is Robbinsville, and its population was 8,030 at the 2020 census.

37077.description: Granville County is in North Carolina. Granville County had 60,992 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Oxford.

37079.description: Greene County is in North Carolina. Greene County had 20,451 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Snow Hill.

37081.description: Guilford County is drained, in part, by the Deep and Haw rivers. As of the 2020 census, the population was 541,299, making it the third-most populous county in North Carolina.

37083.description: Some of Halifax County's natural attractions include Medoc Mountain State Park, Lake Gaston, and Roanoke Rapids Lake. Sylvan Heights Bird Park in Scotland Neck is home to the world's largest collection of waterfowl.

37085.description: Harnett County is in North Carolina. Harnett County had 133,568 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Lillington; its largest community is Anderson Creek.

37087.description: Haywood County is bordered by Madison, Buncombe, Henderson, Transylvania, Jackson, Swain counties in North Carolina, and Cocke and Sevier counties in Tennessee. The Pigeon River originates in Haywood County.

37089.description: Henderson County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of southwestern North Carolina on the South Carolina border. The Eastern Continental Divide passes through it, and Hendersonville is its county seat.

37091.description: Hertford County is in North Carolina. Hertford County had 21,552 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Winton.

37093.description: Hoke County is bordered by Moore, Cumberland, Robeson, Scotland, and Richmond counties. Hoke lies within North Carolina's Sandhills region and Coastal Plain region.

37095.description: The mainland portion of the county also borders the Pamlico Sound, while Ocracoke Island rests on the Atlantic Ocean. Hyde County is characterized by many swamps.

37097.description: Iredell County is located within the Piedmont Region of central North Carolina. The northwestern section of the county contains the Brushy Mountains, a deeply eroded spur of the Blue Ridge Mountains far to the west.

37099.description: Jackson County is in North Carolina. The Tuckasegee River flows through the county. Jackson County had 43,109 residents at the 2020 census.

37101.description: Johnston County is in North Carolina. Johnston County had 215,999 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Smithfield.

37103.description: Jones County is dominated by farmland and swamps. As of the 2020 census, the population was 9,172, making it the fourth-least populous county in North Carolina.

37105.description: Lee County is in North Carolina. Lee County had 63,285 residents at the 2020 census. The county seat is Sanford.

37107.description: Lenoir County is in North Carolina. Lenoir County had 55,122 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Kinston, located on the Neuse River, across which the county has its territory.

37109.description: As of the 2020 census, the population was 86,810, making it the most populous "Lincoln County" in the United States. Its county seat is Lincolnton.

37111.description: McDowell County is in North Carolina. Numerous small creeks and streams flow through the county. The Catawba River originates in and crosses the county and empties into Lake James.

37113.description: Macon County has 46.1% of its land within federally administered Nantahala National Forest. The Nantahala River runs through the county and flows into the Little Tennessee River; Franklin is the county seat.

37115.description: Madison County is located deep in the Appalachian Mountains of western North Carolina, and much of the county's terrain is rugged, heavily forested, and sparsely populated. The county's northern border is with the State of Tennessee.

37117.description: Martin County is in North Carolina. Martin County had 22,031 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Williamston.

37119.description: Mecklenburg County lies in southwestern North Carolina, with Charlotte, the state’s largest municipality, as its county seat. It is the central county of the Charlotte–Concord–Gastonia metropolitan area.

37121.description: Mitchell County is in North Carolina. The northwest sections of county border the state of Tennessee. Sections of both the Blue Ridge Parkway and Appalachian Trail are located in the county.

37123.description: Montgomery County is in North Carolina. Montgomery is bordered by Davidson, Moore, Richmond, Randolph, and Stanly counties. Most of the county lies within the Yadkin-Pee Dee River Basin, with some smaller areas lying within the Cape Fear and Lumber River basins.

37125.description: Moore County lies at the boundary between North Carolina’s Piedmont and Atlantic Coastal Plain, at the northern edge of the Sandhills. Carthage is its county seat, and Pinehurst is its largest community.

37127.description: Nash County lies in northeastern North Carolina, with elevations generally rising from east to west. Its county seat is Nashville, and it is part of the Rocky Mount metropolitan area.

37129.description: New Hanover County is the second-smallest county in North Carolina by land area (ahead of only Chowan County). New Hanover County had 225,702 residents at the 2020 census.

sources.title: Wikipedia: New Hanover County, North Carolina

37131.description: Northampton County is in North Carolina. Northampton County had 17,471 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Jackson.

37133.description: Onslow County is bordered by Jones County, Carteret County, Pender County, and Duplin County. Onslow County had 204,576 residents at the 2020 census.

37135.description: The city of Chapel Hill, is in the southeastern part of Orange County, as is Carrboro. Hillsborough is in the central part of the county and is the county seat.

37137.description: Pamlico County is part of the New Bern micropolitan area in North Carolina. Bayboro is its county seat, and its population was 12,276 at the 2020 census.

37139.description: Pasquotank County is the fifth-smallest county in North Carolina by land area. Almost all of the terrain in Pasquotank County is flatland with a topography near sea level, a characteristic of most of North Carolina's Coastal Plain.

37141.description: Pender County is located in the southeastern portion of the state and shares borders with Bladen, Brunswick, Columbus, Duplin, New Hanover, Onslow, and Sampson Counties. The county's eastern border is the Atlantic Ocean.

37143.description: Perquimans County is in North Carolina. Perquimans County had 13,005 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Hertford.

37145.description: Person County contains parts of three major river basins: the Neuse, the Roanoke and the Tar, providing essential clean drinking water to the south and east of the state. The origin of the Tar River is in southeast Person County.

37147.description: Pitt County is in North Carolina. As of the 2020 census, the population was 170,243, making it the 14th-most populous county in North Carolina. Its county seat is Greenville.

37149.description: Polk County is in North Carolina. Lake Adger is a reservoir formed by the damming of the Green River, which flows from west to east across the county. The northern extent of the river's watershed forms the northern border of the county.

37151.description: Randolph County is bordered by Guilford County, Alamance County, Chatham County, Moore County, Montgomery County, and Davidson County. Randolph County is located in the center of North Carolina, and the city of Asheboro (in the county) is the center point of North Carolina.

37153.description: Richmond County lies on North Carolina’s central southern border, with Rockingham as its county seat. It contains more than half of the Sandhills Game Land, which preserves substantial longleaf pine forest.

37155.description: Robeson County is North Carolina’s largest county by land area and borders South Carolina. Lumberton is its county seat and largest community, and most of the county lies in the Lumber River basin.

37157.description: Rockingham County is bordered by the North Carolina counties of Caswell, Alamance, Guilford, Forsyth, and Stokes, and the Virginia counties of Henry and Pittsylvania. Rockingham County is crossed by four major rivers.

37159.description: Rowan County’s eastern border is formed by the Yadkin River. North of Ellis Crossroads, the South Yadkin River meets the Yadkin.

37161.description: In addition to gold and platinum, minerals like rock crystal, garnet, tourmaline, slate, wolframite, and the rare-earth element samarskite have been mined in Rutherford County. Diamonds have also been found there, including one mined at the JD Twitty Gold Placer Mine in 1845.

37163.description: Sampson County is North Carolina’s second-largest county by land area, with Clinton as its county seat. It lies in the watersheds of the Black and South rivers and Six Run Creek.

37165.description: Scotland County lies in south-central North Carolina along the South Carolina border. Laurinburg is its county seat and largest community, and its population was 34,174 at the 2020 census.

37167.description: Stanly County is in North Carolina. Stanly County had 62,504 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Albemarle.

37169.description: Stokes County lies within the Piedmont region of western North Carolina, and most of the terrain consists of gently rolling countryside. The county is part of Appalachia and the Sauratown Mountains run across the center of the county.

37171.description: The whole county is generally considered part of the Piedmont Triad metropolitan area. Surry County is located in the Yadkin Valley AVA, an American Viticultural Area.

37173.description: Swain County is located in far Western North Carolina in the Great Smoky Mountains. It holds more of the Great Smoky Mountains National Park than any other county in North Carolina or Tennessee.

37175.description: Transylvania County contains the primary headwaters of the French Broad River, locally called North Fork, West Fork, East Fork, and Middle Fork. Since the county's northern and western boundaries follow mountain ridges, all these tributaries originate from sources in the county.

37177.description: Tyrrell County had 3,245 residents at the 2020 census, making it North Carolina’s least populous county. Columbia is its county seat, and the county is designated part of the Inner Banks because of its proximity to the Outer Banks.

37179.description: Union County is in North Carolina. Union County had 238,267 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Monroe.

37181.description: Vance County is in North Carolina. Vance County had 42,578 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Henderson.

37183.description: Wake County is located in the northeast central region of North Carolina, where the North American Piedmont and Atlantic Coastal Plain regions meet. As a result, most of Wake County features gently rolling hills that slope eastward toward the state's flat coastal plain.

37185.description: Warren County is bordered by the North Carolina counties of Franklin, Halifax, Nash, Northampton, and Vance, and the Virginia counties of Brunswick and Mecklenburg. It sits in the northeastern section of the state's Piedmont region and lies within the Roanoke and Tar-Pamlico river basins.

37187.description: Washington County borders the Albemarle Sound. Washington County had 11,003 residents at the 2020 census.

37189.description: Watauga County is extremely mountainous, and all of the county's terrain is located within the Appalachian Mountains range. Isolated by mountainous terrain from the remainder of North Carolina to the east, Watauga County was described in the 19th and early 20th centuries as one of the Lost Provinces of North Carolina.

37191.description: Wayne County's surface is level to gently rolling uplands with broad bottoms along the rivers and some creeks. The largest waterway, the Neuse River, bisects the lower central portion of the county and cuts a deep channel 20 to 40 feet deep as it flows in an eastward direction.

37193.description: Wilkes County is located on the eastern slope of the Blue Ridge Mountains, a part of the Appalachian Mountains chain. The Blue Ridge Mountains run from the southwest to the northeast, and dominate the county's western and northern horizons.

37195.description: Wilson County is in North Carolina. Wilson County had 78,784 residents at the 2020 census. The county seat is Wilson.

37197.description: Yadkin County is bordered by Surry, Forsyth, Davie, Iredell, and Wilkes counties. Yadkin County is located in the Piedmont region of North Carolina and in the northwestern portion of state, close to the Blue Ridge Mountains.

37199.description: Yancey County contains Mount Mitchell, the highest point in the United States east of the Mississippi River. Its Black Mountains include five of the ten highest peaks east of the Mississippi, and Burnsville is the county seat.

38001.description: Adams County borders South Dakota along North Dakota’s southern edge. Its semi-arid terrain consists of low rolling hills that generally slope eastward; Hettinger is the county seat.

38003.description: Barnes County’s central area is crossed by the southward-flowing Sheyenne River. Its rolling hills are carved by drainages and dotted with lakes and ponds, and much of the county is devoted to agriculture. Valley City is the county seat and largest city.

38005.description: Benson County has rolling hills dotted with lakes, ponds and drainages. Devils Lake defines much of its eastern boundary, and the North Fork Sheyenne River crosses its southwestern portion.

38007.description: Billings County has rugged, semi-arid hills in the west and more level ground in the east. The Little Missouri River flows north through its western portion, and the South Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park lies just north of Medora.

38009.description: Bottineau County borders Canada on North Dakota’s northern edge. The Deep River flows through its center, and part of the Turtle Mountain plateau lies in its northeastern corner.

38011.description: Bowman County occupies North Dakota’s southwestern corner, bordering South Dakota and Montana. The Little Missouri River crosses its western portion, while the North Fork of the Grand River feeds Bowman-Haley Lake in the south.

38013.description: Burke County borders Saskatchewan along North Dakota’s northern edge. The Des Lacs and White Earth rivers cross a landscape of semi-arid low hills in the northeast and higher eroded ridges in the southwest.

38015.description: Burleigh County’s lower western boundary follows the Missouri River. Its terrain consists of semi-arid low rolling hills, partly used for agriculture, with south-flowing creeks draining the central area.

38017.description: Cass County borders Minnesota across the northward-flowing Red River. Its low rolling hills are used for agriculture outside developed areas, and the terrain generally slopes north and east.

38019.description: Cavalier County borders Canada at North Dakota’s northern edge. The Pembina River flows through its eastern portion, and rolling hills in the west are dotted with lakes and ponds.

38021.description: Dickey County borders South Dakota, with the James and Maple rivers flowing south-southeast through the county. Its rolling hills are used for agriculture, with lakes and ponds in the western portion.

38023.description: Divide County occupies North Dakota’s northwestern corner, bordering Saskatchewan and Montana. Its semi-arid rolling hills are dotted with lakes and ponds and are partly used for agriculture.

38025.description: Dunn County’s northeastern boundary follows the Missouri River. The Little Missouri crosses the center of the county, and gullies and drainages cut its semi-arid rolling hills toward the river valleys.

38027.description: Eddy County’s upper portion is crossed by the eastward-flowing Sheyenne River. Its semi-arid hills support some agriculture, and New Rockford is the county seat and largest city.

38029.description: Emmons County borders South Dakota to the south and the Missouri River to the west. Low rolling hills cover terrain mostly devoted to agriculture; Linton is the county seat and largest city.

38031.description: Foster County is crossed by the south-southeastward-flowing James River. Its low rolling hills are mostly agricultural, with lakes and ponds in the eastern portion; Carrington is the county seat and largest city.

38033.description: Golden Valley County borders Montana on North Dakota’s western edge. Beaver Creek crosses its northern portion, and the Little Missouri River crosses its southeastern corner.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Golden Valley County, North Dakota

38035.description: Grand Forks County borders Minnesota across the Red River, which flows north along its eastern edge. Its low rolling hills are devoted to agriculture outside urban areas.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Grand Forks County, North Dakota

38037.description: Grant County is crossed by the Heart River in the north, while Cedar Creek follows its southern boundary. Its semi-arid terrain consists of rolling and isolated hills carved by drainages, with some agricultural land.

38039.description: Griggs County’s east-central area is crossed by the southward-flowing Sheyenne River, which enters Lake Ashtabula at the southeastern corner. Cooperstown is the county seat and largest city.

38041.description: Hettinger County is crossed by the east-southeastward-flowing Cannonball River. Its semi-arid rolling hills are mostly agricultural; Mott is the county seat, and New England is its largest city.

38043.description: Kidder County has hills dotted with lakes and ponds, with much of the land used for agriculture. Steele is its county seat and largest city.

38045.description: LaMoure County is crossed by the southeastward-flowing James River. Its rolling hills are mostly agricultural, and LaMoure is both its county seat and largest city.

38047.description: Logan County has rolling hills dotted with lakes and ponds, with much of the land used for agriculture. Napoleon is the county seat and largest city.

38049.description: McHenry County is crossed by a loop of the Souris River, while the Wintering River drains its southern portion. Rolling hills support some agriculture; Towner is the county seat, and Velva is the largest city.

38051.description: McIntosh County borders South Dakota along North Dakota’s southern edge. Its terrain consists of rolling hills dotted with lakes and ponds, and Ashley is the county seat.

38053.description: McKenzie County borders Montana on North Dakota’s western edge. The Missouri River and Lake Sakakawea form its northern and northeastern boundaries, and the Yellowstone River enters its northwestern corner.

38055.description: McLean County’s western boundary follows Lake Sakakawea, while its southwestern boundary follows the Missouri River. Its rolling hills are dotted with lakes and ponds in the east, and much of the county is agricultural.

38057.description: Mercer County’s northern boundary follows Lake Sakakawea, and its eastern boundary follows the Missouri River below the dam. Its rolling hills are largely used for agriculture; Stanton is the county seat.

38059.description: Morton County’s eastern boundary follows the Missouri River, while the Cannonball River marks part of its southern boundary. Gullies and drainages cut its low rolling hills, with agriculture on more level land.

38061.description: Mountrail County’s southwestern boundary follows the Missouri River. The Laurentian Divide crosses its central area, and its largely agricultural rolling hills include ponds and lakes in the northeast.

38063.description: Nelson County has rolling hills dotted with lakes and ponds, with much of its land used for agriculture. Lakota is the county seat and largest city.

38065.description: Oliver County’s northeastern and eastern boundaries follow the Missouri River below Lake Sakakawea. Its rolling hills are mostly agricultural, and Center is its county seat and largest city.

38067.description: Pembina County occupies North Dakota’s northeastern corner, bordering Canada and Minnesota across the Red River. The Pembina and Tongue rivers cross its northern portion, and much of the county is agricultural.

38069.description: Pierce County’s central area is crossed by the eastward-flowing North Fork of the Sheyenne River. Its rolling hills are mostly agricultural, and Rugby is its county seat and largest city.

38071.description: Ramsey County’s southwestern boundary is defined by Devils Lake. Its rolling hills are dotted with lakes and ponds, with much of the county devoted to agriculture; the city of Devils Lake is the county seat.

38073.description: Ransom County is crossed by the meandering Sheyenne River. Its rolling hills include lakes and ponds in the west, with much of the land used for agriculture; Lisbon is the county seat and largest city.

38075.description: Renville County borders Canada on North Dakota’s northern edge. The Souris River flows southeast through its largely agricultural rolling hills, and Mohall is the county seat and largest city.

38077.description: Richland County occupies North Dakota’s southeastern corner, bordering Minnesota across the Red River and South Dakota to the south. The Wild Rice River crosses the county, and the Sheyenne River crosses its northwestern corner.

38079.description: Rolette County borders Canada, with dry rolling hills in the south and greener low hills dotted with lakes and ponds in the north and northwest. Part of the Turtle Mountain plateau lies in its northwest, and Rolla is the county seat.

38081.description: Sargent County lies near North Dakota’s southeastern corner along the South Dakota border. Forman is the county seat, and Gwinner is its largest city.

38083.description: Sheridan County has dry rolling hills dotted with lakes and ponds. Much of its land is used for agriculture, and its terrain slopes north and east.

38085.description: Sioux County borders South Dakota to the south and the Missouri River to the east. Cedar Creek forms its northern boundary, and gullies and drainages cut its low rolling hills.

38087.description: Slope County borders Montana on North Dakota’s western side. The Little Missouri River crosses the county from south to north before turning east and then north into Billings County.

38089.description: Stark County’s central area is crossed by the south branch of the Heart River, which enters Patterson Lake at Dickinson. Its semi-arid rolling hills are mostly used for agriculture.

38091.description: Steele County has rolling hills dotted with lakes and ponds, with land devoted to agriculture. The Sheyenne River flows near and into its western boundary, and the Goose River crosses its northeastern portion.

38093.description: Stutsman County’s east-central area is crossed by the south-southeastward-flowing James River. Its low rolling hills are largely agricultural, with lakes and ponds in the west.

38095.description: Towner County borders Canada along North Dakota’s northern edge. The Laurentian Divide crosses its agricultural rolling hills, which are dotted with lakes and ponds.

38097.description: Traill County borders Minnesota across the Red River. The Goose River flows east across its center to join the Red, and its rolling hills are used for agriculture.

38099.description: Walsh County borders Minnesota across the northward-flowing Red River. The south branch of the Park River flows east across the county to join the Red; Grafton is the county seat and largest city.

38101.description: Ward County’s northeastern area is crossed by the Des Lacs River. Its low rolling hills are largely agricultural, with ponds and lakes in the south and gullies carved by drainages.

38103.description: Wells County is crossed by the east-northeastward-flowing James River. Its rolling hills include lakes and ponds in the southwest; Fessenden is the county seat, and Harvey is its largest city.

38105.description: Williams County borders Montana on North Dakota’s western edge, with the Missouri River along its southern boundary. Williston is its county seat and largest city, and the county has significant exposure to the Bakken formation.

39001.description: Adams County contains Serpent Mound State Memorial in Locust Grove, along with parks and preserves including the Edge of Appalachia Preserve. West Union is its county seat and largest village.

39003.description: Allen County’s county seat and largest city is Lima. Allen County comprises the Lima metropolitan statistical area, and as of the 2020 census, the population was 102,206.

39005.description: Ashland County is in Ohio. Ashland County had 52,447 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Ashland.

39007.description: Ashtabula County is Ohio’s northeasternmost county and its largest by total area. Its county seat is Jefferson, its largest city is Ashtabula, and it is part of the southeastern Lake Erie snowbelt.

39009.description: Athens County is located in the Unglaciated Allegheny Plateau region of Ohio. It features steep, rugged hills, with typical relief of 150 to 400 feet, deeply dissected by stream valleys, many of them remnant from the ancient Teays River drainage system.

39011.description: Auglaize County is Ohio's second-smallest county by area. The county is crossed by the Auglaize River and the Miami and Erie Canal.

39013.description: Belmont County lies along Ohio’s eastern border with West Virginia, across the Ohio River. Captina and McMahon creeks flow east into the Ohio, and the county’s terrain consists of low rolling hills cut by drainages.

39015.description: Brown County lies on the south line of the state of Ohio. Its south border abuts the north border of the state of Kentucky across the Ohio River.

39017.description: The majority of Butler County consists of the river valleys of the Great and Little Miami Rivers. The valley was originally carved by glaciation.

39019.description: Carroll County is in Ohio. Carroll County had 26,721 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Carrollton, while its largest village is Minerva.

39021.description: Champaign County is in Ohio. Champaign County had 38,714 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Urbana.

39023.description: Clark County is in Ohio. Clark County had 136,001 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Springfield.

39025.description: Clermont County had 208,601 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Batavia, and Milford is its largest city.

39027.description: The entire county lies within the Little Miami River watershed, with the exception of extreme eastern areas, which are within the Scioto River watershed. Clinton County lies within the till plains physiographic region, and is somewhat flat or gently rolling.

39029.description: Columbiana County is in Ohio. The Little Beaver Creek watershed is home to Beaver Creek State Forest, Beaver Creek State Park, and Sheepskin Hollow State Nature Preserve. Yellow Creek State Forest is in the southern part of the county.

39031.description: Coshocton County is in Ohio. Coshocton County had 36,612 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Coshocton.

39033.description: Crawford County is drained by the Sandusky and Olentangy Rivers. Crawford County had 42,025 residents at the 2020 census.

39035.description: Cuyahoga County is the second-largest county in Ohio by area. A portion of Cuyahoga Valley National Park is in the county's southeastern section.

39037.description: Darke County is in Ohio. Darke County had 51,881 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Greenville.

39039.description: Defiance County is in Ohio. Defiance County had 38,286 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Defiance.

39041.description: Delaware County has an even terrain and a fertile soil. Delaware County had 214,124 residents at the 2020 census.

39043.description: Erie County is the second-smallest county in Ohio by land area after Lake County. The county is bordered on the north by Lake Erie; the opposite shore is made up of two counties in Ontario, Canada.

39045.description: Fairfield County lies at the edge of Ohio’s Appalachian region. Its once-glaciated northern portion is fairly flat, while foothills begin near Carroll in the south.

39047.description: Fayette County is in Ohio. Fayette County had 28,951 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Washington Court House.

39049.description: Franklin County is located in the Till Plains and the Appalachian Plateau land regions. The county is drained by the Olentangy River and the Scioto River.

39051.description: Fulton County is in Ohio. Fulton County had 42,713 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Wauseon.

39053.description: Gallia County is in Ohio. Gallia County had 29,220 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest village is Gallipolis.

39055.description: Geauga County receives the most precipitation of any county in northern Ohio, with most of the county receiving over 42 inches annually in an average year, and some parts exceeding 44 inches. Geauga County had 95,397 residents at the 2020 census.

39057.description: Greene County is in Ohio. Greene County had 167,966 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Xenia and its largest city is Beavercreek.

39059.description: Guernsey County is in Ohio. Guernsey County had 38,438 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Cambridge.

39061.description: Hamilton County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 830,639, making it the third-most populous county in Ohio. The county seat and most populous city is Cincinnati.

39063.description: Hancock County is in Ohio. Hancock County had 74,920 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Findlay.

39065.description: Hardin County is in Ohio. Hardin County had 30,696 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Kenton.

39067.description: Harrison County had 14,483 residents at the 2020 census, making it Ohio’s fifth-least populous county. Cadiz is its county seat and largest village.

39069.description: Henry County is in Ohio. Henry County had 27,662 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Napoleon.

39071.description: Highland County is in Ohio. Highland County had 43,317 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Hillsboro.

39073.description: Hocking County is in Ohio. Hocking County had 28,050 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Logan.

39075.description: Holmes County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 Census, the population was 44,223. Its county seat is Millersburg.

39077.description: Huron County is in Ohio. Huron County had 58,565 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Norwalk.

39079.description: Jackson County is in Ohio. Jackson County had 32,653 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Jackson.

39081.description: Jefferson County is in Ohio. Jefferson County had 65,249 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Steubenville.

39083.description: Knox County is in Ohio. Approximately 58% of the county is farmland and 28% is forested. Most of the county lies in the Glaciated Allegheny Plateau with rolling hills and valleys.

39085.description: The county’s coast line along Lake Erie spans 31 miles. Additionally, Lake County has an international border with Ontario (across Lake Erie).

39087.description: Lawrence County is the southernmost county in the state of Ohio and part of Appalachian Ohio. Lawrence County had 58,240 residents at the 2020 census.

39089.description: Licking County is the third-largest county in Ohio by land area. At the 2020 census, the population was 178,519.

39091.description: Logan County lies in west-central Ohio, with Bellefontaine as its county seat. Campbell Hill, Ohio’s highest natural point, lies northeast of Bellefontaine.

39093.description: Lorain County lies in northeastern Ohio and is part of the Cleveland metropolitan area. Elyria is its county seat, and Lorain is its largest city.

39095.description: Lucas County is the fourth-smallest county in Ohio by land area. Much of the county lies within what was at the time of its establishment, a vast network of forests, wetlands, and grasslands known as the Great Black Swamp.

39097.description: Madison County is in Ohio. Madison County had 43,824 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is London.

39099.description: Mahoning County is in Ohio. Mahoning County had 228,614 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Youngstown.

39101.description: Marion County is in Ohio. Marion County had 65,359 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Marion.

39103.description: Medina County lies in northeastern Ohio and is part of the Cleveland metropolitan area. Medina is its county seat, and Brunswick is its largest city.

39105.description: Meigs County lies in the Appalachian Plateau physiographic region of the Appalachian Mountains. The landscape ranges from gently rolling to rugged, typical of a dissected plateau.

39107.description: Mercer County has an elevation difference of less than 300 feet across the entire county. Celina is its county seat, and the county forms the Celina micropolitan area.

39109.description: Miami County is in Ohio. Miami County had 108,774 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Troy.

39111.description: Monroe County is bordered by the Ohio River to the east. The terrain is hilly in this area, with waterways cutting through some hills of the Appalachian Plateau, which extends from Lake Erie to the Ohio River, which flows southwest to the south of this county.

39113.description: Montgomery County is in Ohio. At the 2020 census, the population was 537,309, making it the fifth-most populous county in Ohio. The county seat is Dayton.

39115.description: Morgan County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 13,802, making it the third-least populous county in Ohio. Its county seat is McConnelsville.

39117.description: Morrow County is considered to be a part of "Mid Ohio." Morrow County had 34,950 residents at the 2020 census.

39119.description: Muskingum County is the fourth-largest county in Ohio by land area. Muskingum County had 86,410 residents at the 2020 census.

39121.description: Noble County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 14,115, making it the fourth-least populous county in Ohio. Its county seat is Caldwell.

39123.description: Ottawa County is the third-smallest county in Ohio by land area. It borders Ontario across Lake Erie.

39125.description: The land is the most level of any county in the state, and plats look like a checkerboard, with roads every mile. This level terrain resulted in Paulding County being entirely within the Great Black Swamp, unlike any other.

39127.description: Perry County is in Ohio. Perry County had 35,408 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is New Lexington.

39129.description: The Scioto River flows southward through the center of Pickaway County. Big Darby Creek drains the upper western part of the county, discharging into the Scioto at Circleville, and Deer Creek drains the lower western part of the county, flowing southward into Ross County.

39131.description: Pike County is in Ohio. Pike County had 27,088 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Waverly, and the county is named for explorer Zebulon Pike.

39133.description: Portage County lies in northeastern Ohio within the Akron metropolitan area. West Branch State Park surrounds the Michael J. Kirwan Dam and Reservoir in the county’s central area; Ravenna is the county seat.

39135.description: Preble County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 40,999, down 3.0% from the 2010 census population of 42,270. Its county seat is Eaton.

39137.description: Putnam County is in Ohio. The Blanchard River passes through the county. As of the 2020 United States census, the population was 34,451.

39139.description: Richland County is in Ohio. Richland County had 124,936 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Mansfield.

39141.description: Ross County is in Ohio. Paint Creek drains the lower central part of the county, flowing eastward to its terminus with the Scioto at a point southeast of Chillicothe. The county terrain consists of frequent wooded hills, with the intermediate level areas devoted to agriculture.

39143.description: Sandusky County is in Ohio. Sandusky County had 58,896 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat and largest city is Fremont.

39145.description: Many parts of Scioto County are heavily forested, especially in the western half of the county with Shawnee State Park. At the 2020 census, the population was 74,008.

39147.description: Seneca County has nearly level terrain, with almost 80% of its area in agricultural land and about 10% forested. The Sandusky River crosses the county, and Tiffin is its county seat.

39149.description: Shelby County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 United States census, the population was 48,230. Its county seat is Sidney.

39151.description: Stark County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 374,853, making it the eighth-most populous county in Ohio. Its county seat is Canton.

39153.description: Summit County is in Ohio. The largest portion of Cuyahoga Valley National Park is in the northern part of the county. The southern border of the former Connecticut Western Reserve passes through the southern part of the county, leading to jogs in the east and west borders of the county.

39155.description: Trumbull County is approximately a square with sides of 25.24 miles; it is the only square county in Ohio. Trumbull County had 201,977 residents at the 2020 census.

39157.description: Tuscarawas County is in Ohio. Tuscarawas County had 93,263 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is New Philadelphia.

39159.description: Union County is in Ohio. Union County had 62,784 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Marysville.

39161.description: Van Wert County is in Ohio. Van Wert County had 28,931 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Van Wert.

39163.description: Vinton County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 12,800, making it the least populous county of Ohio. Its county seat is McArthur.

39165.description: Warren County lies in southwestern Ohio, with Lebanon as its county seat and Mason as its most populous city. Its population was 242,337 at the 2020 census.

39167.description: Washington County is the fifth-largest county in Ohio by land area. Washington County's southern and eastern boundary is the Ohio River.

39169.description: Wayne County is in Ohio. Wayne County had 116,894 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Wooster.

39171.description: Williams County is in Ohio. As of the 2020 census, the population was 37,102, and was estimated to be 36,549 in 2025. The county seat and the largest city is Bryan.

39173.description: Wood County is in Ohio. Wood County had 132,248 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Bowling Green.

39175.description: Wyandot County is in Ohio. Wyandot County had 21,900 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Upper Sandusky.

40001.description: Adair County is part of the Ozark plateau uplift, the tree-covered foothills of the Boston Mountains. North and central Adair County are drained by the Illinois River and three creeks.

40003.description: Alfalfa County contains Great Salt Plains Lake, Great Salt Plains State Park and Great Salt Plains National Wildlife Refuge, about 12 miles east of Cherokee. Its major waterways are the Salt Fork of the Arkansas River and the Medicine Lodge River.

40005.description: Atoka County is drained by North Boggy, Clear Boggy and Muddy Boggy Creeks, which are tributaries of the Red River, and by McGee Creek, which is a tributary of Muddy Boggy Creek. Atoka Reservoir is in the northern section of the county.

40007.description: Beaver County is the fifth-largest county in Oklahoma by area. Just north of the town of Beaver is the Beaver Dunes Park.

40009.description: Beckham County is drained by the North Fork of the Red River and its tributaries: the Timber, Sweetwater, and Buffalo creeks. The northwestern part of the county is part of the High Plains.

40011.description: Blaine County spans two physiographic areas: the western edge of the Red Bed Plains in the northeast and the Gypsum Hills in the southwest. Watonga is its county seat.

40013.description: Bryan County is in the Coastal Plains physiographic region, and is drained mostly by the Blue River. The Washita River originally drained much of the western part of the county, but now empties into Lake Texoma, which forms much of the southern boundary of the county.

40015.description: Caddo County mostly lies in the Gypsum Hills and the Red Bed plains physiographic areas. The extreme southwestern corner is in the Wichita Mountains.

40017.description: Canadian County lies mostly within the Red Bed Plains, a subregion of the Osage Plains physiographic region. Its northwestern corner is in the Gypsum Hills.

40019.description: Carter County contains parts of several physiographic regions, including the Arbuckle Mountains, the Coastal Plains, the Red Bed plains and the Cross Timbers. The northern part of the county drains to the Washita River, while several creeks drain the southern part directly to the Red River.

40021.description: Cherokee County lies in the foothills of the Ozark Mountains. It includes most of Tenkiller Lake and part of Fort Gibson Lake.

40023.description: Choctaw County is in Oklahoma. The major streams in the county are the Kiamichi River, the Muddy Boggy River and the Clear Boggy River, which all drain into the Red River. Lakes include Hugo Lake, on the Kiamichi River, and Raymond Gary Lake.

40025.description: Cimarron County is Oklahoma’s westernmost county, located in the Panhandle, with Boise City as its county seat. It contains the state’s highest point on Black Mesa; the Cimarron River drains the north and the Beaver River drains the south.

40027.description: Cleveland County is the eighth smallest county in the state. Cleveland County contains the reservoir Lake Thunderbird , constructed between 1962 and 1965.

40029.description: Coal County is the fifth-smallest county in Oklahoma by area. The eastern part of the county lies in the Ouachita Mountains, while the western part has open prairie and lies in the Sandstone Hills physiographic region.

40031.description: Comanche County lies in an area that is typical of the Great Plains with prairie, few trees, and generally flat topography with gently rolling hills. The north region of the county consists of the Wichita Mountains including Mount Scott and Mount Pinchot the area's highest peaks.

40033.description: Cotton County is in Oklahoma. The eastern portion of the county is in the Cross Timbers region. Its creeks and streams drain to the southeast into the Red River, which borders the county on the south.

40035.description: Craig County lies in the Osage Plains, on the western edge of the Ozark Plateau, and drains into several tributaries of the Neosho River. Craig County had 14,107 residents at the 2020 census.

40037.description: Creek County is drained by the Cimarron River, and the Deep Fork and Little Deep Fork of the North Canadian River. Heyburn Lake is contained within the county.

40039.description: Custer County is in Oklahoma. Custer County had 28,513 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Arapaho.

40041.description: Delaware County lies on the western slope of the Ozark Plateau; no oil, gas, or mineral resources of economic consequence are present, but the county has abundant water. Lake Eucha, a man-made reservoir on Spavinaw Creek, completed in 1952, lies primarily within Delaware County.

40043.description: Dewey County is in Oklahoma. Most of the county is in the Gypsum Hills physiographic region, except that the western one-fourth of the county is in the High Plains region. It is drained by the Canadian and North Canadian Rivers.

40045.description: Ellis County is mostly within the Great Plains physiographic region. The major stream is Wolf Creek, a tributary of the North Canadian River.

40047.description: Garfield County is in Oklahoma. Garfield County had 62,846 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Enid.

40049.description: Garvin County lies between the Red Bed plains and the Sandstone Hills physiographic regions. The main waterways are the Washita River, Rush Creek and Wildhorse Creek.

40051.description: Grady County lies in the Red Bed Plains and is mostly covered with rolling prairie. The Canadian River forms the northern boundary and the Washita River runs through the middle.

40053.description: Grant County is in Oklahoma. Most of the county is drained by the Salt Fork of the Arkansas River and its tributaries (Pond, Deer, Osage, and Crooked creeks). The Chikaskia River flows southeast from Kansas into the county's northeastern corner, then crosses east into Kay County.

40055.description: Western Greer County lies in the Gypsum Hills, while the eastern one-third is in the Red Bed Plains physiographic region. The county is drained by the North Fork Red River, Elm Fork Red River, and Salt Fork Red River.

40057.description: Harmon County lies in the Gypsum Hills physiographic region, and is drained by the Red River and its tributaries, the Salt and Elm forks of the Red River and Lebos and Turkey creeks. As of the 2020 Census, the population was 2,488, making it the second-least populous county in Oklahoma, behind only Cimarron County.

40059.description: Harper County is drained by the Cimarron River and the Beaver River. As of the 2020 census, the population was 3,272, making it the third-least populous county in Oklahoma.

40061.description: Haskell County lies in southeastern Oklahoma, with the Sans Bois Mountains in its southern portion. The South Canadian River forms its northern border, and Eufaula Lake and Robert S. Kerr Reservoir account for much of its water area.

40063.description: Hughes County is located in the Sandstone Hills physiographic region. It is drained by the North Canadian River, Canadian River, and Little River.

40065.description: Jackson County is in Oklahoma. Most of the county is within the Red Bed Plains physiographic region. The western part lies in the Gypsum Hills and the northeastern part is in the Wichita Mountains.

40067.description: Jefferson County drains into the Red River via Beaver and Mud creeks. Waurika Lake was created in 1971 by damming Beaver Creek in northwestern Jefferson County.

40069.description: Johnston County is in Oklahoma. The northern part of the county lies in the Arbuckle Mountains, which consist of rock outcroppings and rolling hills. The southern part of the county is part of the Coastal Plains region, and is more suitable for farming.

40071.description: Kay County is in Oklahoma. The lowest point is where the Arkansas River leaves the county. The northern boundary is the border with Kansas and its eastern boundary is with Osage County.

40073.description: Kingfisher County is in Oklahoma. The principal waterway is the Cimarron River, which runs from northwest to east through the county. Kingfisher County had 15,184 residents at the 2020 census.

40075.description: Kiowa County lies in southwestern Oklahoma, with Hobart as its county seat. Its terrain is largely flat, with the Washita Mountains along the southern border and waterways including the Washita River and Elk Creek.

40077.description: Latimer County is in Oklahoma. The Sans Bois Mountains span the northern border of the county, while the Winding Stair Mountains extend into its southern part. The Fourche Maline, Brazil and Sans Bois creeks drain the northern part of the county into the Poteau River, a tributary of the Arkansas River.

40079.description: Le Flore County is in Oklahoma. The Arkansas River forms the northern boundary of the county, while its tributaries, the Poteau and James Fork Rivers drain much of the county into the Arkansas. The Kiamichi, Little and Mountain Fork Rivers drain the rest of the county into the Red River.

40081.description: Lincoln County is drained by the Deep Fork of the Canadian River. The eastern part of the county lies in the Cross Timbers and the Sandstone Hills, while the western part is in the Red Bed Plains.

40083.description: Logan County lies in the Red Bed Plains physiographic area. It is drained by the Cimarron River and the smaller streams Cottonwood Creek and Ephraim Creek.

40085.description: Love County is the fifth-smallest county in Oklahoma by land area. Love County is within the Red River Plains physiographic region, with a rolling to hilly topography.

40087.description: McClain County lies largely in the Red Bed Plains region of the Osage Plains. The western part of the county is hilly and covered with black jack oak trees, while the eastern part is level lowlands.

40089.description: McCurtain County occupies Oklahoma’s southeastern corner and is the state’s third-largest county by total area. It contains the McCurtain County Wilderness Area and Little River National Wildlife Refuge, with Idabel as its county seat.

40091.description: McIntosh County is in Oklahoma. Much of the water surface is attributable to Eufaula Lake, the largest reservoir entirely within the state. Checotah is the nearest city to Lake Eufaula State Park (formerly Fountainhead State Park).

40093.description: Major County lies in northwestern Oklahoma, with Fairview as its county seat. Eagle Chief Creek empties into the Cimarron River near Cleo Springs, and Ringwood is known for watermelon production.

40095.description: Marshall County is in Oklahoma. The Red River drains the county and forms the county's southern boundary. Marshall County had 15,312 residents at the 2020 census.

40097.description: Mayes County is bisected by the Grand River. The eastern half of the county is on the Ozark Plateau, with flat areas divided by deep stream valleys.

40099.description: Murray County’s northern section lies in the Sandstone Hills physiographic region and is suitable for farming, while the southern portion is in the Arbuckle Mountains region, which is dominated by rolling hills and rock outcrops. The Washita River drains the county.

40101.description: Muskogee County has prairie grassland in the west and the Cookson Hills at the Ozark Mountains’ western edge in the east. The Arkansas, Verdigris and Grand rivers converge within the county.

40103.description: Noble County is in Oklahoma. The Arkansas River forms part of the county's northeastern boundary. Two of its tributaries, Red Rock Creek in the north and Black Bear Creek in the south, drain the county watershed before emptying into the Arkansas River.

40105.description: Nowata County is in Oklahoma. The Verdigris River divides the county into eastern and western halves. Creeks in the extreme western part of the county drain into the Caney River.

40107.description: Okfuskee County lies within the Sandstone Hills physiographic region. The northeastern part is drained by the Deep Fork of the Canadian River, while the southern part is drained by the North Canadian River.

40109.description: Oklahoma County is in Oklahoma. As of the 2020 census, the population was 796,292, making it the most populous county in Oklahoma. The county seat is Oklahoma City, the state capital and largest city.

40111.description: Okmulgee County is in Oklahoma. Lake Henryetta, Okmulgee Lake, Nichols Lake, most of Dripping Springs Lake, and the tip of Oklahoma's largest lake, Lake Eufaula, lie within the county. The Deep Fork of the North Canadian River is the principal waterway in the county.

40113.description: Osage County is the largest county in Oklahoma by area. Most of the county is in the Osage Plains, and consists of open prairie.

40115.description: Ottawa County is the fourth-smallest county in Oklahoma by area. The eastern part of the county lies in the Ozark Plains, while the western is in the Neosho Lowlands.

40117.description: Pawnee County is in Oklahoma. The western third of the county is part of the Red Bed plains, while the remainder is in the Sandstone Hills region. The Cimarron and Arkansas Rivers drain the county.

40119.description: Payne County is covered by rolling plains, mostly within the Sandstone Hills physiographic region, but with the western part of the county in the Red Bed plains. The county has two significant reservoirs: Lake McMurtry and Lake Carl Blackwell.

40121.description: Pittsburg County’s topography is generally hilly to mountainous. The Ouachita Mountains extend into the southeastern portion.

40123.description: Pontotoc County is in Oklahoma. The Canadian River forms the northern boundary. Pontotoc County had 38,065 residents at the 2020 census.

40125.description: Pottawatomie County is in Oklahoma. Pottawatomie County had 72,454 residents at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Shawnee.

40127.description: Most of Pushmataha County is mountainous, with the exception of a relatively flat agricultural belt along the county's southern border. The Kiamichi River valley forms a crescent through the county from northeast to southwest.

40129.description: Roger Mills County is in Oklahoma. The Canadian River forms the northern border of the county. The Washita River passes by Cheyenne and Strong City as it crosses the county from west to east.

40131.description: Rogers County is in Oklahoma. The largest body of water is Lake Oologah. The main streams are the Caney River and the Verdigris River.

40133.description: Seminole County is bounded on the north by the North Canadian River and on the south by the Canadian River. Seminole County had 23,556 residents at the 2020 census.

40135.description: Sequoyah County is divided between the Ozark Plateau in the north and the Ouachita Mountains in the south. The Cookson Hills are in the northwest part of the county.

40137.description: Stephens County lies within the Red Bed plains. Although no major river is in the county, some creeks provide drainage.

40139.description: Texas County is the second-largest county in Oklahoma by area. The county lies in the High Plains of the Great Plains physiographic region.

40141.description: Tillman County is located along the Texas border. Tillman County had 6,968 residents at the 2020 census.

40143.description: Tulsa County is in Oklahoma. The Arkansas River drains most of the county. Keystone Lake, formed by a dam on the Arkansas River, lies partially in the county.

40145.description: Wagoner County is part of the Ozark Highlands. The Verdigris River divides the east and west parts of the county.

40147.description: Washington County lies in the Eastern Lowlands physiographic region, and is drained by the Caney River. Lakes and reservoirs include Copan Lake, Silver Lake and Bar-Dew Lake.

40149.description: Washita County lies in the Western Redbeds Plains sub-region of the Osage Plains. The Washita River drains most of the county, except that the southwest corner drains into the North Fork of the Red River.

40151.description: Woods County is located along the Kansas border. Woods County had 8,624 residents at the 2020 census.

40153.description: Woodward County is in Oklahoma. The Cimarron River forms part of the northern boundary and drains the northwestern section of the county. The North Canadian River flows through the county from the northwest to the southeast.

41001.description: The terrain of Baker County is generally rugged, with 30 percent of the county covered with forest. The eastern boundary of the county is described by the northward-flowing Snake River, and the county terrain generally slopes to the Snake River's valley.

41003.description: Benton County’s economic base includes Oregon State University, agriculture, lumber, wood products and printing technology research. Its county seat is Corvallis.

41005.description: Clackamas County has long relied on agriculture, timber, manufacturing and commerce. Mount Hood is a major recreation and tourism attraction, and Oregon City is the county seat.

41007.description: Clatsop County’s highest point is Saddle Mountain in the Northern Oregon Coast Range. Manufacturing, tourism and trade are its principal industries, and Astoria is its county seat.

41009.description: Columbia County’s principal industries include wood products and paper manufacturing, trade, construction and horticulture. Second-growth timber supplies local lumber and paper mills.

41011.description: Coos County’s early settlement was drawn by gold deposits, followed by coal mining between 1890 and 1910. Coquille is its county seat, and the county had 64,929 residents at the 2020 census.

41013.description: Crook County lies in Oregon’s geographic center, with Prineville Reservoir as its largest body of water. Its economy includes forest products, agriculture, livestock raising and recreation services.

41015.description: Curry County contains Cape Blanco, Oregon’s westernmost point. Its forests include black oak, big leaf maple and Douglas fir.

41017.description: The overall defining landscape of Deschutes County is primarily marked with that of lava flows. Most of the lava found in Deschutes County issued forth from Newberry Volcano located just south of Bend.

41019.description: Douglas County extends from the Pacific Ocean to the Cascade Range and contains part of Umpqua National Forest. Almost the entire Umpqua River watershed lies within its boundaries.

41021.description: Gilliam County lies east of the Cascade Range, between the John Day River to the west and Columbia River to the north. Its agricultural economy centers on wheat, barley and beef cattle.

41023.description: Grant County contains most of Malheur National Forest and parts of the Wallowa–Whitman, Umatilla and Ochoco national forests. About 63% of its land area is federally controlled.

41025.description: Harney County is the largest county in Oregon by area and the tenth-largest county in the United States (excluding boroughs and census areas in Alaska). To its southeast is the Alvord Desert—the driest place in Oregon —and the Trout Creek Mountains, which extend south into Nevada.

41027.description: Hood River County spans a transition in the Columbia River Gorge between the Cascade Range’s temperate rain forest and eastern Oregon’s dry desert. Its elevations reach the summit of Mount Hood, Oregon’s highest point.

41029.description: A portion of the Umpqua National Forest is in Jackson County. Located entirely within Jackson County is Bear Creek and its watershed, a tributary of the Rogue River.

41031.description: Jefferson County’s predominant source of income is agriculture, including vegetable, grass and flower seeds, garlic, mint and sugar beets. Madras is its county seat.

41033.description: Josephine County is in Oregon. Josephine County had 88,090 residents at the 2020 census. The county seat is Grants Pass.

41035.description: Klamath County is Oregon’s fourth-largest county by area. Timber and agriculture historically formed its economic base, though these industries now contribute a smaller share of employment and economic activity.

41037.description: Lake County is the third-largest county in Oregon. The area includes alkali lakes, high desert scrub, and forests of Western Juniper, Ponderosa Pine, and Lodgepole Pine in the hills and mountains.

41039.description: Lane County is one of two Oregon counties that extend from the Pacific Ocean to the Cascades (the other is Douglas County.) A portion of the Umpqua National Forest is in Lane County. Portions of the Willamette, McKenzie, and Siuslaw rivers run through the county.

41041.description: Lincoln County’s principal industries include tourism, trade, health services and construction. Newport, its county seat, is also one of Oregon’s two major fishing ports.

41043.description: Linn County’s principal industries include wood products, agriculture, mining and manufacturing. Its economy relies heavily on lumber and wood products, and Albany is its county seat.

41045.description: Malheur County is 94% rangeland, with irrigated farming concentrated in the Western Treasure Valley in its northeastern corner. Vale is the county seat, and Ontario is its largest city.

41047.description: Marion County’s county seat is Salem, Oregon’s capital. Government is its main employer and economic base, alongside agriculture, food processing, lumber, manufacturing and education.

41049.description: Morrow County lies in eastern Oregon, with the Columbia River forming its northern border. Much of it is dry and flat, while the Blue Mountains make the southern portion mountainous.

41051.description: Multnomah County is the smallest county in Oregon by area. It is located along the south side of the Columbia River.

41053.description: About two thirds of Polk County, the western part, is forest, mostly of the coniferous and mixed varieties, bordering on temperate rain forest around Laurel Mountain, the wettest place in Oregon. The eastern half of the county lies in the Willamette Valley.

41055.description: Sherman County lies between the John Day River to the east, Deschutes River to the west and Columbia River to the north. Its mostly flat Columbia Plateau landscape supports an agricultural economy focused on wheat and barley.

41057.description: Tillamook County has a major dairy farming sector, with the Tillamook Cheese Factory as its largest business and private employer. Rogers Peak is its highest point and the highest in the Northern Oregon Coast Range.

41059.description: Umatilla County borders the Columbia River across from Washington. Hermiston is the largest and fastest growing city in Umatilla County, but Pendleton remains the county seat.

41061.description: Union County has 47% of its land owned by the Forest Service. Its natural resource economy includes farming, cattle and sheep ranching, and timber.

41063.description: Wallowa County is Oregon’s northeasternmost county, with agriculture, ranching, lumber and tourism as its principal industries. The Forest Service owns 56% of its land.

41065.description: Wasco County is in Oregon. The northern boundary with Washington is the Columbia River (the state line). Wasco County had 26,670 residents at the 2020 census.

41067.description: Washington County lies west of Portland, with most of its area in the Tualatin Valley. The Portland metropolitan Urban Growth Boundary bisects the county, and agriculture remains a major industry.

41069.description: As of the 2020 census, the population was 1,451, making it Oregon's least populous county. The county seat is Fossil, and Wheeler County is known for having Oregon's largest deposit of fossils.

41071.description: Yamhill County is Oregon’s fifth-smallest county by area. Trask Mountain, in its northwestern corner, is the county’s tallest mountain.

42001.description: The Borough of Gettysburg is located at the center of Adams County. This county seat community is surrounded on three sides by the Gettysburg National Military Park (GNMP).

42003.description: Four major rivers traverse Allegheny County: the Allegheny River and the Monongahela River converge at Downtown Pittsburgh to form the Ohio River. The Youghiogheny River flows into the Monongahela River at McKeesport, to the southeast.

42005.description: Armstrong County is part of Pennsylvania’s Greater Pittsburgh region, with Kittanning as its county seat. Its population was 65,558 at the 2020 census.

42007.description: Beaver County is part of Pennsylvania’s Greater Pittsburgh region. Beaver is its county seat, Aliquippa is its largest city, and its population was 168,215 at the 2020 census.

42009.description: Bedford County’s northwestern boundary lies approximately along the Allegheny Front, which separates the Ridge and Valley province from the Allegheny Plateau. Bedford is its county seat.

42011.description: Berks County is drained mostly by the Schuylkill River. Parts of its northeast drain to the Lehigh River, while other areas drain to the Susquehanna through the Swatara Creek and Conestoga River systems.

42013.description: Blair County comprises the Altoona metropolitan area in southwestern Pennsylvania. Hollidaysburg is its county seat, and Altoona is its largest city.

42015.description: Bradford County lies in northeastern Pennsylvania, with Towanda as its county seat. Its major employers include the natural gas industry, farming, logging and manufacturing businesses.

42017.description: The southern third of the county between Philadelphia and Trenton, New Jersey, often called Lower Bucks, resides in the Atlantic Coastal Plain; it is flat and near sea level, and is the county's most populated and industrialized area.
