Bucks County shares a western border with Montgomery County, and also borders Philadelphia to the southwest, and Northampton and Lehigh Counties to the north.

42019.description: Butler County is part of Pennsylvania’s Pittsburgh region, with Butler as its county seat. It contains Moraine State Park and Lake Arthur.

42021.description: Cambria County comprises the Johnstown metropolitan area in southwestern Pennsylvania. Its county seat is Ebensburg, and its population was 133,472 at the 2020 census.

42023.description: Cameron County had 4,547 residents at the 2020 census, making it Pennsylvania’s least populous county. Emporium is its county seat, and the county is part of the state’s North Central region.

42025.description: Blue Mountain forms the southern boundary of Carbon County. The northeast area of the county is located in the Pocono Mountains and the northwest area includes portions of Broad and Spring mountains.

42027.description: Centre County comprises the State College metropolitan area in central Pennsylvania, with Bellefonte as its county seat. It is Pennsylvania’s fifth-largest county by area.

42029.description: The topography consists of rolling hills and valleys and it is part of the region known as the Piedmont. Watersheds that serve Chester County include the Octoraro, Brandywine, and Chester creeks, and the Schuylkill River.

42031.description: Clarion County lies in northwestern Pennsylvania and is entirely within the Pittsburgh media market. Clarion is its county seat, and its population was 37,241 at the 2020 census.

42033.description: Clearfield County is crossed by the West Branch Susquehanna River, which bisects the county seat of Clearfield. Lumber and coal were its two major industries from the mid-1800s to the early 1900s.

42035.description: Clinton County comprises the Lock Haven micropolitan area, within the Williamsport–Lock Haven combined statistical area. Lock Haven is its county seat, and its population was 37,450 at the 2020 census.

42037.description: The southern tip of Columbia County is part of the Coal Region. The area of the county from the Susquehanna River south to several miles south of Numidia consists mostly of farmland and state game lands.

42039.description: Crawford County comprises the Meadville micropolitan area in northwestern Pennsylvania. Meadville is its county seat, and its population was 83,938 at the 2020 census.

42041.description: Cumberland County’s northern natural boundary follows Blue Mountain, while Yellow Breeches Creek forms part of its southeastern boundary. Carlisle is its county seat, and the county is part of the Harrisburg–Carlisle metropolitan area.

42043.description: Dauphin County’s county seat is Harrisburg, Pennsylvania’s capital. The Susquehanna River forms its western boundary apart from a small peninsula near Duncannon, and the county is part of the Harrisburg–Carlisle metropolitan area.

42045.description: Delaware County borders Philadelphia to the northeast and is Pennsylvania’s third-smallest county by area. The Delaware River forms its southeastern border with New Jersey.

42047.description: Elk County lies in north-central Pennsylvania, with Ridgway as its county seat. Manufacturing was its largest source of employment in the 2021 ACS five-year estimates, followed by education, health care and social services.

42049.description: Erie County’s terrain is generally rolling and well-watered, with a high ridge running roughly parallel to the Lake Erie shore. It is the only Pennsylvania county with a significant amount of land north of the 42nd parallel.

42051.description: Fayette County’s western portion contains rolling foothills and valleys along the Monongahela and Youghiogheny rivers.

42053.description: Forest County had 6,973 residents at the 2020 census, making it Pennsylvania’s third-least populous county. Tionesta is its county seat, and it is part of the state’s North Central region.

42055.description: Franklin County is in the watershed of the Chesapeake Bay and the overwhelming majority of it is drained by the Potomac River, but the Conodoguinet Creek and the Shermans Creek drain northeastern portions into the Susquehanna River. It has a hot-summer humid continental climate (Dfa) and its hardiness zone is 6b.

42057.description: Fulton County is in the watershed of the Chesapeake Bay and, although most of the county is drained by the Potomac River, some northern and northeastern areas are drained by the Juniata River into the Susquehanna River. It has a humid continental climate (Dfa/Dfb) and average monthly temperatures in McConnellsburg range from 29.2 °F in January to 73.0 °F in July.

42059.description: Greene County lies in southwestern Pennsylvania, with Waynesburg as its county seat. Coal and natural gas have a long history in its economy, and the county is part of the Pittsburgh media market.

42061.description: Huntingdon County comprises the Huntingdon micropolitan area in southwestern Pennsylvania. Its county seat is Huntingdon, and its population was 44,092 at the 2020 census.

42063.description: Indiana County is in Pennsylvania. Located in the county is the Buttermilk Falls Natural Area. The county has a humid continental climate (Dfb), except along the Conemaugh, from below Strangford and the Kiskiminetas River, where it is (Dfa).

42065.description: Jefferson County lies in north-central Pennsylvania, with Brookville as its county seat. Its population was 44,492 at the 2020 census.

42067.description: Juniata County is largely agricultural and forested land, with mountains including Tuscarora Mountain and Shade Mountain. The Susquehanna and Juniata rivers are among its major waterways, and Mifflintown is its county seat.

42069.description: Lackawanna County lies in northeastern Pennsylvania, with Scranton as its county seat and most populous city. It had 215,615 residents in 2022 and was the state’s last county to be created.

42071.description: Lancaster County comprises the Lancaster metropolitan area, with Lancaster as its county seat. Its Amish community is a major tourist attraction, and its population was 552,984 at the 2020 census.

42073.description: Lawrence County is in Pennsylvania. Major waterways are the Shenango River, Neshannock Creek and the Mahoning River which form the Beaver River. Also, the Slippery Rock Creek and Connoquenessing Creak empty into the Beaver River.

42075.description: Lebanon County is in Pennsylvania. Most of it is drained by the Swatara Creek into the Susquehanna River while some eastern portions are drained by the Tulpehocken Creek (which originates in the county near Myerstown) eastward into the Schuylkill River. It consists in large part of a valley.

42077.description: Lehigh County’s county seat is Allentown, Pennsylvania’s third-largest city. Together with Northampton County, it forms the Lehigh Valley region of eastern Pennsylvania.

42079.description: Luzerne County had 325,594 residents at the 2020 census, making it northeastern Pennsylvania’s most populous county. Its economy is the largest in northeastern Pennsylvania.

42081.description: Lycoming County is Pennsylvania’s largest county by land area and comprises the Williamsport metropolitan area. Its county seat is Williamsport, and its population was 114,188 at the 2020 census.

42083.description: McKean County is a rural county in north-central Pennsylvania bordering New York. It includes part of Allegheny National Forest, and the Allegheny River crosses much of its eastern portion; Smethport is the county seat.

42085.description: Mercer County lies in northwestern Pennsylvania, with Mercer as its county seat and Hermitage as its largest city. Its population was 110,652 at the 2020 census.

42087.description: Mifflin County terrain is formed by the folded Appalachian Mountain ridges which run from southwest to northeast across the county. The terrain slopes to the northeast, with its highest point (Broad Mtn) East Northeast from the county's Northwest corner, just south of the county's border with Centre County.

42089.description: Monroe County lies in northeastern Pennsylvania, with Stroudsburg as its county seat. It contains Tobyhanna Army Depot, a major U.S. Department of Defense center for repairing and fabricating electronic systems.

42091.description: Montgomery County is part of the Philadelphia metropolitan area, with Norristown as its county seat. Its population was 856,553 at the 2020 census, making it Pennsylvania’s third-most populous county.

42093.description: Montour County is the smallest county by area in Pennsylvania. A total of 45% of Montour County is wooded.

42095.description: Northampton County joins neighboring Lehigh County to form eastern Pennsylvania’s Lehigh Valley. Easton is its county seat, and its population was 312,951 at the 2020 census.

42097.description: Northumberland County lies in central Pennsylvania, with Sunbury as its county seat. Anthracite mining and manufacturing were major employers historically, but mines began closing and factories relocating in the 1950s.

42099.description: Green Park, an unincorporated village located in northeastern Tyrone Township, serves as Perry County's midpoint between the Conococheague Mountain in the west and the Susquehanna River to the east. The county terrain is formed by the folded Appalachian Mountain ridges which run from southwest to northeast across the county.

42101.description: Philadelphia County is the second-smallest county in Pennsylvania by area. Bodies of water include the Delaware River, Schuylkill River, Cobbs Creek, Wissahickon Creek, and Pennypack Creek.

42103.description: The terrain rises rapidly from the river valley in the east to the rolling foothills of the Poconos in the west. Because of its location, Pike County is the only county in Pennsylvania to border New York and New Jersey, both east of the Delaware River.

42105.description: Three major watersheds meet, forming a triple divide, in Potter County: Chesapeake Bay, St. Lawrence River, and Mississippi River.

42107.description: Schuylkill County contains the Schuylkill River’s headwaters in the Appalachian Mountains. The Schuylkill drains most of the county, while some northern and western areas drain to the Susquehanna River.

42109.description: Snyder County is the fifth-smallest county in Pennsylvania by area. Snyder County is in the Ridge and Valley region of the Appalachian Mountains.

42111.description: Somerset County is one of the far southern counties of Pennsylvania, along its straight southern edge. The county borders Garrett and Allegany Counties in Maryland, and the Pennsylvania counties of Fayette, Westmoreland, Cambria, and Bedford.

42113.description: Sullivan County’s elevations range from 2,593 feet at North Mountain in Davidson Township to 779 feet along Loyalsock Creek at the Lycoming County line. Laporte is its county seat.

42115.description: Susquehanna County is very mountainous, with large concentrations of mountains in the east and smaller, more hill-like mountains in the west. The highest mountain in the county is North Knob just west of Union Dale.

42117.description: Tioga is one of Pennsylvania’s largest counties by land area, with Wellsboro as its county seat. Its North Central Pennsylvania setting includes highland country with a cool-summer continental climate.

42119.description: Union County is centered on Lewisburg, its county seat, and includes the Lewisburg micropolitan area. It is among Pennsylvania’s smallest counties by area.

42121.description: Venango County includes the Allegheny River corridor, where French Creek meets the Allegheny at Franklin. Oil City anchors its small metropolitan area in northwestern Pennsylvania.

42123.description: The Allegheny River, Allegheny Reservoir, Kinzua Dam, and Allegheny National Forest are defining features of Warren County. The county seat of Warren anchors a small metropolitan area in north-central Pennsylvania.

42125.description: Washington County sits within the Pittsburgh region, with the city of Washington as its county seat. Southpointe is a major business park, and the county also has an active coal mining presence.

42127.description: Wayne County’s terrain ranges from rugged northern uplands and western hills to a broad middle plain and lower eastern ground near the Delaware River. Honesdale is the county seat, and the county is linked to the New York metropolitan area.

42129.description: Westmoreland County is part of metropolitan Pittsburgh, with Greensburg as its county seat and Hempfield Township its largest community. Coal mining, coke production, and iron, steel, and glassmaking shaped its industrial history.

42131.description: The North Branch Susquehanna River and several large creeks cross Wyoming County, whose terrain includes hills and mountain ridges. Tunkhannock is the county seat, within the Scranton–Wilkes-Barre metropolitan area.

42133.description: York County lies in the Susquehanna Valley, with the river forming its eastern edge and the Mason–Dixon line its southern border. The county seat of York anchors a metropolitan area extending to Hanover.

44001.description: Bristol County is the smallest county in Rhode Island by land area. Water makes up 46% of its total area.

44003.description: Kent County lies in the Providence metropolitan area and includes East Greenwich as its county seat. Water makes up about 10% of its area; Rhode Island counties serve court and administrative boundaries rather than general-purpose local government.

44005.description: Newport County spans Aquidneck, Conanicut, and Prudence islands as well as Rhode Island’s eastern mainland. Water accounts for about two-thirds of its area, and Pocasset Hill in Tiverton is its highest point.

44007.description: Providence County contains Providence, Rhode Island’s capital and largest city, and more than three-fifths of the state’s population in 2020. The Blackstone, Woonasquatucket, Moshassuck, and Pawtuxet river systems shape its urban and suburban landscape.

44009.description: Known locally as South County, Washington County stretches from Rhode Island’s shoreline into gently rolling inland terrain. Water makes up about 41% of its total area.

45001.description: Abbeville County lies in South Carolina’s Upstate, within the Savannah and Saluda river basins. Abbeville is the county seat, and the county is part of the broader Greenville–Spartanburg–Anderson region.

45003.description: Aiken County spans three South Carolina landscapes: mostly Sandhills, with the Piedmont to the north and Coastal Plain to the south. Aiken is both the county seat and largest community, within the Augusta metropolitan area.

45005.description: The Savannah River forms Allendale County’s western boundary with Georgia, and Allendale is its county seat. Cotton, soybeans, melons, and timber are identified as important parts of the local economy.

45007.description: Anderson County borders Georgia in northwestern South Carolina and includes part of Lake Hartwell. Anderson is the county seat in this Greenville–Anderson–Greer metropolitan county.

45009.description: Bamberg County is a small southwestern South Carolina county, with Bamberg as its county seat. Voorhees University, a historically Black institution founded in the late nineteenth century, is located there.

45011.description: Barnwell County lies in South Carolina’s Central Savannah River Area, with the city of Barnwell as its county seat. Its economy includes manufacturing and other employers across a largely inland setting.

45013.description: Beaufort County combines a low-country coastline with the fast-growing communities of Hilton Head Island, Bluffton, and Beaufort. The county is part of the Hilton Head Island–Bluffton–Port Royal metropolitan area, and water covers more than a third of its total area.

45015.description: Berkeley County is part of the Charleston metropolitan area, with Moncks Corner as county seat and Goose Creek as its largest community. It is a large inland-and-coastal county where water accounts for about one-tenth of total area.

45017.description: Calhoun County is one of South Carolina’s smallest counties by area, with St. Matthews as its county seat. Lake Marion is among its notable features, and local industry includes factories such as a sausage-casing plant and a coffee-roasting facility.

45019.description: Charleston County follows South Carolina’s Atlantic coast and is the state’s largest county by total area. Charleston is its county seat, and water covers nearly one-third of the county.

45021.description: Cherokee County is centered on Gaffney in the South Carolina Upstate. Three national heritage sites lie within its boundaries: the Overmountain Victory National Historic Trail, Kings Mountain National Military Park, and Cowpens National Battlefield.

45023.description: Chester County’s economy combines industry, agriculture, and extensive timber production. The county seat is Chester, within the Charlotte metropolitan area.

45025.description: Chesterfield County is centered on Chesterfield, its county seat, and Cheraw, its largest community. It lies in the Pee Dee region along the North Carolina border.

45027.description: Clarendon County sits below the fall line between the Coastal Plain, the Lowcountry, and the Pee Dee. Lake Marion occupies a substantial part of the county’s southern area, and Manning is its county seat.

45029.description: Walterboro is the county seat of Colleton County in South Carolina’s Lowcountry. It is the state’s fifth-largest county by land area and fourth-largest by total area.

45031.description: Darlington County is part of the Florence metropolitan area, with Darlington as county seat and Hartsville its largest community. The county is also home to Darlington Raceway and Coker University.

45033.description: Dillon County is one of South Carolina’s smaller counties by area, with the city of Dillon as its county seat. Major local employers include food retail, health care, and poultry processing.

45035.description: Dorchester County is part of the Charleston metropolitan area and the Lowcountry, with St. George as its county seat. Its largest employers include manufacturers and grocery retailers, as well as the town of Summerville.

45037.description: Edgefield County meets Georgia at the Savannah River, across from Augusta. Edgefield is both its county seat and largest community, and the county belongs to the Augusta metropolitan area.

45039.description: Fairfield County lies in the Columbia metropolitan area, with Winnsboro as its county seat. Sumter National Forest and Lake Wateree State Recreation Area are among its outdoor destinations.

45041.description: Florence County is centered on Florence, its county seat and the core of the county’s metropolitan area. Major employers span energy, higher education, health care, manufacturing, and retail.

45043.description: Georgetown County’s rivers—the Pee Dee, Waccamaw, Black, and Sampit—flow toward Winyah Bay, while the Santee River marks its southern edge. Georgetown is the county seat, and water covers about one-fifth of its area.

45045.description: Greenville County is South Carolina’s most populous county, centered on the city of Greenville. Its northern boundary follows Blue Ridge ridges, reaching the state’s northernmost point.

45047.description: Greenwood County lies in the Savannah and Saluda river basins, with Greenwood as its county seat. Its economy includes manufacturing and research, including Fujifilm’s North American headquarters and the Greenwood Genetic Center.

45049.description: Hampton County is a rural South Carolina county with Hampton as its county seat. Its largest employers include food retail, a regional medical center, and a cookware manufacturer.

45051.description: Horry County reaches from the Atlantic coast across a broad area of rivers, beaches, forests, and swamps. It is South Carolina’s largest county by land area and centers on the Myrtle Beach metropolitan area.

45053.description: Jasper County is the southernmost county in South Carolina, with Ridgeland as county seat and Hardeeville its largest community. It is part of the Hilton Head Island–Bluffton–Port Royal metropolitan area.

45055.description: Kershaw County is organized around Camden, its county seat and largest community. The Wateree River and Lake Wateree are notable features of the county’s landscape.

45057.description: Lancaster County’s western boundary follows the Catawba River and Sugar Creek, while the Lynches River borders it to the east. Lancaster is the county seat and an urban center in the Charlotte region.

45059.description: Laurens County is centered on Laurens, its county seat, in the Greenville–Anderson–Greer metropolitan area.

45061.description: Lee County is among South Carolina’s least populous counties, with Bishopville as its county seat.

45063.description: Lexington County is part of metropolitan Columbia, with Lexington as its largest community and county seat. Lake Murray and the Broad, Saluda, and Congaree rivers are prominent features; the county also hosts Columbia Metropolitan Airport.

45065.description: McCormick County lies in the Savannah River basin and is South Carolina’s smallest county by land area. It is a sparsely populated inland county in the state’s western region.

45067.description: Marion County lies in South Carolina’s coastal plain, with Marion as its county seat.

45069.description: Marlboro County sits along South Carolina’s northern border in the Pee Dee region. The county seat is Bennettsville, and its economy includes manufacturing and agriculture.

45071.description: Newberry County is centered on Newberry, its county seat and micropolitan center, in inland South Carolina.

45073.description: Oconee County is South Carolina’s westernmost county, with Walhalla as county seat and Seneca its largest community. Three large man-made lakes support recreation and hydroelectric power.

45075.description: Orangeburg County is a large inland county in South Carolina’s central region, with Orangeburg as its county seat. It lies in the state’s agricultural Midlands and includes a network of rivers and creeks.

45077.description: Pickens County contains Sassafras Mountain, South Carolina’s highest natural point, and Table Rock State Park. Pickens is its county seat, within the Greenville–Anderson–Greer metropolitan area.

45079.description: Richland County contains Columbia, South Carolina’s capital and its largest city, and forms part of the Columbia metropolitan area. The Congaree River and broad urban and suburban development shape the county.

45081.description: Saluda County lies mostly in the Saluda River basin, with a small western portion in the Savannah River basin. Saluda is the county seat, and the county is part of metropolitan Columbia.

45083.description: Spartanburg County is centered on Spartanburg, its county seat, in the Spartanburg metropolitan area. It is the largest county within that metro area.

45085.description: Sumter is the county seat of Sumter County in South Carolina’s Midlands. Shaw Air Force Base lies within the county, whose western border is formed by the Wateree River.

45087.description: Union County is centered on the city of Union, its county seat, and is part of the Spartanburg metropolitan area.

45089.description: Williamsburg County is centered on Kingstree, its county seat and largest community. It is in South Carolina’s northeastern region.

45091.description: York County is part of the Charlotte metropolitan area, with the city of York as its county seat and Rock Hill as its largest community. Its position along the North Carolina line places it in South Carolina’s fast-growing northern Piedmont.

46003.description: Aurora County is a small South Dakota county of low rolling hills, small lakes, and ponds. Its terrain slopes east-northeastward.

46005.description: Beadle County centers on Huron, its county seat and largest city. The James River crosses this east-central South Dakota county, whose surrounding terrain is rolling and largely agricultural.

46007.description: Bennett County lies in southwestern South Dakota, where the White River crosses a landscape of rolling, semi-arid uplands. Martin is the county seat, and the county includes tribal trust lands.

46009.description: Bon Homme County borders Nebraska across the Missouri River, which marks its southern edge. Tyndall is the county seat in this southeastern South Dakota county.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Bon Homme County, South Dakota

46011.description: Brookings County lies along South Dakota’s eastern border with Minnesota, and the Big Sioux River crosses its eastern side. Brookings is its county seat and a regional center for the state’s east-central prairie.

46013.description: Brown County sits along South Dakota’s northern border, with Aberdeen as its county seat and largest city. The James River runs south through the county’s open prairie landscape.

46015.description: The Missouri River forms the western boundary of Brule County, with Chamberlain as its county seat. Rolling hills rise inland from the river corridor in this central South Dakota county.

46017.description: Buffalo County is one of South Dakota’s least populous counties, and its county seat, Gann Valley, is one of the country’s smallest county seats. The Missouri River runs along its western edge through semi-arid rolling hills.

46019.description: Butte County lies on South Dakota’s western edge, bordering Montana and Wyoming. Its semi-arid rolling hills are cut by northwest–southeast drainages.

46021.description: Campbell County meets North Dakota to the north and the Missouri River along its western edge. Mound City is its county seat, in a semi-arid, rolling landscape.

46023.description: Charles Mix County borders Nebraska across the Missouri River, which follows its southern edge. Lake Andes is the county seat in this south-central county.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Charles Mix County, South Dakota

46025.description: Clark County’s rolling hills are dotted with lakes and ponds, especially in its east-central area. The county seat is Clark, in eastern South Dakota.

46027.description: Clay County borders Nebraska across the Missouri River, which traces its southern edge. Vermillion, home to the University of South Dakota, is its county seat and largest community.

46029.description: Codington County is a lake-dotted, rolling county in northeastern South Dakota. Watertown, its county seat and largest city, is a regional center surrounded by agricultural land.

46031.description: Corson County meets North Dakota to the north, with the Missouri River running along its eastern boundary. McIntosh is its county seat in a semi-arid landscape of rolling hills.

46033.description: Custer County borders Wyoming and contains Jewel Cave National Monument and Wind Cave National Park, two of the longest caves in the United States. Custer is its county seat.

46035.description: Davison County is centered on Mitchell, its county seat and largest city, in east-central South Dakota. The James River passes through the county’s northeastern area amid rolling agricultural land.

46037.description: Day County’s rolling hills are dotted with many lakes and ponds, especially in the east. Webster is the county seat in this northeastern South Dakota county.

46039.description: Deuel County borders Minnesota on South Dakota’s eastern edge, with Clear Lake as its county seat. Its rolling terrain slopes toward the northeast across a largely agricultural landscape.

46041.description: The Moreau River crosses Dewey County before joining the Missouri near its northeast corner. Timber Lake is the county seat; almost all the county lies within the Cheyenne River Indian Reservation, with the remainder in Standing Rock.

46043.description: Douglas County is a small southeastern South Dakota county of rolling agricultural hills. Armour is its county seat.

46045.description: Edmunds County is a rolling prairie county in north-central South Dakota, with Ipswich as its county seat. Its land is largely used for agriculture.

46047.description: Hot Springs is the county seat of Fall River County in southwestern South Dakota. The county borders Wyoming to the west and Nebraska to the south.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Fall River County, South Dakota

46049.description: Faulk County is a low, rolling prairie county in central South Dakota, with Faulkton as its county seat. Its terrain slopes gradually eastward across agricultural land.

46051.description: Grant County borders Minnesota in eastern South Dakota, with Milbank as its county seat and largest community. Rolling agricultural land slopes toward the northeast.

46053.description: Gregory County meets Nebraska to the south and follows the Missouri River along its eastern boundary. Burke is the county seat, and farming and ranching are key parts of the local economy.

46055.description: Haakon County is a semi-arid county of rolling hills, cut by gullies and drainages. The Cheyenne River marks its northern edge, and Philip is the county seat.

46057.description: Hamlin County’s low rolling hills contain many small lakes and ponds. Hayti is the county seat in this agricultural county of eastern South Dakota.

46059.description: Hand County’s gently rolling terrain includes scattered ponds and small lakes. Miller, the county seat, sits amid the county’s broad agricultural landscape.

46061.description: Hanson County is a low, rolling county in southeastern South Dakota, with Alexandria as its county seat. The James River crosses its southwest area and shapes the local drainage.

46063.description: Harding County occupies South Dakota’s northwestern corner, meeting both Montana and North Dakota. Buffalo is its county seat in a high, rolling landscape of semi-arid plains.

46065.description: Hughes County contains Pierre, the state capital, and its county seat. The Missouri River forms its southwestern boundary, alongside rolling hills cut by gullies and drainages.

46067.description: The James River runs south through Hutchinson County, with the surrounding rolling land sloping toward its valley. Olivet is the county seat in this southeastern South Dakota county.

46069.description: Hyde County is a sparsely populated, semi-arid county of rolling hills in central South Dakota. The Missouri River reaches its southwestern corner, and Highmore is the county seat.

46071.description: Jackson County’s arid, rolling hills rise to rugged uplands, while the White River meanders east through the county. Kadoka is the county seat in this south-central landscape.

46073.description: Jerauld County is a low, rolling prairie county in central South Dakota, with Wessington Springs as its county seat. Its terrain slopes toward the south and east.

46075.description: Jones County is South Dakota’s least populous county, with Murdo as its county seat. The Bad River crosses the northwest, while the White River traces its southern boundary through gullied, semi-arid terrain.

46077.description: Kingsbury County has low rolling hills and many lakes and ponds in its central and eastern areas. De Smet is the county seat in this east-central agricultural county.

46079.description: Lake County has rolling agricultural hills, with Buffalo Creek and a tributary of the Vermillion River draining its landscape. Madison is the county seat.

46081.description: Lawrence County contains the Black Hills in western South Dakota, with mountains in the south and west giving way to hills in the northeast. Deadwood is the county seat, within the Rapid City region.

46083.description: Lincoln County borders Iowa across the Big Sioux River and is part of metropolitan Sioux Falls. Its rolling terrain slopes toward the river valley along the eastern edge.

46085.description: Lyman County follows the Missouri River along its northern and eastern edges, while the White River crosses its southern area. Kennebec is the county seat in this river-cut central county.

46087.description: McCook County lies within the Sioux Falls metropolitan area, with Salem as its county seat. Its rolling agricultural landscape slopes south and southwest.

46089.description: McPherson County borders North Dakota along South Dakota’s northern edge. Leola is the county seat in a rolling agricultural landscape dotted with small lakes and ponds.

46091.description: Marshall County borders North Dakota and is dotted with lakes and ponds, particularly in the southeast. Britton is the county seat in a landscape of rolling hills.

46093.description: Meade County is part of metropolitan Rapid City and includes the Black Hills’ mountain ridges in its west and southwest. Sturgis is its county seat; the remainder transitions to rolling, semi-arid prairie drained by the Cheyenne River.

46095.description: Mellette County is historically Lakota territory, and 33.35% of its land is trust land associated with the Rosebud Sioux Tribe. White River is the county seat, and the White and Little White rivers cross the county.

46097.description: Miner County is a small east-central South Dakota county of rolling hills, dotted with lakes and ponds. Howard is its county seat.

46099.description: Minnehaha County contains Sioux Falls, South Dakota’s largest city, and is the state’s most populous county. The Big Sioux River crosses its rolling landscape and frames its eastern border.

46101.description: Moody County lies on South Dakota’s eastern edge and borders Minnesota. The Big Sioux River flows south through its rolling agricultural landscape, with Flandreau as the county seat.

46102.description: Oglala Lakota County is an unorganized county whose largest community is Pine Ridge; Hot Springs in neighboring Fall River County serves as its administrative center. The White River crosses its semi-arid, rolling landscape, which also includes tribal trust lands.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Oglala Lakota County, South Dakota

46103.description: Pennington County stretches from forested, gullied western terrain around Black Elk Peak to rolling hill country in the east. Rapid City is its county seat.

46105.description: Perkins County’s semi-arid hills are cut by drainages and crossed by the Grand and Moreau rivers. Shadehill Reservoir sits on the Grand River, and Bison is the county seat.

46107.description: The Missouri River forms Potter County’s western boundary, with Gettysburg as its county seat. Rolling agricultural hills slope toward the river valley.

46109.description: Roberts County sits at South Dakota’s northeast corner, bordering both Minnesota and North Dakota. Sisseton is its county seat amid rolling agricultural land.

46111.description: The James River runs through the eastern part of Sanborn County, whose rolling hills are largely agricultural. Woonsocket is both the county seat and largest city.

46115.description: Spink County is a rolling agricultural county in eastern South Dakota, with Redfield as its county seat. The James River flows south through its center.

46117.description: Stanley County follows the Cheyenne and Missouri rivers around Fort Pierre, its county seat. The interior is semi-arid rolling country cut by drainages.

46119.description: Sully County borders the Missouri River, which marks its western side. Onida is the county seat in a semi-arid landscape of rolling hills.

46121.description: Todd County is unorganized, with Winner in neighboring Tripp County serving as its administrative center and Mission as its largest city. The semi-arid landscape of rolling hills is cut by gullies and includes irrigated agricultural land.

46123.description: Tripp County meets Nebraska to the south and is bordered by the White River to the north. Winner is the county seat in a rolling landscape cut by gullies and drainages.

46125.description: Turner County is part of metropolitan Sioux Falls, with Parker as its county seat. Its rolling hills are cut by gullies and drainages across a predominantly agricultural landscape.

46127.description: Union County sits at South Dakota’s southeast corner, across the Big Sioux River from Iowa and the Missouri River from Nebraska. Elk Point is its county seat.

46129.description: The Missouri River follows Walworth County’s western boundary, with Selby as its county seat. The county sits in north-central South Dakota.

46135.description: Yankton County is organized around the city of Yankton, its county seat and micropolitan center. Gavins Point Dam impounds Lewis and Clark Lake along the Missouri River in the county’s southwest.

46137.description: Ziebach County consists entirely of Indian reservations, including much of the Cheyenne River Indian Reservation. The Cheyenne and Moreau rivers and Cherry Creek cross its semi-arid rolling hills; Dupree is the county seat.

47001.description: Anderson County sits in East Tennessee north of Knoxville, with Clinton as its county seat. Norris Lake and several museums are among its major attractions.

47003.description: Bedford County lies in south-central Tennessee, with Shelbyville as its county seat. It forms the Shelbyville micropolitan area, within the larger Nashville region.

47005.description: Benton County lies in northwest Tennessee along the western branch of the Tennessee River. Camden is the county seat, about 30 miles south of the Kentucky border.

47007.description: Bledsoe County sits on the Cumberland Plateau in eastern Tennessee, with Pikeville as its county seat. The plateau’s northern escarpment is a prominent feature of its landscape.

47009.description: Blount County is part of metropolitan Knoxville, with Maryville as both county seat and largest city. Its southern portion reaches the Great Smoky Mountains, while the Tennessee River borders the north.

47011.description: Bradley County is centered on Cleveland, its county seat and a major manufacturing hub. The city lies amid parallel ridges of the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians.

47013.description: Campbell County lies on Tennessee’s northern border between the Cumberland Mountains and the Appalachian Ridge-and-Valley region. Jacksboro is its county seat, and the county is part of metropolitan Knoxville.

47015.description: Cannon County is part of the Nashville metropolitan area, with Woodbury as its county seat. It lies in the central part of Middle Tennessee.

47017.description: Carroll County lies in western Tennessee, with Huntingdon as its county seat. It is part of the western division of the state.

47019.description: Carter County lies entirely within the Blue Ridge Mountains, including the Unaka and Iron Mountain ranges. Elizabethton is the county seat in the Johnson City metropolitan area.

47021.description: Cheatham County is part of metropolitan Nashville, with Ashland City as its county seat. The Cumberland River cuts northwest to southeast through the county, and the Harpeth River crosses its southern part.

47023.description: Chester County is part of the Jackson metropolitan area, with Henderson as its county seat. It lies in western Tennessee.

47025.description: Claiborne County is centered on Tazewell, its county seat, and Harrogate, its largest city. The Powell and Clinch rivers are among its major waterways, with the Clinch forming part of Norris Lake.

47027.description: The Cumberland River flows north to south through Clay County, joined by the Obey River at Celina. Dale Hollow Lake impounds the Obey and extends across much of the county’s eastern area.

47029.description: Cocke County borders North Carolina on Tennessee’s eastern edge, with Newport as its county seat. Its southern part lies within Great Smoky Mountains National Park, while the northern part includes the French Broad River valley.

47031.description: Coffee County lies in central Tennessee and is centered on Manchester, its county seat. Short Springs State Natural Area and Machine Falls are among the county’s outdoor features.

47033.description: Crockett County lies in western Tennessee within the Jackson metropolitan area. Alamo is its county seat.

47035.description: Cumberland County sits atop the Cumberland Plateau, with Crossville as its county seat and micropolitan center. The Crab Orchard Mountains rise in its northeastern part.

47037.description: Davidson County contains Nashville, Tennessee’s capital and largest city, and shares a consolidated government with it. The Cumberland River crosses the county, where Old Hickory and J. Percy Priest dams form major reservoirs.

47039.description: Decatur County lies in western Tennessee, with Decaturville as its county seat. It is a small county along the Tennessee River region.

47041.description: DeKalb County’s Austin Bottom is a peninsula on Center Hill Lake and is accessible by road only through neighboring Putnam County. Smithville is the county seat.

47043.description: Dickson County is part of metropolitan Nashville, with Charlotte as its county seat. The Cumberland and Harpeth rivers mark its northeastern and eastern edges.

47045.description: Dyer County lies in Tennessee’s far west, with Dyersburg as its county seat and micropolitan center. The Mississippi River forms its western boundary, and the Forked Deer and Obion rivers meet nearby.

47047.description: Fayette County is one of Tennessee’s largest counties by area and lies within the Memphis metropolitan region. Somerville is its county seat.

47049.description: Fentress County includes part of Dale Hollow Reservoir and is drained by the Obey and Cumberland rivers. Jamestown is the county seat.

47051.description: Franklin County lies on the southern edge of Middle Tennessee, bordering Alabama. Winchester is its county seat, and Tims Ford Lake is a notable feature.

47053.description: Gibson County is part of the Jackson metropolitan area in western Tennessee. Trenton is its county seat.

47055.description: Giles County lies in southern Middle Tennessee, with Pulaski as its county seat. It borders Alabama.

47057.description: Grainger County is part of metropolitan Knoxville, with Rutledge as its county seat. The Clinch River marks its northwest boundary, beneath the Clinch Mountain range.

47059.description: Greene County lies along Tennessee’s eastern border, with Greeneville as its county seat and micropolitan center. Most of the county is in the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians, with long ridges alternating with valleys.

47061.description: Altamont is the county seat of Grundy County, Tennessee. The county had 13,529 residents in 2020.

47063.description: Hamblen County is centered on Morristown, its county seat and only incorporated city. It is the core of the Morristown metropolitan area, with several large industrial parks.

47065.description: Chattanooga is the county seat and largest city of Hamilton County on Tennessee’s border with Georgia. The Tennessee River flows through the county.

47067.description: Hancock County lies in northeastern Tennessee, with Sneedville as its county seat. Elrod Falls is one of its notable natural features.

47069.description: Hardeman County is one of Tennessee’s largest counties by area, with Bolivar as its county seat. It lies in the western part of the state.

47071.description: Hardin County borders Mississippi and Alabama in southern Tennessee, with Savannah as its county seat. The Tennessee River divides the county’s landscape.

47073.description: Hawkins County is centered on Rogersville, its county seat, in the Tri-Cities region. The county’s terrain includes Big Creek Valley and Carter Valley.

47075.description: Haywood County is centered on Brownsville, its county seat and largest city, in West Tennessee. Agriculture is its largest industry, with cotton especially prominent.

47077.description: Henderson County straddles the Tennessee Valley Divide: waters flow east toward the Tennessee River and west toward the Mississippi River. Lexington is the county seat; local streams include the Beech and Forked Deer rivers.

47079.description: Henry County lies along Tennessee’s northwestern border, with Paris as its county seat. Water accounts for more than five percent of its total area.

47081.description: Hickman County is part of the Nashville metropolitan area, with Centerville as its county seat. The Duck and Piney rivers and many creeks cross the county.

47083.description: Erin is the county seat of Houston County, Tennessee. The county had 8,283 residents in the 2020 census.

47085.description: Humphreys County lies in western Middle Tennessee, with Waverly as its county seat. Water accounts for a modest share of its total area.

47087.description: Gainesboro is the county seat of Jackson County, part of the Cookeville micropolitan area. Small portions of the far north drain into Jennings Creek.

47089.description: Jefferson County is part of the Morristown metropolitan area, with Dandridge as its county seat. Douglas Lake and Cherokee Lake occupy substantial parts of the county along the French Broad and Holston rivers.

47091.description: Johnson County is Tennessee’s easternmost county, lying entirely within the Blue Ridge Mountains. Mountain City is its county seat.

47093.description: Knox County contains Knoxville, its county seat and the region’s largest city. It lies among the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians, with ridges and valleys extending across the county.

47095.description: Lake County sits in Tennessee’s northwest corner, bordered by Kentucky and separated from Missouri by the Mississippi River. Tiptonville is its county seat, near Reelfoot Lake.

47097.description: Lauderdale County borders the Mississippi River on Tennessee’s western edge, with Ripley as its county seat. The Forked Deer and Hatchie rivers form parts of its northern and southern boundaries.

47099.description: Lawrence County lies in southwestern Middle Tennessee, with Lawrenceburg as both county seat and largest city. David Crockett State Park and Crockett Falls are local landmarks.

47101.description: Lewis County is a small county in southern Middle Tennessee, with Hohenwald as its county seat. Meriwether Lewis is buried near the town.

47103.description: Lincoln County lies in south-central Tennessee, with Fayetteville as both county seat and largest city. The county borders Alabama.

47105.description: Loudon County is part of metropolitan Knoxville, with Loudon as its county seat. The Little Tennessee River joins the Tennessee River near Lenoir City, and its lower reaches form Tellico Lake.

47107.description: McMinn County lies mostly in the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians, where parallel ridges alternate with valleys. Athens is the county seat in East Tennessee.

47109.description: McNairy County is centered on Selmer, its county seat and largest city, along Tennessee’s border with Mississippi. U.S. Routes 64 and 45 cross and meet in Selmer.

47111.description: Macon County lies in the northeastern Highland Rim, where its landscape is rugged and hilly. Lafayette is its county seat, and the county is part of metropolitan Nashville.

47113.description: Madison County is centered on Jackson, its county seat and a regional center in western Tennessee. It is part of the Jackson metropolitan area.

47115.description: Marion County is part of metropolitan Chattanooga and sits in the Sequatchie Valley. Jasper is its county seat; the county also includes Nickajack Lake and Foster Falls.

47117.description: The Duck River drains much of Marshall County in Middle Tennessee. Lewisburg is its county seat, within the Nashville metropolitan area.

47119.description: Maury County lies in Middle Tennessee within the Nashville metropolitan area. Columbia is its county seat.

47121.description: The Tennessee River forms Meigs County’s western boundary, with Watts Bar Dam and Watts Bar Lake along the river. Decatur is the county seat.

47123.description: The Unicoi Mountains dominate Monroe County’s southeastern part along the North Carolina border. Madisonville is the county seat, and Sweetwater its largest city.

47125.description: Montgomery County borders Kentucky, with Clarksville as its county seat and only incorporated municipality. The Cumberland River crosses its hilly, tree-covered landscape.

47127.description: Moore County is among Tennessee’s smallest counties and has a consolidated city-county government centered on Lynchburg. Its terrain spans the rugged Highland Rim and flatter Nashville Basin; the Jack Daniel Distillery is located there.

47129.description: Morgan County lies along the eastern edge of the Cumberland Plateau, with rugged mountain terrain and cold streams and rivers. Wartburg is the county seat.

47131.description: Obion County lies in Tennessee’s northwest corner, with Union City as its county seat. Its landscape consists of rolling hills.

47133.description: Overton County straddles the Eastern Highland Rim, where low rolling hills are divided by narrow creek valleys. Livingston is the county seat in the Cookeville micropolitan area.

47135.description: Perry County lies on Middle Tennessee’s western edge, where high ridges separate creeks flowing toward two rivers. Linden is its county seat and largest town.

47137.description: Pickett County lies between Dale Hollow Lake and the Kentucky border, with Byrdstown as its county seat. Its eastern portion includes the Cumberland Plateau and Pickett State Forest.

47139.description: Polk County occupies Tennessee’s southeastern corner between Georgia and North Carolina, with Benton as its county seat. Much of its terrain is mountainous and part of the southern Blue Ridge; tourism has grown as copper mining declined.

47141.description: Putnam County is centered on Cookeville, its county seat and micropolitan center. It lies within the Cumberland River watershed and includes Burgess Falls near its southern border.

47143.description: Rhea County follows the Tennessee River and includes Watts Bar Nuclear Generating Station. Dayton is its county seat, with Walden Ridge marking the edge of the Cumberland Plateau.

47145.description: The Tennessee, Clinch, and Emory rivers pass through Roane County and meet near Kingston. Kingston is the county seat in the Knoxville metropolitan area.

47147.description: Robertson County sits along Tennessee’s central northern border, with Springfield as its county seat. It is in Middle Tennessee.

47149.description: Rutherford County lies in Middle Tennessee and is part of the Nashville metropolitan area. Murfreesboro is its county seat and largest city.

47151.description: Scott County borders Kentucky and is part of the Big South Fork of the Cumberland River region. Huntsville is its county seat, and Oneida its largest town.

47153.description: Sequatchie County lies within the Sequatchie Valley and is part of metropolitan Chattanooga. Dunlap is its county seat.

47155.description: Sevier County includes part of the Great Smoky Mountains and is centered on Sevierville, its county seat and largest city. Tourism in the Smokies is a major feature of its economy.

47157.description: Shelby County is Tennessee’s westernmost and most populous county, centered on Memphis. The Mississippi River marks the state’s lowest elevation along the county’s western edge.

47159.description: Smith County lies in Middle Tennessee in a transition between rugged highlands and rolling lowlands. Carthage is its county seat.

47161.description: Stewart County is in northwestern Middle Tennessee, with Dover as its county seat. The Cumberland River and Lake Barkley cross its rugged Highland Rim landscape.

47163.description: Sullivan County is part of the Kingsport–Bristol metropolitan area on Tennessee’s northeastern border. Its western landscape lies in the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians.

47165.description: Sumner County borders Kentucky along Tennessee’s central northern edge, with Gallatin as its county seat. It is part of metropolitan Nashville.

47167.description: Tipton County lies in Tennessee’s Mississippi Delta, with Covington as its county seat. Cotton fields and U.S. Highway 51 are prominent in its western landscape.

47169.description: Trousdale County is Tennessee’s smallest county by area, with a consolidated government centered on Hartsville. The county seat is Hartsville.

47171.description: Unicoi County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of eastern Tennessee, with Erwin as its county seat. The Nolichucky River and Appalachian Trail cross its mountainous terrain.

47173.description: Union County is part of metropolitan Knoxville, with Maynardville as its county seat. Its landscape is in the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians and includes about one-tenth water by area.

47175.description: Van Buren County straddles the western edge of the Cumberland Plateau, with Spencer as its county seat. The plateau occupies its eastern side, while the west slopes toward lower ground.

47177.description: Warren County lies along the Eastern Highland Rim near the Cumberland Plateau, with McMinnville as its county seat. The Caney Fork River and Twin Falls at Rock Island State Park are notable features.

47179.description: Washington County is centered on Jonesborough, its county seat, within the Johnson City metropolitan area. It lies in the Appalachian region of northeastern Tennessee.

47181.description: Waynesboro is the county seat of Wayne County, Tennessee’s second-largest county by area. The Tennessee River follows its northwestern boundary, while the Buffalo River crosses the northern part of the county.

47183.description: Weakley County lies in northwestern Tennessee, with Dresden as its county seat and Martin as its largest city. The North and Middle forks of the Obion River cross the county.

47185.description: White County lies in the Cookeville micropolitan area, with Sparta as its county seat. The eastern side rises onto the Cumberland Plateau.

47187.description: Williamson County lies in Middle Tennessee, with Franklin as its county seat. The Harpeth and Little Harpeth rivers are its primary streams.

47189.description: Wilson County lies in Middle Tennessee and is part of the Nashville metropolitan area. Lebanon is its county seat, and the Cumberland River marks its northern border.

48001.description: Anderson County lies at the meeting of East Texas’s Piney Woods and East Central Texas forests. Palestine is its county seat and micropolitan center.

48003.description: Andrews County lies in West Texas, with the city of Andrews as its county seat. Playa lakes, including Baird and Shafter lakes, dot the county.

48005.description: Lufkin is the county seat of Angelina County in East Texas. The Lufkin micropolitan area includes the entire county, which had 86,395 residents in 2020.

48007.description: Aransas County lies on the South Texas coast, with Rockport as its county seat and micropolitan center. More than half its total area is water.

48009.description: Archer County lies in the Wichita Falls metropolitan area, with Archer City as its county seat. Its landscape includes the red beds of north-central Texas.

48011.description: Armstrong County lies in the Texas Panhandle, with Claude as its county seat. It is part of the Amarillo metropolitan area.

48013.description: Atascosa County lies in South Texas, where rolling hills slope southeast toward the Atascosa River. Jourdanton is its county seat.

48015.description: Austin County is an agricultural county in southeastern Texas, with Bellville as its county seat. Its communities include a substantial German-settled history.

48017.description: Muleshoe is the county seat of Bailey County, Texas. The county had 6,904 residents in the 2020 census.

48019.description: Bandera County lies on the Edwards Plateau in the Texas Hill Country, within the Greater San Antonio area. Bandera is its county seat.

48021.description: Bastrop County lies in Central Texas within the Austin–Round Rock metropolitan area. Bastrop is its county seat.

48023.description: Baylor County lies in north-central Texas, with Seymour as its county seat. Its landscape is part of the Texas Red Beds, a region of Permian-era rock.

48025.description: Bee County is centered on Beeville, its county seat and micropolitan hub. The Aransas River begins in the county southwest of Beeville.

48027.description: Bell County is part of the Killeen–Temple metropolitan area in Central Texas. Belton is its county seat.

48029.description: Bexar County contains San Antonio, its county seat and largest city, in south-central Texas. It is a major urban county in the state’s southern region.

48031.description: Johnson City is the county seat of Blanco County in central Texas’s Hill Country, west of Austin and north of San Antonio. The Blanco and Pedernales rivers flow through the county.

48033.description: Borden County is a sparsely populated West Texas county, with Gail as its county seat. It is one of Texas’s few remaining counties without a paved road.

48035.description: Bosque County lies northwest of Waco in the greater Waco area, with Meridian as its county seat. Clifton is its largest community.

48037.description: Bowie County lies in northeast Texas, within the Texarkana metropolitan area. Boston is its legal county seat, while the courthouse is in New Boston.

48039.description: Brazoria County is part of the Houston–Pasadena–The Woodlands metropolitan area, with Angleton as county seat. It reaches the Gulf Coast, and water covers about one-sixth of its area.

48041.description: Bryan is the county seat of Brazos County, part of the Bryan–College Station metropolitan area. The Brazos River forms the county’s western border.

48043.description: Brewster County is the largest county in Texas by area and lies in the Trans-Pecos along the Mexican border. Alpine is its only city and county seat.

48045.description: Silverton is the county seat of Briscoe County, Texas. Caprock Canyons State Park and Trailway lies within the county.

48047.description: Brooks County is centered on Falfurrias, its county seat, in South Texas. It has very little surface water by area.

48049.description: Brown County lies in central Texas, with Brownwood as its county seat. It is part of the Brownwood metropolitan area.

48051.description: Caldwell is the county seat of Burleson County, part of the College Station–Bryan metropolitan area. Its population was 17,642 in 2020.

48053.description: Burnet County lies on the Edwards Plateau, northwest of Austin, with Burnet as its county seat. It is part of the Texas Hill Country.

48055.description: Caldwell County is centered on Lockhart, its county seat, and is part of the Austin metropolitan area. It sits in Central Texas south of the capital.

48057.description: Calhoun County borders the Gulf of Mexico, with Port Lavaca as its county seat. Water accounts for about half of its total area.

48059.description: Callahan County lies in central Texas, with Baird as its county seat. The Callahan Divide, a range of hills, extends across the county.

48061.description: Cameron County is Texas’s southernmost county, bordering the Gulf of Mexico. Brownsville is its county seat and largest city, with Harlingen the second-largest.

48063.description: Camp County is a small county in eastern Texas, with Pittsburg as its county seat. It is among the state’s smallest counties by area.

48065.description: Carson County lies in the Texas Panhandle, with Panhandle as its county seat. It is part of the Amarillo metropolitan area.

48067.description: Cass County sits in northeast Texas at the tripoint of Texas, Arkansas, and Louisiana. Linden is its county seat.

48069.description: Dimmitt is the county seat of Castro County, Texas. The county had 7,371 residents in the 2020 census.

48071.description: Chambers County is part of Greater Houston and meets Galveston Bay at Trinity Bay and East Bay. Anahuac is its county seat, and water covers nearly a third of the county.

48073.description: Rusk is the county seat of Cherokee County, Texas. The county forms the Jacksonville micropolitan area, which is part of the wider Tyler–Jacksonville combined area.

48075.description: Childress is the county seat of Childress County, Texas. The county had 6,664 residents in the 2020 census.

48077.description: Clay County lies in north-central Texas, with Henrietta as its county seat. Lake Arrowhead and its state park are prominent recreation features.

48079.description: Cochran County sits on the high plains of the Llano Estacado along the New Mexico border. Morton is its county seat.

48081.description: Coke County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Robert Lee as its county seat. It is an inland county in west-central Texas.

48083.description: Coleman County is centered on the city of Coleman, its county seat. It lies in central Texas.

48085.description: Collin County is part of the Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area, with a small portion of Dallas extending into it. It is a fast-growing suburban county north of Dallas.

48087.description: Wellington is the county seat of Collingsworth County, Texas. The county had 2,652 residents in the 2020 census.

48089.description: Columbus is the county seat of Colorado County, Texas. The county is named for the Colorado River and had 20,557 residents in 2020.

48091.description: Comal County lies on the Edwards Plateau within the Texas German Belt. The Balcones Escarpment crosses the county, separating rocky western hills from lower ground to the east.

48093.description: Comanche County sits on the Edwards Plateau in Central Texas, with Comanche as its county seat. It lies north of the state’s geographic center.

48095.description: Concho County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Paint Rock as its county seat. It is a sparsely populated county in west-central Texas.

48097.description: Cooke County borders Oklahoma in north-central Texas, with Gainesville as its county seat. It lies within the Dallas–Fort Worth region.

48099.description: Coryell County is centered on Gatesville, its county seat, in Central Texas. It is part of the Killeen–Temple metropolitan area.

48101.description: Cottle County lies in the Texas Panhandle, with Paducah as its county seat. It is a sparsely populated county in north-central Texas.

48103.description: Crane County lies in West Texas, with Crane as its county seat. Oil and gas production make up its largest economic sector.

48105.description: Crockett County lies on the Edwards Plateau in West Texas, with Ozona as its county seat. Nearly all of its area is land.

48107.description: Crosbyton is the county seat of Crosby County, Texas. Along with Lubbock and Lynn counties, it is part of the Lubbock metropolitan area.

48109.description: Culberson County is one of Texas’s largest counties by area, with Van Horn as its county seat. The Trans-Pecos landscape includes the Guadalupe Mountains.

48111.description: Dallam County is Texas’s northwesternmost county and borders both Oklahoma and New Mexico. Dalhart is its county seat.

48113.description: Dallas County contains the city of Dallas and is one of Texas’s largest urban counties. It lies in the heart of the Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area.

48115.description: Lamesa is the county seat of Dawson County, which forms the Lamesa micropolitan area. The county had 12,456 residents in 2020.

48117.description: Deaf Smith County is centered on Hereford, its county seat, in the Texas Panhandle. Hereford is known for its cattle and beef industry.

48119.description: Delta County is named for its triangular shape between two forks of the Sulphur River. Cooper is both its county seat and largest city.

48121.description: Denton County is part of the Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area, with Denton as its county seat. Its cities include Denton and a portion of Dallas.

48123.description: Cuero is the county seat of DeWitt County, Texas. Founded in 1846, the county was named for Green DeWitt, who established an early Texas colony.

48125.description: Dickens is the county seat of Dickens County, Texas. The county had 1,770 residents in the 2020 census.

48127.description: Carrizo Springs is the county seat of Dimmit County, Texas. The county had 8,615 residents in the 2020 census.

48129.description: Clarendon is the county seat of Donley County, Texas. The county had 3,258 residents in the 2020 census.

48131.description: San Diego is the county seat of Duval County, Texas. The county had 9,831 residents in the 2020 census.

48133.description: Eastland is the county seat of Eastland County in central West Texas. The communities of Cisco and Ranger each have a junior college.

48135.description: Ector County is centered on Odessa, its county seat, in West Texas. Its flat, semiarid landscape receives about 14 inches of average annual rainfall.

48137.description: Rocksprings is the county seat of Edwards County on Texas’s Edwards Plateau. The county had 1,422 residents in 2020.

48139.description: Ellis County is part of the Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area, with Waxahachie as its county seat. Lake Waxahachie lies south of the city.

48141.description: El Paso County occupies Texas’s westernmost edge along the U.S.–Mexico border. El Paso is its county seat and only large city.

48143.description: Erath County is centered on Stephenville, its county seat, in north-central Texas. It is part of the Stephenville micropolitan area.

48145.description: Falls County is centered on Marlin, its county seat, along the Brazos River. The county takes its name from waterfalls that once marked the river here.

48147.description: Fannin County borders Oklahoma on the western edge of Northeast Texas. Bonham is its county seat, and Bois d’Arc Creek and the Sulphur River drain the county.

48149.description: La Grange is the county seat of Fayette County in central Texas. Settled by German and Czech emigrants in the 1830s, the county lies in the Texas German belt.

48151.description: Roby is the county seat of Fisher County, Texas. The county had 3,672 residents in the 2020 census.

48153.description: Floydada is the county seat of Floyd County, Texas. The county had 5,402 residents in the 2020 census.

48155.description: Crowell is the county seat and only incorporated community in Foard County, Texas. The county had 1,095 residents in 2020.

48157.description: Fort Bend County is part of Greater Houston, with Richmond as its county seat. The county was named for a blockhouse on a bend of the Brazos River.

48159.description: Franklin County is centered on Mount Vernon, its county seat, in northeast Texas. Water accounts for a small share of its total area.

48161.description: Fairfield is the county seat of Freestone County, Texas. The county had 19,435 residents in the 2020 census.

48163.description: Frio County is centered on Pearsall, its county seat, in South Texas. It is an inland county in the state’s southern region.

48165.description: Seminole is the county seat of Gaines County, Texas. The county had 21,598 residents in the 2020 census.

48167.description: Galveston County follows the Gulf Coast and surrounds Galveston Bay, with Galveston as its county seat. Water covers more than half of its total area.

48169.description: Garza County lies southeast of Lubbock along the Llano Estacado escarpment and its canyonlands. Post is its county seat and only incorporated municipality.

48171.description: Gillespie County lies on the Edwards Plateau in the Texas German Belt. Fredericksburg is its county seat and largest city.

48173.description: Glasscock County is centered on Garden City, its county seat, in West Texas. The Spraberry oil field underlies much of the county.

48175.description: Goliad County is centered on the city of Goliad, its county seat, in South Texas. It is part of the Victoria metropolitan area.

48177.description: Gonzales County lies along the Austin–San Antonio corridor, with Gonzales as its county seat. The county’s roads connect communities in this rapidly developing corridor.

48179.description: Gray County is centered on Pampa, its county seat, in the Texas Panhandle. It is part of the Pampa micropolitan area.

48181.description: Grayson County is centered on Sherman, its county seat, along the Oklahoma border. It is part of the Sherman–Denison metropolitan area.

48183.description: Gregg County lies in East Texas, with Longview as its county seat and largest city. It is part of the Longview metropolitan area.

48185.description: Grimes County is centered on Anderson, its county seat, in southeastern Texas. It was historically rural and agricultural before growth late in the twentieth century.

48187.description: Seguin is the county seat of Guadalupe County, part of the San Antonio metropolitan area. The county is named for the Guadalupe River and had 172,706 residents in 2020.

48189.description: Plainview is the county seat of Hale County, Texas. The county forms the Plainview micropolitan area and had 32,522 residents in 2020.

48191.description: Memphis is the county seat of Hall County, Texas. The county had 2,825 residents in the 2020 census.

48193.description: Hamilton County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Hamilton as its county seat. It is part of Central Texas.

48195.description: Spearman is the county seat of Hansford County, Texas. The county had 5,285 residents in the 2020 census.

48197.description: Hardeman County is centered on Quanah, its county seat and largest city, in the Texas Panhandle. The Red River forms its northern edge.

48199.description: Hardin County lies on the flat coastal plains of southeast Texas, where much of the land is covered by Big Thicket forest. Kountze is its county seat.

48201.description: Harris County contains Houston and is Texas’s most populous county, with more than 4.7 million residents in 2020. The county is part of the Houston metropolitan area.

48203.description: Harrison County borders Louisiana in eastern Texas, with Marshall as its county seat. Caddo Lake and several bayous drain the north and east toward the Red River.

48205.description: Channing is the county seat of Hartley County, Texas. The county had 5,382 residents in the 2020 census.

48207.description: Haskell County is centered on the city of Haskell, its county seat, in north-central Texas. It is a sparsely populated inland county.

48209.description: Hays County is part of the Austin metropolitan area, with San Marcos as its county seat. Its landscape spans the Edwards Plateau and Texas Blackland Prairies.

48211.description: Canadian is the county seat of Hemphill County, Texas. The county had 3,382 residents in the 2020 census.

48213.description: Athens is the county seat of Henderson County, Texas. The county forms the Athens micropolitan area, included in the Dallas–Fort Worth combined area.

48215.description: Hidalgo County lies in South Texas along the Rio Grande, with Edinburg as its county seat and McAllen as its largest city. Its northern soils include sandy and light loamy surface layers over clayey subsoil.

48217.description: Hillsboro is the county seat of Hill County in Central Texas. The county had 35,874 residents in 2020 and lies outside the Texas Hill Country.

48219.description: Levelland is the county seat of Hockley County. The county forms the Levelland micropolitan area, part of the wider Lubbock–Levelland combined area.

48221.description: Granbury is the county seat of Hood County, which forms the Granbury micropolitan area. The county is adjacent to the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex.

48223.description: Sulphur Springs is the county seat of Hopkins County, which forms the Sulphur Springs micropolitan area. Once known as the Dairy Capital of Texas, the county is home to the Southwest Dairy Museum.

48225.description: Houston County is centered on Crockett, its county seat, in East Texas. Davy Crockett National Forest and Ratcliff Lake Recreation Area lie east of the town.

48227.description: Howard County is centered on Big Spring, its county seat, at the boundary between the Llano Estacado and Edwards Plateau. Beals Creek drains the county.

48229.description: Hudspeth County borders Mexico in far west Texas and is one of the state’s largest counties by area. Sierra Blanca is its county seat, and part of Guadalupe Mountains National Park lies within it.

48231.description: Hunt County lies in Northeast Texas and combines Blackland Prairie, East Central Texas forest, and the edge of the Piney Woods. Greenville is its county seat.

48233.description: Hutchinson County is centered on Stinnett, its county seat, in the Texas Panhandle. It is part of the Borger micropolitan area.

48235.description: Irion County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Mertzon as its county seat. The Spraberry oil field underlies much of the county.

48237.description: Jack County lies in north-central Texas, with Jacksboro as its county seat. Ranching is a major part of its agricultural economy.

48239.description: Edna is the county seat of Jackson County, Texas. The county had 14,988 residents in the 2020 census.

48241.description: Jasper is the county seat of Jasper County, Texas. The county was organized in 1837 and had 32,980 residents in 2020.

48243.description: Jeff Davis County contains the Davis Mountains, the highest mountain range located entirely within Texas. Fort Davis is its county seat in the Trans-Pecos.

48245.description: Jefferson County lies on the Gulf Coast plains of southeast Texas, with Beaumont as its county seat. The Neches River marks its northeastern boundary, and water covers about one-fifth of its area.

48247.description: Jim Hogg County lies in South Texas, with Hebbronville as its county seat. Nearly all of its area is land.

48249.description: Alice is the county seat of Jim Wells County, which forms the Alice micropolitan area. The county is included in the wider Corpus Christi–Kingsville–Alice combined area.

48251.description: Cleburne is the county seat of Johnson County, part of the Dallas–Fort Worth–Arlington metropolitan area. The county had 179,927 residents in 2020.

48253.description: Jones County lies in central West Texas, with Anson as its county seat. It is part of the Abilene metropolitan area.

48255.description: Karnes County is centered on Karnes City, its county seat, in south-central Texas. Oil production has been an important part of its economy since the late 2000s.

48257.description: Kaufman is the county seat and Forney the largest city in Kaufman County in northeastern Texas. The Trinity River bounds its southwest side, and its east fork drains the county.

48259.description: Kendall County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Boerne as its county seat. It is part of the San Antonio metropolitan area.

48261.description: Kenedy County borders the Gulf of Mexico, with Sarita as its county seat. It is one of the largest Texas counties by area, despite having very few residents.

48263.description: Kent County is one of Texas’s least populous counties, with Jayton as its county seat. It lies in West Texas.

48265.description: Kerrville is the county seat and largest city in Kerr County on Texas’s Edwards Plateau. The county forms the Kerrville micropolitan area.

48267.description: Kimble County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Junction as its county seat. The county contains the highest natural point in the Texas Hill Country.

48269.description: King County is among the least populated counties in Texas and is centered on Guthrie, its county seat. Its landscape includes grassland and broken, hilly country; cattle raising is a main industry.

48271.description: Kinney County lies along the Rio Grande opposite Mexico, with Brackettville as its county seat. Small tributaries of the river drain the county.

48273.description: Kleberg County borders the Gulf of Mexico, with Kingsville as its county seat. Baffin Bay forms much of its boundary with Kenedy County, and water covers about one-fifth of its area.

48275.description: Benjamin is the county seat of Knox County, Texas. The county had 3,353 residents in the 2020 census.

48277.description: Lamar County lies in Northeast Texas, with Paris as its county seat. It is part of the Paris micropolitan area.

48279.description: Littlefield is the county seat of Lamb County, Texas. The county had 13,045 residents in the 2020 census.

48281.description: Lampasas County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Lampasas as its county seat. It is part of the Killeen–Temple metropolitan area.

48283.description: Cotulla is the county seat of La Salle County, Texas. Interstate 35 passes south of Cotulla, and the county had 6,664 residents in 2020.

48285.description: Lavaca County is centered on Hallettsville, its county seat, in southeastern Texas. The Lavaca River runs through the county.

48287.description: Giddings is the county seat of Lee County, Texas. The county had 17,478 residents in the 2020 census.

48289.description: Centerville is the county seat of Leon County, Texas. The county had 15,719 residents in the 2020 census.

48291.description: Liberty County is centered on the city of Liberty, its county seat, in southeast Texas. The Trinity River divides much of the county and connects it to the San Jacinto River system.

48293.description: Groesbeck is the county seat of Limestone County, Texas. The county had 22,146 residents in the 2020 census.

48295.description: Lipscomb County lies in the Texas Panhandle, with Lipscomb as its county seat. Nearly all of its total area is land.

48297.description: Live Oak County is centered on George West, its county seat, in South Texas. Choke Canyon Reservoir is a prominent feature.

48299.description: Llano County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Llano as its county seat. Enchanted Rock State Natural Area is in the county’s southern part.

48301.description: Loving County is the least populous county in the United States, with 64 residents in 2020. Mentone is its county seat and only community.

48303.description: Lubbock is the county seat and largest city in Lubbock County. Along with Crosby and Lynn counties, it forms the Lubbock metropolitan area.

48305.description: Tahoka is the county seat of Lynn County, part of the Lubbock metropolitan area. Local museums include the Tahoka Pioneer Museum and the O’Donnell Heritage Museum.

48307.description: Brady is the county seat of McCulloch County on the Edwards Plateau. Texas’s geographic center lies within the county near Brady.

48309.description: McLennan County is centered on Waco, its county seat and largest city, in Central Texas. The Brazos River passes through Waco.

48311.description: McMullen County is one of Texas’s least populous counties, with Tilden as its county seat. It lies in South Texas.

48313.description: Madison County lies between the Trinity and Navasota rivers in east-central Texas. Madisonville is its county seat.

48315.description: Jefferson is the county seat of Marion County, Texas. The county had 9,725 residents in the 2020 census.

48317.description: Martin County is centered on Stanton, its county seat, in West Texas. The Spraberry oil field underlies much of the county.

48319.description: Mason County is a rural county on the Edwards Plateau, with the town of Mason as its county seat. Ranchland is characteristic of its landscape.

48321.description: Matagorda County meets the Gulf of Mexico and includes Matagorda Bay, with Bay City as its county seat. Water covers nearly one-third of its total area.

48323.description: Maverick County lies along the Mexican border, with Eagle Pass as its county seat and micropolitan center. It is part of South Texas.
