48325.description: Medina County lies in south-central Texas, with Hondo as its county seat. Its northern edge rises into the Edwards Plateau and Texas Hill Country, and the Medina Dam is a notable landmark.

48327.description: Menard County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Menard as its county seat. It is a sparsely populated county in central Texas.

48329.description: Midland County is centered on the city of Midland, its county seat and metropolitan core. The Spraberry oil field underlies much of the county.

48331.description: Cameron is the county seat of Milam County, Texas. The county had 24,754 residents in the 2020 census.

48333.description: Mills County lies near the center of Texas, across the Limestone Cut Plain and Western Cross Timbers subregions. Goldthwaite is its county seat.

48335.description: Mitchell County is centered on Colorado City, its county seat, in West Texas. Lake Colorado City and Lake Champion are two reservoirs in the county.

48337.description: Montague is the county seat of Montague County, Texas. The county had 19,965 residents in the 2020 census.

48339.description: Montgomery County is part of metropolitan Houston, with Conroe as its county seat. It lies north of the city of Houston.

48341.description: Moore County is centered on Dumas, its county seat and micropolitan center, in the Texas Panhandle. Window on the Plains Museum in Dumas documents the area’s history.

48343.description: Morris County lies near Texas’s eastern border, with Daingerfield as its county seat. It is one of the state’s smallest counties by area.

48345.description: Motley County is one of Texas’s least populous counties, with Matador as its county seat. It lies in the Texas Panhandle.

48347.description: Nacogdoches County is centered on Nacogdoches, its county seat and micropolitan hub, in East Texas. It is the state’s leading blueberry producer.

48349.description: Navarro County is centered on Corsicana, its county seat and micropolitan center. It is part of the Dallas–Fort Worth combined statistical area.

48351.description: Newton County is Texas’s easternmost county, with Newton as its county seat. It is part of the Beaumont–Port Arthur metropolitan area.

48353.description: Nolan County lies in west-central Texas, with Sweetwater as its county seat and micropolitan center. Its landscape includes parts of the Cross Timbers and Rolling Plains.

48355.description: Nueces County lies along the Gulf of Mexico, with Corpus Christi as its county seat and largest city. Water accounts for more than one-quarter of its total area.

48357.description: Ochiltree County lies in the Texas Panhandle, with Perryton as its county seat. Almost all of its area is land.

48359.description: Oldham County is part of the Amarillo metropolitan area, with Vega as its county seat. Its southern area sits on the Llano Estacado.

48361.description: Orange County occupies Texas’s southeast corner in the Golden Triangle, bordering Louisiana and the Sabine River. Orange is its county seat, and the local economy includes petroleum refining and paper milling.

48363.description: Palo Pinto County lies in north-central Texas, with Palo Pinto as its county seat. It is part of the Mineral Wells micropolitan area.

48365.description: Panola County lies in East Texas, with Carthage as its county seat. It developed historically around cotton plantations.

48367.description: Parker County is centered on Weatherford, its county seat, west of Fort Worth. The Brazos River crosses the county.

48369.description: Parmer County lies on the High Plains of the Llano Estacado in the southwestern Texas Panhandle. Farwell is its county seat.

48371.description: Pecos County is the second-largest county in Texas by area, with Fort Stockton as its county seat. It lies in West Texas.

48373.description: Polk County lies in East Texas, with Livingston as its county seat. The Alabama–Coushatta Indian Reservation is located within the county.

48375.description: Potter County contains Amarillo, its county seat and largest city, in the Texas Panhandle. It is part of the Amarillo metropolitan area.

48377.description: Presidio County lies along the Rio Grande and the Mexican border in the Trans-Pecos. Marfa is its county seat.

48379.description: Rains County is centered on Emory, its county seat, in northeast Texas. Lake Tawakoni and Lake Fork Reservoir extend into the county.

48381.description: Randall County contains Palo Duro Canyon, the second-largest canyon in the United States. Canyon is its county seat, and the county is part of the Amarillo metropolitan area.

48383.description: Reagan County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Big Lake as its county seat. The Spraberry oil field underlies much of the county.

48385.description: Leakey is the county seat of Real County on Texas’s Edwards Plateau. The county had 2,758 residents in 2020.

48387.description: Red River County is centered on Clarksville, its county seat, in northeast Texas. The Red River marks its northern boundary.

48389.description: Reeves County is a large West Texas county, with Pecos as its county seat and most populous city. It is part of the Trans-Pecos.

48391.description: Refugio is the county seat of Refugio County, Texas. The county had 6,741 residents in the 2020 census.

48393.description: Roberts County lies in the Texas Panhandle, with Miami as its county seat and only incorporated community. The Canadian River valley cuts across otherwise relatively flat terrain, much of it used for cattle ranching.

48395.description: Franklin is the county seat of Robertson County in east-central Texas. The county is part of the College Station–Bryan metropolitan area.

48397.description: Rockwall County is the smallest county in Texas by area, with Rockwall as its county seat. It is part of the Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area.

48399.description: Ballinger is the county seat of Runnels County, Texas. The county had 9,900 residents in the 2020 census.

48401.description: Rusk County lies in East Texas, with Henderson as its county seat. It is part of the Longview metropolitan area.

48403.description: The Sabine River forms the eastern border of Sabine County, on Texas’s central eastern edge. Water covers 15 percent of its total area, and the county had 9,894 residents in 2020.

48405.description: San Augustine County lies in East Texas, with San Augustine as its county seat. Water accounts for about one-tenth of its area.

48407.description: Coldspring is the county seat of San Jacinto County, Texas. The county had 27,402 residents in the 2020 census.

48409.description: San Patricio County lies near the lower Gulf Coast and is part of metropolitan Corpus Christi. Sinton is its county seat, and the Gulf of Mexico borders the county.

48411.description: San Saba County lies on the Edwards Plateau in western Central Texas, with San Saba as its county seat. The San Saba River and Colorado River meet near the county.

48413.description: Schleicher County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Eldorado as its county seat. It is a sparsely populated county in west-central Texas.

48415.description: Scurry County is centered on Snyder, its county seat and home of Western Texas College. Lake J. B. Thomas is a major reservoir in the county.

48417.description: Albany is the county seat of Shackelford County, Texas. Historic Fort Griffin lies within the county, and residents stage the Fort Griffin Fandangle musical in Albany each June.

48419.description: Shelby County lies in far eastern Texas, with Center as its county seat. It borders Louisiana.

48421.description: Stratford is the county seat of Sherman County, Texas. The county had 2,782 residents in the 2020 census.

48423.description: Smith County is centered on Tyler, its county seat and largest city, in East Texas. It is part of the Tyler metropolitan area.

48425.description: Somervell County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Glen Rose as its county seat. It is one of the smallest counties in Texas by area.

48427.description: Starr County lies along the Rio Grande in South Texas, with Rio Grande City as its county seat. Oilseeds and dry beans are among its major crops.

48429.description: Breckenridge is the county seat of Stephens County, Texas. The county had 9,101 residents in the 2020 census.

48431.description: Sterling County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Sterling City as its county seat. It is among the state’s least populous counties.

48433.description: Stonewall County lies in north-central Texas, with Aspermont as its county seat. It is a sparsely populated inland county.

48435.description: Sonora is the county seat of Sutton County on Texas’s Edwards Plateau. The county had 3,372 residents in 2020.

48437.description: Tulia is the county seat of Swisher County, Texas. The county had 6,971 residents in the 2020 census.

48439.description: Tarrant County contains Fort Worth, its county seat and largest city, in the Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area. It is one of the most populous counties in Texas.

48441.description: Taylor County is centered on Abilene, its county seat, in west-central Texas. It is part of the Abilene metropolitan area.

48443.description: Terrell County lies in West Texas, with Sanderson as its county seat. Its landscape is mostly semiarid steppe, and nearly all of its area is land.

48445.description: Brownfield is the county seat of Terry County, Texas. The county had 11,831 residents in 2020 and is among the country’s most productive pumpkin-producing counties.

48447.description: Throckmorton County lies in north-central Texas, with Throckmorton as its county seat. It is a sparsely populated inland county.

48449.description: Titus County is centered on Mount Pleasant, its county seat, in northeastern Texas. Water accounts for a small share of its total area.

48451.description: Tom Green County is centered on San Angelo, its county seat, on the Edwards Plateau. Lake Nasworthy, O.C. Fisher Reservoir, Twin Buttes Reservoir, and San Angelo State Park are among its protected areas.

48453.description: Travis County is centered on Austin, the state capital and county seat, in Central Texas. It is part of the Austin metropolitan area.

48455.description: Trinity County lies in East Texas, with Groveton as its county seat. It is part of the Huntsville micropolitan area.

48457.description: Woodville is the county seat of Tyler County, Texas. The county had 19,798 residents in the 2020 census.

48459.description: Upshur County is centered on Gilmer, its county seat, in eastern Texas. It is part of the Longview metropolitan area.

48461.description: Upton County lies on the Edwards Plateau, with Rankin as its county seat. The Spraberry oil field underlies much of the county.

48463.description: Uvalde County lies in South Texas, with Uvalde as its county seat. It is part of the Uvalde micropolitan area.

48465.description: Del Rio is the county seat of Val Verde County on the southern Edwards Plateau. The Del Rio micropolitan area includes the entire county, which had 47,586 residents in 2020.

48467.description: Van Zandt County lies in northeast Texas, with Canton as its county seat. Its landscape spans the Blackland Prairie, Post Oak Savannah, and Piney Woods.

48469.description: Victoria is the county seat of Victoria County, Texas. The county had 91,319 residents in the 2020 census.

48471.description: Walker County lies in east-central Texas, with Huntsville as its county seat. It is part of the Huntsville micropolitan area.

48473.description: Waller County is centered on Hempstead, its county seat, in southeast Texas. It is part of the Houston metropolitan area, and Igloo Corporation is headquartered there.

48475.description: Ward County is centered on Monahans, its county seat, in West Texas. Almost all of its land area is dry land.

48477.description: Washington County lies in southeastern Texas, with Brenham as its county seat. It sits northwest of Houston along U.S. Highway 290.

48479.description: Webb County forms the Laredo metropolitan area, with Laredo as its county seat and largest city. It borders the Mexican states of Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas.

48481.description: Wharton County forms the El Campo micropolitan area, part of the larger Houston–The Woodlands combined statistical area. Wharton is the county seat, and the 2020 population was 41,570.

48483.description: Wheeler is the county seat of Wheeler County, which had 4,990 residents in 2020. Shamrock lies at the intersection of Interstate 40 and Highway 83.

48485.description: The Wichita River and other streams drain Wichita County, part of the Texas Red Beds of Early Permian sedimentary rock. Wichita Falls is the county seat.

48487.description: Vernon is the county seat of Wilbarger County in North Texas. The county had 12,887 residents in the 2020 census.

48489.description: Willacy County borders the Gulf of Mexico, with water covering 25 percent of its area. Raymondville is its county seat, and the county is part of the Rio Grande Valley region.

48491.description: The Balcones Escarpment divides Williamson County’s hilly western brushland from its flat to gently rolling eastern plains. Cattle ranching remains important in some areas, and cotton is still grown toward Hutto and Taylor.

48493.description: Floresville is the county seat of Wilson County, part of the San Antonio–New Braunfels metropolitan area. The county had 49,753 residents in 2020.

48495.description: Winkler County has a generally dry climate, with hot conditions in spring and summer. Kermit is its county seat, and its 2020 population was 7,791.

48497.description: Decatur is the county seat of Wise County, part of the Dallas–Fort Worth–Arlington metropolitan area. Its population was 68,632 in 2020.

48499.description: Quitman is the county seat of Wood County, where water covers 7.3 percent of the area. Early industries included sawmills, cotton gins and railroad tie cutting, and several communities began as sawmill towns.

48501.description: Yoakum County lies in the western Texas Panhandle, with Plains as its county seat. It had 7,694 residents in 2020, and virtually all its area is land.

48503.description: Graham is the county seat of Young County, Texas. The county had 17,867 residents in 2020, and water covers about 1.8 percent of its total area.

48505.description: Zapata County lies in the Lower Rio Grande Valley on the shore of Falcon International Reservoir. Zapata is its county seat, and the Falcon Dam Port of Entry links the county to Mexico.

48507.description: Crystal City is the county seat and largest city of Zavala County, Texas. The 2020 census counted 9,670 residents.

49001.description: Beaver County’s eastern Tushar Mountains give way westward to desert valleys separated by mountains with light juniper forest. Beaver is the county seat and largest city.

49003.description: Box Elder County combines barren desert with high forested mountains in northwestern Utah. Its main cities lie along the Wasatch Front on the southeastern border, and Brigham City is the county seat.

49005.description: Cache Valley and the Bear River lie between the Wellsville Mountains to the west and Bear River Mountains to the east. Logan is Cache County’s seat and largest city.

49007.description: The Green River forms Carbon County’s eastern border, while the Wasatch Range and Book Cliffs surround its lower central valley. Price is the county seat and largest city.

49009.description: Daggett County contains part of the Uinta Mountains and the deep Green River gorge used to create Flaming Gorge Reservoir. Manila is its county seat.

49011.description: Davis County lies between the Great Salt Lake and Wasatch Range and includes Antelope Island. Farmington is its county seat, while Layton is its largest city.

49013.description: Duchesne County's terrain is semi-arid, rough, and scarred with drainages. Its county seat is Duchesne, and the largest city is Roosevelt.

49015.description: The San Rafael Swell occupies much of eastern Emery County, while the Wasatch Plateau marks its western boundary. Castle Dale is the county seat, and Huntington is the largest city.

49017.description: The Colorado River forms Garfield County’s eastern boundary, beyond a landscape of mountains, plateaus and canyons. Panguitch is its county seat and largest city.

49019.description: Grand County’s arid terrain exposes red rock formations carved by water and wind. Moab is its county seat and largest city, and the county serves as a gateway to Arches and Canyonlands national parks.

49021.description: Iron County ranges from the arid Escalante Desert and Great Basin ranges in the west to High Plateau meadows and forests in the east. Parowan is the county seat, while Cedar City is the largest city.

49023.description: Juab County has arid plains, hills and low mountains, with its eastern border loosely following a Wasatch Mountains ridgeline. Nephi is its county seat and largest city.

49025.description: Lake Powell forms Kane County’s eastern border, and Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument covers much of its terrain. Kanab is the county seat and largest city.

49027.description: The Sevier Desert covers much of Millard County, while the Pahvant Mountains form its eastern boundary. Fillmore is the county seat, and Delta is the largest city.

49029.description: Morgan County centers on the narrow, mountain-ringed Morgan Valley, through which the Weber River flows. Morgan is its county seat and largest city.

49031.description: The Sevier River flows north through west-central Piute County, with the Tushar Mountains along its western border. Junction is the county seat, and Circleville is the largest town.

49033.description: Rich County includes the farming-oriented Bear River Valley and the southern part of Bear Lake Valley. Randolph is its county seat, and Garden City is its largest town.

49035.description: The Wasatch and Oquirrh mountains frame Salt Lake Valley, crossed by the north-flowing Jordan River. Salt Lake City is Salt Lake County’s seat and largest city.

49037.description: San Juan County’s western and southern boundaries follow deep gorges carved by the Colorado and San Juan rivers. Monticello is the county seat, and Blanding is the most populous city.

49039.description: Sanpete Valley runs north to south through the county between the Wasatch Plateau and lower, drier San Pitch Mountains. Manti is Sanpete County’s seat, and Ephraim is its largest city.

49041.description: Sevier County terrain consists of semi-arid but arable rolling areas punctuated by northeast–southwest mountain ridges, usually forested. Its county seat and largest city is Richfield.

49043.description: Summit County’s central and eastern portions contain the Uinta Mountains, while its west reaches the Wasatch Mountains’ eastern slopes. Coalville is the county seat, and Park City is its largest city.

49045.description: Tooele County includes large parts of the Great Salt Lake Desert and the parallel Oquirrh, Stansbury and Cedar mountain ranges. Tooele is its county seat and largest city.

49047.description: Uintah County ranges from the Uinta Mountains through Ashley Valley to rugged canyonlands and southern hills. Vernal is the county seat, and oil, natural gas, phosphate and gilsonite extraction are primary economic activities.

49049.description: Utah County ranges from steep Wasatch mountains to Utah Valley, where Utah Lake occupies much of the valley floor. Provo is the county seat and largest city.

49051.description: Mountain-ringed Heber Valley lies in Wasatch County, which spans the Colorado and Great Basin drainage systems. Heber City is the county seat and largest city.

49053.description: Washington County’s arid terrain spans parts of the Colorado Plateau, Great Basin and Mojave Desert. St. George is its county seat and largest city.

49055.description: Wayne County ranges from western forests to eastern deserts and river-carved terrain. The Green and Colorado rivers form its eastern boundary, while most residents live in Rabbit Valley.

49057.description: Weber County extends from the Wasatch Range into the Great Salt Lake, with the Weber and Ogden rivers running through its valleys. Ogden is its county seat and largest city.

50001.description: Otter Creek flows south to north through Addison County in western Vermont. Middlebury is the county seat, and the county had 37,363 residents in 2020.

50003.description: Bennington and Manchester jointly serve as Bennington County’s county seats. Bennington is also its largest municipality, and the county had 37,347 residents in 2020.

50005.description: The Connecticut River forms part of Caledonia County’s eastern boundary, receiving the south-flowing Passumpsic River at Barnet. St. Johnsbury is the county seat.

50007.description: Burlington is Chittenden County’s seat, home to the University of Vermont and its affiliated medical center. Mount Mansfield, Vermont’s highest summit, lies in the county’s town of Underhill.

50009.description: Essex County contains a bog and wildlife refuge within the Nulhegan Basin. Guildhall is its county seat, and its 2020 population of 5,920 made it the least populous county in New England.

50011.description: Franklin County borders Quebec and is part of the Burlington metropolitan area, with St. Albans as its county seat. In 2009 it had 239 dairy farms, the most of any Vermont county.

50013.description: Four of Grand Isle County’s five towns lie entirely on Lake Champlain islands, while Alburgh occupies a peninsula extending south from Quebec. North Hero is the county seat.

50015.description: Hyde Park is the county seat of Lamoille County, while Morristown is its largest town and main commercial center. It is Vermont’s second-smallest county by area.

50017.description: Orange County’s hilly terrain is crossed by Interstate 89 in the west and Interstate 91 along its eastern edge. Chelsea is the county seat.

50019.description: Orleans County lies between the eastern and western ranges of the Green Mountains. Its shire town is the city of Newport.

50021.description: Otter Creek runs south to north through Rutland County, Vermont’s second-largest county by area. Rutland is the county seat and most populous municipality.

50023.description: Montpelier is the county seat of Washington County, while Barre is its most populous city. The county had 59,807 residents in 2020.

50025.description: Newfane is the county seat and Brattleboro the largest municipality in Windham County. It is Vermont’s third-largest county by land area and had 45,905 residents in 2020.

50027.description: Windsor County is Vermont’s largest county by area, with Woodstock as its county seat. Hartford is its largest municipality, and the 2020 population was 57,753.

51001.description: Accomack County forms part of Virginia’s Eastern Shore on the southern Delmarva Peninsula, between Chesapeake Bay and the Atlantic Ocean. Accomac is the county seat, and Chincoteague is its largest town.

51003.description: Albemarle County lies in Virginia’s Piedmont region and is part of the Charlottesville metropolitan area. Its county seat is Charlottesville, an independent city entirely surrounded by the county.

51005.description: Alleghany County is entirely within the Valley and Ridge physiographic region of Virginia. The county seat is Covington, an independent city completely surrounded by the county.

51007.description: Amelia County lies in the Piedmont region of Virginia, known for rolling hills and small ridges that lie between the Blue Ridge Mountains and Coastal Plain of Virginia. Its county seat is Amelia Court House.

51009.description: Amherst County lies in Virginia’s Piedmont region and is part of the Lynchburg metropolitan area. Its county seat is Amherst, and its population was 31,307 in 2020.

51011.description: Appomattox County lies near the center of Virginia in the Piedmont region. Its county seat is Appomattox, and it is part of the Lynchburg metropolitan area.

51013.description: Arlington County lies across the Potomac River from Washington, with terrain spanning the Appalachian Piedmont and Atlantic Coastal Plain. It contains both suburban and urbanized districts.

51015.description: Augusta County lies in the Shenandoah Valley and completely surrounds the independent cities of Staunton and Waynesboro. Staunton is its county seat, while county offices are in Verona.

51017.description: Forests cover 89 percent of Bath County, including large areas of George Washington National Forest. Warm Springs is the county seat, and Hot Springs is the largest community.

51019.description: Bedford County lies in Virginia’s Piedmont region, with Bedford as its county seat. Bedford rejoined the county in 2013 after having been an independent city since 1968.

51021.description: Bland County lies entirely in the Ridge and Valley province, with mountains separated by small river valleys. Bland is its county seat, and the North Fork of the Holston River has its headwaters in the county.

51023.description: The Blue Ridge Mountains run along eastern Botetourt County and the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians along its west. Fincastle is the county seat, and the county is part of the Roanoke metropolitan area.

51025.description: Brunswick County lies on Virginia’s southern border, with Lawrenceville as its county seat. The 2020 census counted 15,849 residents.

51027.description: Buchanan County lies on the rugged Appalachian Plateau in far western Virginia, bordering both Kentucky and West Virginia. Grundy is its county seat.

51029.description: Buckingham County is part of the Piedmont region of Virginia, and the county seat is Buckingham Courthouse. The 2020 census counted 16,824 residents.

51031.description: Rustburg is the county seat of Campbell County in south-central Virginia. The county lies in the Piedmont region, borders the Blue Ridge Mountains and forms part of the Lynchburg metropolitan area.

51033.description: Caroline County lies in eastern Virginia, with part of its northern boundary along the Rappahannock River. Bowling Green is the county seat.

51035.description: About one fifth of Carroll County lies in the Piedmont, while the remainder is in the Appalachian Mountains. Hillsville is its county seat and only town.

51036.description: Charles City County lies southeast of Richmond, bounded by the James River to the south and Chickahominy River to the east. Charles City is the county seat.

51037.description: Charlotte County is bounded on the southwest by the Roanoke River, locally known as the "Staunton River". Its county seat is the town of Charlotte Court House.

51041.description: Chesterfield County lies south of Richmond, with borders largely defined by the James and Appomattox rivers. Its landscape spans the hillier Piedmont and flatter coastal plain, and Chesterfield Court House is the county seat.

51043.description: Clarke County borders West Virginia along Virginia’s northern border and forms part of the Washington metropolitan area. Berryville is the county seat.

51045.description: Craig County is a rural, mountainous county in western Virginia with more than 112,000 acres of national forest. New Castle is its county seat and only town.

51047.description: The Rappahannock River defines Culpeper County’s northeastern border, while the Rapidan River marks its southern border. Culpeper is the county seat.

51049.description: Cumberland County is a rural county near Virginia’s geographic center. The small town of Cumberland is its county seat, and the population was 9,675 in 2020.

51051.description: Dickenson County lies on the mountainous Appalachian Plateau near Virginia’s far western point, bordering Kentucky. Clintwood is its county seat, and its 2020 population was 14,124.

51053.description: Dinwiddie County is largely rural and lies southwest of the independent city of Petersburg. Dinwiddie is its county seat, and its 2020 population was 27,947.

51057.description: Essex County lies on Virginia’s Middle Peninsula, bordered by the Rappahannock River to the north. Tappahannock is its county seat.

51059.description: Fairfax County is bounded on the north and southeast by the Potomac River. The county seat is Fairfax; however, because it is an independent city under Virginia law, the city of Fairfax is not part of the county.

51061.description: Fauquier County lies on Virginia’s Piedmont plateau and is part of the Washington metropolitan area. Warrenton is its county seat, and some areas have experienced exurban development from Washington.

51063.description: Floyd County occupies a high plateau in the Blue Ridge Mountains of southwestern Virginia. Floyd is its county seat, and the county is part of the Blacksburg–Christiansburg metropolitan area.

51065.description: Fluvanna County lies in Virginia’s Piedmont region and is part of the Charlottesville metropolitan area. Palmyra is its county seat, while Lake Monticello is its most populous community.

51067.description: Franklin County lies in the Blue Ridge foothills, with the Roanoke River forming its northeastern boundary with Bedford County. Rocky Mount is its seat of government, and the county is part of the Roanoke metropolitan area.

51069.description: Frederick County is Virginia’s northernmost county and is included in the Winchester metropolitan area. Its county seat is the independent city of Winchester.

51071.description: Giles County borders West Virginia and contains Mountain Lake, one of Virginia’s two natural freshwater lakes. Pearisburg is its county seat.

51073.description: Gloucester Courthouse is the county seat of Gloucester County, Virginia. Water covers 24.4 percent of the county’s area, and its 2020 population was 38,711.

51075.description: Goochland County lies in Virginia’s Piedmont, with the James River forming its southern border. Goochland is the county seat, and the county is part of the Greater Richmond Region.

51077.description: Grayson County in southwestern Virginia contains Mount Rogers, the state’s highest peak. Independence is its county seat, and its 2020 population was 15,333.

51079.description: Greene County is part of the Charlottesville metropolitan area, with Stanardsville as its county seat. Shenandoah National Park and Virginia’s foothills attract visitors to the county.

51081.description: The Meherrin River forms Greensville County’s boundary with Southampton County. The independent city of Emporia is its county seat.

51083.description: Halifax is the county seat of Halifax County, Virginia. The county had 34,022 residents in 2020, and water covers about 1.4 percent of its total area.

51085.description: Hanover County forms part of the Greater Richmond Region, with Hanover as its county seat. The 2020 census counted 109,979 residents.

51087.description: Henrico County is part of the Greater Richmond Region and has no incorporated communities. Its population was 334,000 in the 2020 census.

51089.description: Henry County’s offices and courthouse are in Collinsville, although Martinsville is its traditional county seat. The county is part of the Martinsville micropolitan area and the Appalachian Regional Commission’s service region.

51091.description: Highland County lies between the Allegheny Mountains along its western border and Shenandoah Mountain along its eastern border. Monterey is the county seat.

51093.description: Isle of Wight County is bounded by the James River on the north and the Blackwater River to the south. Its county seat is Isle of Wight, an unincorporated community.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Isle of Wight County, Virginia

51095.description: James City County straddles the James and York river watersheds on the Virginia Peninsula. Its county seat is the adjacent independent city of Williamsburg, which is politically separate from the county.

51097.description: King and Queen County lies on Virginia’s Middle Peninsula and has no incorporated towns or cities. King and Queen Court House is the county seat, and the county had 6,608 residents in 2020.

sources.title: Wikipedia: King and Queen County, Virginia

51099.description: King George County occupies the Northern Neck between the Potomac River to the north and Rappahannock River to the south. King George is its county seat.

51101.description: The Mattaponi and Pamunkey rivers bound King William County and meet at West Point to form the York River. King William is its county seat.

51103.description: Lancaster County lies on the Northern Neck near the mouth of the Rappahannock River. Lancaster is its county seat, and water covers 42.4 percent of the county’s area.

51105.description: The Powell River flows through Lee County, Virginia’s westernmost county. Jonesville is its county seat, and its 2020 population was 22,173.

51107.description: The Bull Run Mountains and Catoctin Mountain bisect Loudoun County. Leesburg is the county seat.

51109.description: Louisa is the county seat of Louisa County. The 2020 census counted 37,596 residents.

51111.description: Lunenburg is the county seat of Lunenburg County. The 2020 census counted 11,936 residents.

51113.description: Western Madison County includes part of Shenandoah National Park, including Hawksbill Mountain and Old Rag Mountain. Madison is the county seat.

51115.description: Mathews County has a prominent position on Chesapeake Bay and extensive waterfront. Mathews is its county seat.

51117.description: Boydton is the county seat of Mecklenburg County, Virginia. The 2020 census counted 30,319 residents.

51119.description: Middlesex County is located at the eastern end of Virginia's Middle Peninsula region. Its county seat is Saluda.

51121.description: Western Montgomery County lies in the New River watershed. Christiansburg is the county seat, while Blacksburg is the largest town.

51125.description: The Blue Ridge Mountains form Nelson County’s northwestern boundary, while the James River marks its southeastern boundary. Lovingston is the county seat.

51127.description: The Pamunkey River defines New Kent County’s northeastern border, and the Chickahominy River defines its southwestern border. New Kent is its county seat.

51131.description: Eastville is the county seat of Northampton County, Virginia. Its population was 12,282 in the 2020 census.

51133.description: Northumberland County is located between the Rappahannock River to the south and Potomac River to the north. Its county seat is Heathsville.

51135.description: Nottoway is the county seat of Nottoway County, Virginia. The 2020 census counted 15,642 residents.

51137.description: Orange County’s rolling hills generally rise westward toward the Blue Ridge Mountains. Orange is the county seat.

51139.description: Luray is the county seat of Page County, Virginia. The 2020 census counted 23,709 residents.

51141.description: About one third of Patrick County lies in the rolling Piedmont, with the remainder in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Stuart is its county seat.

51143.description: The Roanoke River bounds Pittsylvania County to the north, the Banister crosses its center, and the Dan drains its south. Chatham is the county seat.

51145.description: Powhatan County is bordered on the north by the James River and on the south by the Appomattox River. Its county seat is Powhatan.

51147.description: Most of Prince Edward County’s streams drain into the Appomattox River, while southeastern streams flow toward the Nottoway River. Farmville is the county seat.

51149.description: Prince George is the county seat of Prince George County, Virginia. The county had 43,010 residents in 2020.

51153.description: Prince William stretches from the Potomac River’s coastal plain to the Bull Run Mountains, with suburban development and rural landscapes. Its 482,204 residents in the 2020 Census were counted separately from the independent cities of Manassas and Manassas Park.

sources.title: Prince William Conservation Alliance: County geography

51155.description: Pulaski County contains Claytor Lake State Park on a reservoir created on the New River for a hydroelectric project. Pulaski is its county seat.

51157.description: The Rappahannock River forms Rappahannock County’s northeastern boundary with Fauquier County. Washington is its county seat and only incorporated town.

51159.description: Warsaw is the county seat of Richmond County. Richmond County is a county located on the Northern Neck in the U.S. state of Virginia.

51161.description: Roanoke County’s county seat is Salem, but the county administrative offices are located in the census-designated place of Cave Spring. The 2020 census counted 96,929 residents.

51163.description: Rockbridge County lies in the Shenandoah Valley and completely surrounds the independent cities of Lexington and Buena Vista. Lexington is its county seat.

51165.description: Rockingham County spans the Shenandoah Valley between the Allegheny and Blue Ridge mountains and is divided by Massanutten Mountain. Its county seat is the independent city of Harrisonburg.

51167.description: Russell County has the fourth highest peak in Virginia, Beartown Mountain. Its county seat is Lebanon.

51169.description: Gate City is the county seat of Scott County. The 2020 census counted 21,576 residents.

51171.description: Shenandoah County includes Fort Valley and the western slopes of Massanutten Mountain. Woodstock is its county seat.

51173.description: Marion is the county seat of Smyth County. The 2020 census counted 29,800 residents.

51175.description: Southampton County is bounded by the Blackwater River on the east and the Meherrin River on the west. Its county seat is Courtland.

51177.description: Spotsylvania Courthouse is the county seat of Spotsylvania County. The 2020 census counted 140,032 residents.

51179.description: Stafford County lies across the Rappahannock River from Fredericksburg and is part of the Washington metropolitan area. Stafford is its county seat.

51181.description: Surry County is a county in the southeastern part of the Commonwealth of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 6,561 residents.

51183.description: Sussex is the county seat of Sussex County. The 2020 census counted 10,829 residents.

51185.description: Tazewell County spans parts of the Ridge-and-Valley Appalachians and Cumberland Plateau. Tazewell is the county seat.

51187.description: Front Royal is the county seat of Warren County. The 2020 census counted 40,727 residents.

51191.description: Abingdon is the county seat of Washington County. The 2020 census counted 53,935 residents.

51193.description: Montross is the county seat of Westmoreland County. Westmoreland County is located in the Northern Neck of the Commonwealth of Virginia.

51195.description: Wise County lies in the Appalachians and includes High Knob and Powell Valley. Wise is its county seat.

51197.description: Wythe County lies mainly on an elevated plateau between Iron Mountain and Walker’s Mountain. Wytheville is its county seat.

51199.description: Yorktown is the county seat of York County, Virginia. An industrial area along the York River includes a power plant and a petroleum terminal at a former oil refinery site.

51510.description: Alexandria is an independent city in the U.S. state of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 159,467 residents.

51520.description: Bristol is an independent city in Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 17,219 residents.

51530.description: Buena Vista is an independent city located in the Blue Ridge Mountains region of Virginia in the United States. The 2020 census counted 6,641 residents.

51540.description: Charlottesville is an independent city in Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 46,553 residents.

51550.description: Chesapeake is an independent city in Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 249,422 residents.

51570.description: Colonial Heights is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 18,170 residents.

51580.description: Covington is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 5,737 residents.

51590.description: Danville is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia in the United States. The 2020 census counted 42,590 residents.

51595.description: Emporia is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia in the United States. The 2020 census counted 5,766 residents.

51600.description: Fairfax is an independent city in Virginia and the county seat of Fairfax County, Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 24,146 residents.

51610.description: Falls Church is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 14,658 residents.

51620.description: Franklin is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 8,180 residents.

51630.description: Fredericksburg is an independent city in Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 27,982 residents.

51640.description: Galax is an independent city in the southwestern part of the Commonwealth of Virginia, in the United States. The 2020 census counted 6,720 residents.

51650.description: Hampton is an independent city in Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 137,148 residents.

51660.description: Harrisonburg is an independent city in the Shenandoah Valley region of the Commonwealth of Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 51,814 residents.

51670.description: Hopewell is an independent city surrounded by Prince George County and the Appomattox River in the Commonwealth of Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 23,033 residents.

51678.description: Lexington is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 7,320 residents.

51680.description: Lynchburg is an independent city in Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 79,009 residents.

51683.description: Manassas is a compact independent city in Northern Virginia, with 42,772 residents in just under 10 square miles at the 2020 Census. Its population is counted separately from neighboring Prince William County.

51685.description: Manassas Park is an independent city in the U.S. state of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 17,219 residents.

51690.description: Martinsville is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia in the United States. The 2020 census counted 13,485 residents.

51700.description: Newport News is an independent city in southeastern Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 186,247 residents.

51710.description: Norfolk is an independent city in the U.S. commonwealth of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 238,005 residents.

51720.description: Norton is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia, located in the far western tip of the state and surrounded by Wise County, Virginia. The 2020 census counted 3,687 residents.

51730.description: Petersburg is an independent city in the U.S. state of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 33,458 residents.

51735.description: Poquoson is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 12,460 residents.

51740.description: Portsmouth is an independent city in southeastern Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 97,915 residents.

51750.description: Radford is an independent city in the U.S. state of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 16,070 residents.

51760.description: Richmond is Virginia’s capital and an independent city at the James River’s fall line. The 2020 census counted 226,610 residents.

51770.description: Roanoke is an independent city in Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 100,011 residents.

51775.description: Salem is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 25,346 residents.

51790.description: Staunton is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 25,750 residents.

51800.description: Suffolk is an independent city in Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 94,324 residents.

51810.description: Virginia Beach lies on the Atlantic Ocean at the mouth of Chesapeake Bay in southeastern Virginia. It had 459,470 residents in 2020 and is a principal city of the Hampton Roads metropolitan area.

51820.description: Waynesboro is an independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 22,196 residents.

51830.description: Williamsburg is an independent city in the U.S. state of Virginia. The 2020 census counted 15,425 residents.

51840.description: Winchester is the northernmost independent city in the Commonwealth of Virginia, United States. The 2020 census counted 28,120 residents.

53001.description: Adams County’s county seat is Ritzville, and its largest city is Othello. The 2020 census counted 20,613 residents.

53003.description: Asotin County is part of the Palouse, a wide and rolling prairie-like region of the middle Columbia basin. The county seat is at Asotin, and its largest city is Clarkston.

53005.description: Benton County lies in south-central Washington, with Prosser as its county seat and Kennewick as its most populous city. Rattlesnake Mountain is its highest point.

53007.description: Wenatchee is the county seat and largest city of Chelan County, Washington’s third-largest county by area. The county had 79,074 residents in 2020.

53009.description: Clallam County contains Cape Alava, the westernmost point in the contiguous United States. Port Angeles is the county seat and largest city.

53011.description: Clark County is surrounded on two sides by the Columbia River and on the north by the North Fork of the Lewis River. Its county seat and largest city is Vancouver.

53013.description: Columbia County is part of the Palouse, a wide and rolling prairie-like region of the middle Columbia basin. The county seat and largest city is Dayton.

53015.description: Cowlitz County lies in southwestern Washington beside the Cascade Mountains, in the Puget Sound–Willamette Depression. Kelso is its county seat, and Longview is its largest city.

53017.description: Douglas County’s county seat is Waterville, while its largest settlement is East Wenatchee. The 2020 census counted 42,938 residents.

53019.description: The rugged Kettle River Range covers most of Ferry County, reaching from the Canadian border toward the Columbia River and Roosevelt Lake. Republic is its county seat and largest city.

53021.description: Franklin County’s county seat and largest city is Pasco. The 2020 census counted 96,749 residents.

53023.description: Garfield County is part of the Palouse, a wide and rolling prairie-like region of the middle Columbia basin. The county seat and only city is Pomeroy.

53025.description: Grant County lies in the Cascade Mountains’ rain shadow and has hot summers and cold winters. Ephrata is its county seat, while Moses Lake is its largest city.

53027.description: Grays Harbor County has flat terrain within the Chehalis River watershed’s drainage to the Pacific Ocean. Montesano is its county seat, and Aberdeen is its largest city.

53029.description: Island County’s county seat is Coupeville, while its largest city is Oak Harbor. The 2020 census counted 86,857 residents.

53031.description: Jefferson County extends from eastern inland waterways across the Olympic Mountains to the Pacific coast. Port Townsend is its county seat and only incorporated city, and no road entirely within the county connects its eastern and western parts.

53033.description: King County includes Vashon and Maury islands in Puget Sound and contains hundreds of lakes. Seattle is its county seat and Washington’s most populous city.

53035.description: Kitsap County occupies most of the Kitsap Peninsula and includes Bainbridge and Blake islands. Port Orchard is its county seat, and Bremerton is its largest city.

53037.description: Ellensburg is the county seat and largest city of Kittitas County, whose highest point is Mount Daniel. The county had 44,337 residents in 2020.

53039.description: Klickitat County’s county seat and largest city is Goldendale. The 2020 census counted 22,735 residents.

53041.description: Lewis County lies along the Interstate 5 corridor in Washington. Chehalis is the county seat, and Centralia is its largest city.

53043.description: Lincoln County lies on the Channeled Scablands of the Big Bend Plateau, where glacial rivers and streams eroded channels into bedrock. Davenport is the county seat and largest city.

53045.description: Mason County’s county seat and only incorporated city is Shelton. The 2020 census counted 65,726 residents.

53047.description: Okanogan County is Washington’s largest county by area, with agricultural valleys, forests and mountains. Agriculture and forestry are major parts of its economy, and Okanogan is its county seat.

53049.description: Pacific County’s county seat is South Bend, and its largest city is Raymond. The 2020 census counted 23,365 residents.

53051.description: Pend Oreille County’s county seat and largest city is Newport. The 2020 census counted 13,401 residents.

53053.description: Pierce County contains Mount Rainier, Washington’s highest natural point. Tacoma is its county seat and largest city.

53055.description: San Juan County comprises more than 400 islands and rocks in the Salish Sea, with rugged shorelines and several mountains. Friday Harbor, on San Juan Island, is its county seat and only incorporated town.

53057.description: Skagit County’s broad, fertile river valley supports cultivation of tulips, blueberries and strawberries. Mount Vernon is the county seat and largest city.

53059.description: Forests cover 90 percent of Skamania County, with 80 percent of the county in Gifford Pinchot National Forest. Stevenson is the county seat and largest incorporated city.

53061.description: Snohomish County ranges from western plains and rolling hills to the Cascade Range in the east. Everett is its county seat and largest city.

53063.description: Spokane County lies between the Columbia Basin’s steppe plains and the timbered foothills of the Rocky Mountains. Spokane is its county seat and largest city.

53065.description: Stevens County lies along the Canadian border in Washington, with Colville as its county seat and largest city. Its 2020 population was 46,445.

53067.description: Thurston County’s county seat is Olympia, the state capital. The 2020 census counted 294,793 residents.

53069.description: Wahkiakum County’s county seat and only incorporated town is Cathlamet. The 2020 census counted 4,422 residents.

53071.description: Walla Walla County’s county seat and most populous city is Walla Walla. The 2020 census counted 62,584 residents.

53073.description: Whatcom County ranges from the Fraser Lowland in the west to the Cascade Range, including Mount Baker. Bellingham is its county seat and largest population center.

53075.description: Whitman County is part of the Palouse, a wide and rolling prairie-like region of the middle Columbia basin. The county seat is Colfax, and its largest city is Pullman.

53077.description: Yakima Valley agriculture depends on extensive irrigation from the Yakima Project, with reservoirs and mountain snowpack supporting the basin’s water supply. Yakima is the county seat and most populous city of Yakima County.

sources.title: Washington Ecology: Yakima Basin Integrated Plan

54001.description: Barbour County lies on the Allegheny Plateau at the western edge of the Allegheny Mountains. The Tygart Valley River drains most of the county, and Philippi is its county seat.

54003.description: Berkeley County lies in the Shenandoah Valley in West Virginia’s eastern panhandle. Martinsburg is the county seat, and the county is part of the Hagerstown–Martinsburg metropolitan area.

54005.description: Boone County’s terrain consists of low wooded mountains, carved with drainages. Its county seat is Madison.

54007.description: Sutton is the county seat of Braxton County in central West Virginia. The county had 12,447 residents in 2020.

54009.description: Brooke County lies in West Virginia’s Northern Panhandle and is the state’s second-smallest county by area. Wellsburg is its county seat.

54011.description: Huntington is the county seat of Cabell County. The 2020 census counted 94,350 residents.

54013.description: Grantsville is the county seat of Calhoun County. The 2020 census counted 6,229 residents.

54015.description: Clay County has Interstate 79 access at Big Otter and Wallback. Clay is its county seat, and the county had 8,051 residents in 2020.

54017.description: West Union is the county seat of Doddridge County, part of the Clarksburg micropolitan area. The county had 7,808 residents in 2020.

54019.description: Fayette County contains Plum Orchard Lake, a reservoir southwest of Oak Hill. Fayetteville is its county seat, and the county is part of the Beckley metropolitan area.

54021.description: Glenville is the county seat of Gilmer County. The 2020 census counted 7,408 residents.

54023.description: Petersburg is the county seat of Grant County. The 2020 census counted 10,976 residents.

54025.description: Much of northern and western Greenbrier County consists of national forest, coal land or privately owned forest. Lewisburg is its county seat.

54027.description: Hampshire County’s county seat is Romney, West Virginia's oldest town. The 2020 census counted 23,093 residents.

54029.description: Hancock County’s county seat is New Cumberland and its largest city is Weirton. The 2020 census counted 29,095 residents.

54031.description: Hardy County contains the South Branch Potomac River valley, flanked by high, heavily wooded mountains. Moorefield is the county seat, and agriculture and livestock raising are important to the valley.

54033.description: Harrison County’s low, largely wooded hills slope toward the West Fork River valley. Clarksburg is its county seat.

54035.description: The Ohio River forms part of Jackson County’s western border, while Sandy and Mill creeks cross its northern and central areas. Ripley is the county seat, and Ravenswood is its largest municipality.

54037.description: Jefferson County lies in the Shenandoah Valley and includes the Blue Ridge Mountains and Shenandoah River. Charles Town is the county seat.

54039.description: Kanawha County’s county seat is Charleston, which is also the state capital and most populous city. The 2020 census counted 180,745 residents.

54041.description: Weston is the county seat of Lewis County. The 2020 census counted 17,033 residents.

54043.description: Hamlin is the county seat of Lincoln County, part of the Huntington–Ashland metropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 20,463 residents.

54045.description: Logan County forms the Logan micropolitan area, with Logan as its county seat. The 2020 census counted 32,567 residents.

54047.description: McDowell County lies in the Cumberland Mountains at West Virginia’s southernmost end. Welch is its county seat and largest city.

54049.description: Fairmont is the county seat of Marion County, which forms the Fairmont micropolitan area. Its population was 56,205 in 2020.

54051.description: Marshall County forms the base of West Virginia’s Northern Panhandle and contains Blairs Ridge. Moundsville is its county seat.

54053.description: Mason County’s county seat and largest city is Point Pleasant. The 2020 census counted 25,453 residents.

54055.description: Mercer County lies along West Virginia’s southeastern border. Princeton is its county seat, and the 2020 census counted 59,664 residents.

54057.description: Keyser is the county seat of Mineral County, part of the Cumberland metropolitan area. The county had 26,938 residents in 2020.

54059.description: Mingo County’s county seat and largest city is Williamson. The 2020 census counted 23,568 residents.

54061.description: Morgantown is the county seat of Monongalia County. The 2020 census counted 105,822 residents.

54063.description: Monroe County has mountainous, tree-covered terrain, with agriculture on its sufficiently level land. Union is its county seat, and the New River follows a short part of its southwestern border.

54065.description: Berkeley Springs is the county seat of Morgan County. The 2020 census counted 17,063 residents.

54067.description: Summersville is the county seat of Nicholas County in central West Virginia. The county had 24,604 residents in 2020.

54069.description: Ohio County lies in West Virginia’s Northern Panhandle and is drained by Wheeling Creek and other small creeks. Wheeling is its county seat, and the county forms part of the Wheeling metropolitan area.

54071.description: Franklin is the county seat of Pendleton County. The 2020 census counted 6,143 residents.

54073.description: St. Marys is the county seat of Pleasants County, West Virginia. The county had 7,653 residents in 2020.

54075.description: Pocahontas County is West Virginia’s third-largest county by area, with its highest point at Thorny Flat on Cheat Mountain. Marlinton is the county seat.

54077.description: Kingwood is the county seat of Preston County. The 2020 census counted 34,216 residents.

54079.description: The Kanawha River flows through wooded hills in central Putnam County. Winfield is the county seat, while Hurricane is its largest incorporated city.

54081.description: Wooded hills cover Raleigh County, with the New River flowing along its eastern border. Beckley is its county seat.

54083.description: Randolph County is West Virginia’s largest county by area and forms the Elkins micropolitan area. Elkins is its county seat, and the county had 27,932 residents in 2020.

54085.description: Harrisville is the county seat of Ritchie County. The 2020 census counted 8,444 residents.

54087.description: Spencer is the county seat of Roane County. The 2020 census counted 14,028 residents.

54089.description: Hinton is the county seat of Summers County, West Virginia. Its population was 11,959 in the 2020 census.

54091.description: Grafton is the county seat of Taylor County, part of the Clarksburg micropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 16,705 residents.

54093.description: Parsons is the county seat of Tucker County. The 2020 census counted 6,762 residents.

54095.description: Middlebourne is the county seat of Tyler County. The 2020 census counted 8,313 residents.

54097.description: Upshur County lies within the United States National Radio Quiet Zone. Buckhannon is its county seat, and the county had 23,816 residents in 2020.

54099.description: Wayne County is West Virginia’s westernmost county and forms part of the Huntington–Ashland metropolitan area. Wayne is its county seat.

54101.description: Webster Springs is the county seat of Webster County. The 2020 census counted 8,378 residents.

54103.description: New Martinsville is the county seat of Wetzel County. The 2020 census counted 14,442 residents.

54105.description: Elizabeth is the county seat of Wirt County, West Virginia. Its population of 5,194 in 2020 made it the state’s least populous county.

54107.description: The Ohio River forms Wood County’s northern and western boundary, receiving the Little Kanawha River at Parkersburg. Parkersburg is the county seat.

54109.description: Wyoming County has mountainous terrain drained by branches of the Sandy and Guyandotte rivers. Pineville is its county seat.

55001.description: Adams County had 20,654 residents in the 2020 census, with Friendship as its county seat. The county is classified by the U.S. Department of Agriculture as a high-recreation retirement destination.

55003.description: Ashland County includes most of the Apostle Islands in Lake Superior, with water accounting for 54% of its total area. Ashland is the county seat, and the county partly overlaps the Bad River Band's reservation.

55005.description: Barron County had 46,711 residents in the 2020 census, with Barron as its county seat.

55007.description: Bayfield County is Wisconsin's second-largest county by land area, with Washburn as its county seat. The Red Cliff Band of Lake Superior Chippewa has a reservation in the county and is its largest employer.

55009.description: Brown County is part of the Green Bay metropolitan area, with Green Bay as its county seat. Its 2020 census population of 268,740 made it Wisconsin's fourth-most populous county.

55011.description: Buffalo County had 13,317 residents in the 2020 census, with Alma as its county seat. The U.S. Department of Agriculture classifies it as a high-farming concentration county, meaning at least 20% of its earnings came from agriculture.

55013.description: Burnett County includes Saginaw Lake, south of the Namekagon River, and has its county seat at Siren. The St. Croix Chippewa Indians of Wisconsin have reservation lands in the county and are its largest employer.

55015.description: Calumet County's western boundary lies largely in Lake Winnebago, with the Niagara Escarpment running north–south farther east. Dairy farming is prominent, and Chilton is the county seat.

55017.description: The Chippewa River bends around Flambeau Ridge, passes through Holcombe Flowage and Lake Wissota, and exits Chippewa County between Chippewa Falls and Eau Claire. Chippewa Falls is the county seat, and the county belongs to the Eau Claire metropolitan area.

55019.description: Clark County had 34,659 residents in the 2020 census, with Neillsville as its county seat. Rolling farmland lies on the shoulders of North Bluff north of Willard.

55021.description: Columbia County is part of the Madison metropolitan area, with Portage as its county seat and largest city. Its highest point lies in the Baraboo Range near Durward's Glen, at 1,480 feet above sea level.

55023.description: Crawford County lies in southwestern Wisconsin, with the Mississippi River on its western border and the Wisconsin River on its southern edge. The Kickapoo River crosses the county, whose river landscapes include limestone cliffs, bluffs, prairies and sandy islands; Prairie du Chien is the county seat.

55025.description: Dane County forms the core of the Madison metropolitan area, with Madison serving as both county seat and Wisconsin's capital. New healthcare and technology jobs have driven the county's recent growth.

55027.description: Dodge County includes Beaver Dam Lake and Fox Lake, with Juneau as its county seat. It comprises the Beaver Dam micropolitan area, which belongs to the broader Milwaukee–Racine–Waukesha combined statistical area.

55029.description: Door County covers most of the Door Peninsula, with water accounting for 80% of its total area. Sturgeon Bay is its county seat and largest city, and tourism is a major contributor to the county's economy.

55031.description: Douglas County lies in Wisconsin's northwestern corner, with Superior as its county seat, and belongs to the Duluth metropolitan area. Part of the Fond du Lac Indian Reservation lies within the county.

55033.description: Dunn County comprises the Menomonie micropolitan area, with Menomonie as its county seat. It had 45,440 residents in the 2020 census and is part of the broader Eau Claire–Menomonie combined statistical area.

55035.description: Eau Claire County had 105,710 residents in the 2020 census, with Eau Claire as its county seat. It belongs to the Eau Claire metropolitan area and the broader Eau Claire–Menomonie combined statistical area.

55037.description: Florence County had 4,558 residents in the 2020 census, making it Wisconsin's second-least populous county. Its county seat is Florence, and it is part of the Iron Mountain, Michigan–Wisconsin micropolitan area.

55039.description: Fond du Lac County lies at the southern shore of Lake Winnebago, with Fond du Lac as its county seat. It comprises the Fond du Lac metropolitan area, and the Holyland region lies in its northeastern portion.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Fond du Lac County, Wisconsin

55041.description: Forest County includes Sugarbush Hill, Wisconsin's second-highest elevation, with Crandon as its county seat. The Forest County Potawatomi Community and Sokaogon Chippewa Community have reservations in the county.

55043.description: Grant County occupies Wisconsin's southwestern corner in the tri-state area adjoining Illinois and Iowa. Lancaster is its county seat, Platteville is its largest city, and the county comprises the Platteville micropolitan area.

55045.description: Green County had 37,093 residents in the 2020 census, with Monroe as its county seat. It is included in the Madison metropolitan area.

55047.description: Green Lake County is Wisconsin's third-smallest county by total area, with Green Lake as its county seat. The state's center of population was located near Markesan in the county in 2020.

55049.description: Iowa County contains the headwaters of the Pecatonica River and rises to 1,716 feet at West Blue Mound. Dodgeville is its county seat and largest city, and the county is part of the Madison metropolitan area.

55051.description: Iron County lies within the Gogebic Range and overlaps small parts of the Bad River and Lac du Flambeau Indian reservations. Its county seat is Hurley, and its 2020 census population was 6,137.

55053.description: Jackson County had 21,145 residents in the 2020 census, with Black River Falls as its county seat. Its largest employer is the Ho-Chunk Nation.

55055.description: Jefferson County comprises the Watertown–Fort Atkinson micropolitan area, within the broader Milwaukee–Racine–Waukesha combined statistical area. Its county seat is Jefferson, and its 2020 census population was 84,900.

55057.description: Juneau County had 26,718 residents in the 2020 census, with Mauston as its county seat.

55059.description: Kenosha County occupies Wisconsin's southeastern corner on Lake Michigan's southwestern shore, with Kenosha as its county seat and largest city. It belongs to the broader Chicago–Naperville combined statistical area and has a direct Metra rail link to Chicago.

55061.description: Northern Kewaunee County lies on the Door Peninsula between Green Bay and Lake Michigan, and the northern Kettle Moraine extends into the county. With Kewaunee as its county seat, the county is classified by the U.S. Department of Agriculture as having concentrations in both farming and manufacturing.

55063.description: La Crosse County lies on Wisconsin's western border and is part of the La Crosse–Onalaska, Wisconsin–Minnesota metropolitan area. Its county seat is La Crosse, and its 2020 census population was 120,784.

55065.description: Lafayette County had 16,611 residents in the 2020 census, with Darlington as its county seat. The U.S. Department of Agriculture classifies it as a high-farming concentration county, meaning at least 20% of its earnings came from agriculture.

55067.description: Langlade County's highest point is at the foot of Basswood Lookout Tower, west of Summit Lake, at 1,857 feet. Its county seat is Antigo, and its 2020 census population was 19,491.

55069.description: Lincoln County comprises the Merrill micropolitan area, within the broader Wausau–Stevens Point–Wisconsin Rapids combined statistical area. Its county seat is Merrill, and its 2020 census population was 28,415.

55071.description: Manitowoc County comprises the Manitowoc micropolitan area, with Manitowoc as its county seat. It had 81,359 residents in the 2020 census, and water accounts for 61% of its total area.

55073.description: Marathon County is Wisconsin's largest county by land area, with Wausau as its county seat. It comprises the Wausau metropolitan area and contains the intersection of 45° north latitude and 90° west longitude near Rietbrock.

55075.description: Marinette County is Wisconsin's third-largest county by land area, and part of it borders Lake Michigan. Marinette is its county seat, and the county belongs to the Marinette, Wisconsin–Michigan micropolitan area.

55077.description: Marquette County includes the Mecan River, Buffalo Lake and Puckaway Lake, with its highest point in a rocky area called Mt. Shaw. Montello is the county seat.

55078.description: Menominee County is essentially coterminous with the Menominee Indian Reservation, with its county seat at Keshena. Its 2020 census population of 4,255 made it Wisconsin's least populous county.

55079.description: Milwaukee County is Wisconsin's most populous and most densely populated county, with Milwaukee as its county seat. The Milwaukee, Menomonee, Kinnickinnic and Root rivers drain its undulating landscape.

55081.description: Monroe County had 46,274 residents in the 2020 census, with Sparta as its county seat. Tomah has a Walmart distribution center and a Toro plant.

55083.description: Oconto County is part of the Green Bay metropolitan area and the broader Green Bay–Shawano combined statistical area. Its county seat is Oconto, and its 2020 census population was 38,965.

55085.description: Oneida County's lakes draw visitors, particularly to Minocqua, while Rhinelander serves as the county seat. Water covers 10% of the county's total area.

55087.description: Outagamie County lies in northeastern Wisconsin's Fox Cities region, with Appleton as its county seat. It belongs to the Appleton metropolitan area and had 190,705 residents in the 2020 census.

55089.description: Ozaukee County is Wisconsin's second-smallest county by land area, with jurisdiction extending over a much larger water area, mostly in Lake Michigan. Port Washington is its county seat, and Lion's Den Gorge Nature Preserve protects lakeshore bluffs and wetlands.

55091.description: Pepin County is Wisconsin's smallest county by land area, with Durand as its county seat. Its 2020 census population of 7,318 made it the state's fourth-least populous county.

55093.description: Pierce County belongs to the Minneapolis–St. Paul–Bloomington, Minnesota–Wisconsin metropolitan area. Its county seat is Ellsworth, and its 2020 census population was 42,212.

55095.description: Polk County is Wisconsin's westernmost county, with Balsam Lake as its county seat. Its population was 44,977 in the 2020 census.

55097.description: Portage County comprises the Stevens Point micropolitan area, with Stevens Point as its county seat. It had 70,377 residents in the 2020 census and belongs to the broader Wausau–Stevens Point–Wisconsin Rapids combined statistical area.

55099.description: Price County contains Timms Hill, Wisconsin's highest natural point. Its county seat is Phillips, and its 2020 census population was 14,054.

55101.description: Racine County lies in southeastern Wisconsin and comprises the Racine metropolitan area, within the broader Milwaukee–Racine–Waukesha combined statistical area. Racine is its county seat, and its 2020 census population was 197,727.

55103.description: Richland County had 17,304 residents in the 2020 census, with Richland Center as its county seat.

55105.description: Rock County comprises the Janesville–Beloit metropolitan area, with Janesville as its county seat. Cook Memorial Arboretum, northwest of Janesville, provides birding and nature trails.

55107.description: The Chippewa and Flambeau rivers and their tributaries flow through Rusk County, whose landscapes include corn, soybean and dairy farms, lakes with vacation homes, and Blue Hills hiking trails. Ladysmith is the county seat.

55109.description: St. Croix County belongs to the Minneapolis–St. Paul–Bloomington metropolitan area, with Hudson as its county seat. Its population reached 93,536 in the 2020 census after it was Wisconsin's fastest-growing county from 2000 to 2010.

55111.description: Sauk County's highest point, Sauk Point, lies in the Baraboo bluffs, with Baraboo serving as county seat and largest city. Tourism is a major economic contributor, and the Ho-Chunk Nation is the county's largest employer.

55113.description: Sawyer County is largely rural, with lakes and sandy loam soils common in its northwestern half and more swamps in the southeast. Hayward is the county seat, the county partly overlaps the Lac Courte Oreilles reservation, and its economy includes government services and tourism.

55115.description: Shawano County, Wisconsin, had 40,881 residents at the 2020 census, and its county seat is Shawano. It forms the Shawano micropolitan area, within the Green Bay–Shawano combined statistical area.

55117.description: Sheboygan County, Wisconsin, has Sheboygan as its county seat and comprises the Sheboygan metropolitan area. Part of the Holyland region lies in the county's northwest.

55119.description: Taylor County, Wisconsin, is mostly rural, lying where corn and dairy farms to the south give way to forest and swamp to the north. Medford is its county seat, and the county spans three river systems that ultimately drain to the Mississippi.

55121.description: Trempealeau County, Wisconsin, is part of the Driftless Zone. Its county seat is Whitehall, and its population was 30,760 at the 2020 census.

55123.description: Vernon County, Wisconsin, has Viroqua as its county seat and had 30,714 residents at the 2020 census. It is home to the headquarters of Organic Valley, a cooperative of family farmers.

55125.description: Vilas County, Wisconsin, contains 1,318 lakes and extensive national, state, and county forest lands, with Eagle River as its county seat. Tourism centers on its lakes and forests, including hunting, sport fishing, ice fishing, and snowmobiling.

55127.description: Walworth County, Wisconsin, has Elkhorn as its county seat and includes the University of Wisconsin–Whitewater. Tourism is a major part of its economy, with destinations including Lake Geneva, Alpine Valley Resort, and Alpine Valley Music Theatre.

55129.description: Washburn County, Wisconsin, had 16,623 residents at the 2020 census, and its county seat is Shell Lake. The U.S. Department of Agriculture classifies it as a high-recreation retirement destination.

55131.description: Washington County, Wisconsin, is part of the Milwaukee metropolitan area, with West Bend as its county seat. It had 136,761 residents at the 2020 census and is Wisconsin's fifth-smallest county by total area.

55133.description: Waukesha County lies west of Milwaukee and is part of the Milwaukee metropolitan area. The Fox River runs through the county, whose county seat and largest city is Waukesha.

55135.description: Waupaca County, Wisconsin, has Waupaca as its county seat and includes the 22 lakes of the Waupaca Chain O' Lakes. These mostly spring-fed lakes are connected by the Crystal River outlet.

55137.description: Waushara County lies in central Wisconsin, about 80 miles north of Madison. Its county seat is Wautoma, and its population was 24,520 at the 2020 census.

55139.description: Winnebago County, Wisconsin, has Oshkosh as its county seat and comprises the Oshkosh–Neenah metropolitan area. Water accounts for about one-quarter of the county's total area.

55141.description: Wood County, Wisconsin, spans the Northern Highlands and Central Plain, with Wisconsin Rapids as its county seat. Its northern cropland supports corn, soybeans, hay, and dairy, while its flat, marshy central and southern areas include a major cranberry-producing region.

56001.description: Albany County, Wyoming, borders Colorado to the south. Its county seat is Laramie, home to the University of Wyoming, and the county comprises the Laramie micropolitan area.

56003.description: Big Horn County, Wyoming, borders Montana to the north. Its county seat is Basin, and its population was 11,521 at the 2020 census.

56005.description: Campbell County, Wyoming, had 47,026 residents at the 2020 census, making it the state's third-most populous county. Its county seat is Gillette, and it comprises the Gillette micropolitan area.

56007.description: Carbon County, Wyoming, borders Colorado to the south and is the state's third-largest county by area. Its county seat is Rawlins, and its population was 14,537 at the 2020 census.

56009.description: Converse County, Wyoming, had a population of 13,751 at the 2020 census. Douglas is its county seat.

56011.description: Crook County occupies Wyoming's northeastern corner at the northwestern end of the Black Hills, with Sundance as its county seat and largest city. Devils Tower National Monument lies in the county's Bear Lodge Mountains.

56013.description: Fremont County, Wyoming, ranges from desert at Boysen State Park to glaciers at Gannett Peak, with much of its western boundary following the Continental Divide in the Wind River Range. Lander is the county seat, while Riverton is its largest community.

56015.description: Goshen County lies in Wyoming's High Plains along the North Platte River and borders Nebraska to the east. Torrington is its county seat, and the county produces more beef cattle than any other Wyoming county.

56017.description: Hot Springs County includes the southern part of Wyoming's Big Horn Basin and much of Wind River Canyon, surrounded by mountain ranges. Thermopolis is its county seat, and the county takes its name from the springs in Hot Springs State Park.

56019.description: Johnson County lies in north-central Wyoming, southeast of the Bighorn Mountains, with Buffalo as its county seat and Kaycee as its only other incorporated town. The Powder River flows north through the county's eastern portion.

56021.description: Laramie County occupies Wyoming's southeastern corner, north of Colorado and west of Nebraska. Its county seat is Cheyenne, the state capital, and it comprises the Cheyenne metropolitan area.

56023.description: Lincoln County, Wyoming, borders Idaho and Utah to the west. Its county seat is Kemmerer, and its population was 19,581 at the 2020 census.

56025.description: Natrona County, Wyoming, has Casper as its county seat and comprises the Casper metropolitan area. Its population was 79,955 at the 2020 census, making it the state's second-most populous county.

56027.description: Niobrara County, Wyoming, borders Nebraska and South Dakota to the east, with Lusk as its county seat. It was Wyoming's least populous county at the 2020 census, with 2,467 residents.

56029.description: Park County, Wyoming, includes most of Shoshone National Forest and more than half of Yellowstone National Park's land area. Cody is its county seat, and the county is a major tourism destination.

56031.description: Platte County, Wyoming, is the state's third-smallest county by area. Its county seat is Wheatland, and its population was 8,605 at the 2020 census.

56033.description: Sheridan County, Wyoming, borders Montana to the north, with Sheridan as its county seat. It comprises the Sheridan micropolitan area and had 30,921 residents at the 2020 census.

56035.description: Sublette County is a sparsely populated rural county in western Wyoming along the Green River. Its county seat is Pinedale, and its population was 8,728 at the 2020 census.

56037.description: Sweetwater County is Wyoming's largest county by area, bordering Colorado and Utah to the south, with Green River as its county seat. The Continental Divide crosses the county, and most of the Great Divide Basin lies within its northeastern portion.

56039.description: Teton County, Wyoming, has Jackson as its county seat and contains all of Grand Teton National Park and 40.4% of Yellowstone National Park's total area. It also contains the Jackson Hole ski area.
