56041.description: Uinta County, Wyoming, borders Utah to the south and west, with Evanston as its county seat. It is the state's second-smallest county by area and joins Rich County, Utah, in the Evanston micropolitan area.

56043.description: Washakie County, Wyoming, had a population of 7,685 at the 2020 census. Its county seat is Worland.

56045.description: Weston County, Wyoming, borders South Dakota to the east. Its county seat is Newcastle, and its population was 6,838 at the 2020 census.

72001.description: Adjuntas is a mountainous municipality in Puerto Rico's Cordillera Central, with Monte Guilarte as its highest peak. Coffee, bananas, and other crops have long been part of its agricultural economy.

72003.description: Aguada is a municipality on Puerto Rico's northwestern Atlantic coast, with mostly flat, fertile alluvial terrain and mountains to the south and southeast. Sugarcane processing historically dominated its economy; the Central Coloso refinery closed in 2003.

72005.description: Aguadilla is a municipality on Puerto Rico's northwestern coast, with mostly level terrain in the Western Coastal Plains. Industrial and pharmaceutical plants are part of its economy, including facilities in San Antonio Technological Park.

72007.description: Aguas Buenas is a municipality in central-eastern Puerto Rico with moderately mountainous terrain on the northern edge of the Sierra de Cayey. Coffee plantations formed the early basis of its economy.

72009.description: Aibonito is a mountain municipality in Puerto Rico's Sierra de Cayey, with the island's highest-elevation main square at 732 meters above sea level. Coffee, tobacco, flower cultivation, and poultry production are among its economic activities.

72011.description: Añasco is a municipality on Puerto Rico's western coastal plain, bordering the Mona Passage and the Río Grande de Añasco. Its terrain is mostly level but includes hills and mountains such as Canta Gallo, Gordo, and Pichón.

72013.description: Arecibo is a municipality extending from Puerto Rico's northern Atlantic coast into the Northern Karst Belt, with the Río Grande de Arecibo running through it. Pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and fishing contribute to its diverse economy.

72015.description: Arroyo is a municipality on Puerto Rico's southern Caribbean coast in the Southern Coastal Valley. Its dry alluvial plains rely on irrigation for agricultural production, and Cerro Tumbado is its highest point.

72017.description: Barceloneta is a municipality on Puerto Rico's Atlantic coast in the Northern Karst region, with mostly flat terrain as well as hills, caves, and coastal wetlands. A large pharmaceutical complex is a prominent part of its economy.

72019.description: Barranquitas is a landlocked, mountainous municipality in Puerto Rico's Cordillera Central, with San Cristóbal and Las Bocas canyons among its features. Its crops include plantains, coffee, lemons, and other fruits and vegetables.

72021.description: Bayamón is a municipality in the San Juan metropolitan area on Puerto Rico's northeastern coastal plain and Northern Karst Belt. Its mostly flat terrain includes limestone hills and higher foothills of the Cordillera Central.

72023.description: Cabo Rojo is a municipality at Puerto Rico's southwestern corner, bordering the Caribbean Sea and Mona Passage. The Sierra Bermeja crosses its otherwise largely flat Western Coastal Plains terrain.

72025.description: Caguas is a municipality in central-eastern Puerto Rico's Caguas Valley, between the Sierra de Cayey and Sierra de Luquillo. It is a principal city of the San Juan metropolitan area and had 127,244 residents at the 2020 census.

72027.description: Camuy is a municipality bordering the Atlantic Ocean in Puerto Rico's Northern Karst zone. Its terrain includes level plateau areas, wooded hills and depressions near Cibao, and the Camuy River cavern system.

72029.description: Canóvanas is a municipality in northeastern Puerto Rico, combining flat alluvial plains in the north and center with rugged mountains to the south and southeast. Its economy has traditionally relied on agriculture, especially sugarcane and coffee.

72031.description: Carolina is a municipality on Puerto Rico's northeastern coastal plain, immediately east of San Juan and part of its metropolitan area. Its coastal Isla Verde district contains Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport, Puerto Rico's main international airport.

72033.description: Cataño is a municipality of mostly flat plains on San Juan Bay and is Puerto Rico's smallest municipality by land area. Port activities, fishing, transport, logistics, and the Bacardi distillery are parts of its economy.

72035.description: Cayey is a municipality in a valley surrounded by the Sierra de Cayey and the main ranges of Puerto Rico's Cordillera Central. Its rivers include the Guavate, Jájome, La Plata, and Maton, and its highest point is Cerro La Santa.

72037.description: Ceiba is a municipality on Puerto Rico's northeastern Atlantic coast, where the Medio Mundo and Daguao Nature Reserve extends toward Fajardo with predominantly mangrove forest. Manufacturing includes plywood, apparel, and hardware products.

72039.description: Ciales is a municipality spanning Puerto Rico's Northern Karst zone in the north and the Cordillera Central in the south. Coffee, fruit, and dairy production have long been important to its agricultural economy.

72041.description: Cidra is a municipality on a hilltop in the eastern Cordillera Central of Puerto Rico, with Cerro Viento Caliente as its highest point. Coffee, tobacco, fruit, and cattle ranching have contributed to its economy, alongside pharmaceutical and clothing industries.

72043.description: Coamo is a municipality in south-central Puerto Rico, with its town and parts of its barrios set in a valley east of Ponce. Local agriculture includes mangoes, plantains, citrus, poultry, and cattle.

72045.description: Comerío is a municipality in central-eastern Puerto Rico, with Comerío Pueblo serving as its downtown and administrative center. The Río de la Plata and Río Hondo are among its rivers.

72047.description: Corozal is a mountainous municipality near the center of Puerto Rico, with Quebrada Jacinta valley among its landscape features. Its agriculture includes plantains, eggs, and hydroponic crops such as lettuce and recao.

72049.description: Culebra is an island municipality and archipelago northeast of the main island of Puerto Rico, including Culebrita and several cays. Its coastline has cliffs, sandy coral beaches, and mangrove forests, while construction and tourism are its main sources of revenue.

72051.description: Dorado is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s northern coast, west of San Juan in the Northern Karst region. Its geology includes limestone and coastal sediments, and its industries include clothing and medical equipment manufacturing.

72053.description: Fajardo is a coastal municipality in Puerto Rico with offshore islets, lagoons, and river gorges. Recreational boating, fishing, manufacturing, and pharmaceutical businesses are part of its local economy.

72054.description: Florida is a small municipality in Puerto Rico’s northern karst region, surrounded by limestone haystack hills known as mogotes. Its economy historically relied on pineapple cultivation, and pharmaceutical manufacturing plants have since been established there.

72055.description: Guánica is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s southern coast, with a town on a narrow harbor bordered by rugged hills. Guánica State Forest protects tropical dry coastal forest near the town.

72057.description: Guayama is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s Caribbean coast, extending from the Southern Coastal Valley to the central mountain range. Its economy includes pharmaceutical and other manufacturing companies.

72059.description: Guayanilla is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s southern coast, with Guayanilla Bay to the south and mountains in its northern territory. Petrochemical manufacturing and thermoelectric power generation are among its industries.

72061.description: Guaynabo is a municipality west of San Juan on Puerto Rico’s northeastern coastal plain, with flatter terrain and karst hills in the north and hills to the south. It hosts corporate headquarters, sales offices, and television studios.

72063.description: Gurabo is a municipality in the Caguas Valley of eastern Puerto Rico. Its manufacturing sectors include metal, paper, plastics, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and electrical equipment.

72065.description: Hatillo is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s northern coast in the Northern Karst region, between Camuy and Arecibo. It is a major producer of milk on the island.

72067.description: Hormigueros is a municipality in western Puerto Rico whose terrain includes northern hills, a semi-mountainous area extending through downtown, and a flat valley to the south. Hormigueros Pueblo is its downtown and administrative center.

72069.description: Humacao is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s eastern coast, bordered by the Atlantic Ocean. Most of its territory lies on the flat Eastern Coastal Plains, with minor elevations to the southwest and northwest.

72071.description: Isabela is a municipality in northwestern Puerto Rico spanning the Northern Coastal Plains and Northern Karst region. Its landscape includes beaches, coastal cliffs and flats, caves, rivers, forests, and the Aymamón Mountains in the south.

72073.description: Jayuya is a municipality in a valley within Puerto Rico’s Cordillera Central, with mostly rough, steep terrain and part of Toro Negro State Forest. Its agriculture includes coffee, tomatoes, other vegetables, and livestock.

72075.description: Juana Díaz is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s southern coast, crossed by the Inabón and Jacaguas rivers. Its economy includes plantains, bananas, mangoes, livestock, rum production, and beige marble.

72077.description: Juncos is a municipality in east-central Puerto Rico, where the Río Valenciano crosses the town before joining the Río Gurabo to the north. Agriculture and pharmaceutical and biotechnology manufacturing are among its economic activities.

72079.description: Lajas is a municipality in the Lajas Valley of southwestern Puerto Rico, bordering the Caribbean Sea. Laguna Cartagena National Wildlife Refuge is located within the municipality.

72081.description: Lares is a mountainous municipality in central-western Puerto Rico, with Lares Pueblo as its downtown. Its primarily agricultural economy includes bananas, coffee, oranges, and tomatoes, alongside tourism.

72083.description: Las Marías is a municipality in central-western Puerto Rico, east of Mayagüez and west of Lares. The Río Grande de Añasco is located in the municipality, and Las Marías Pueblo is its downtown and administrative center.

72085.description: Las Piedras is a landlocked municipality in eastern Puerto Rico. Its highest point is El Toro on the boundary with Río Grande, also the highest point in the Sierra de Luquillo and El Yunque National Forest.

72087.description: Loíza is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s northeastern coastal plain, east of Carolina within the San Juan metropolitan area. It is known for Afro-Puerto Rican culture and heritage, as well as the beaches and mangrove forest of Piñones.

72089.description: Luquillo is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s northeastern Atlantic coast, northwest of Fajardo and east of Río Grande. Its landscape lies between the ocean and El Yunque National Forest, and includes the beginning of the Northeast Ecological Corridor Nature Reserve.

72091.description: Manatí is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s north-central coast in the Northern Karst region. Its economy includes pineapple cultivation and processing, other crops, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

72093.description: Maricao is a municipality in the rugged western Cordillera Central of Puerto Rico. Its economy has long relied on coffee plantations, with fruit and vegetable cultivation, manufacturing, and tourism also present.

72095.description: Maunabo is a municipality in the Maunabo Valley on Puerto Rico’s southeastern coast, surrounded by high mountains on two sides. It had a population of 10,589 in 2020.

72097.description: Mayagüez is a municipality near the center of Puerto Rico’s western coast, with coastal plains, river valleys, marshland, hills, and mountains. The Yagüez River flows through downtown before entering the Mona Passage.

72099.description: Moca is a municipality in northwestern Puerto Rico’s Northern Karst region, crossed from east to west by the Río Culebrinas. The town is known for Mundillo, a handmade bobbin lace tradition.

72101.description: Morovis is a mountainous municipality in central Puerto Rico, between the Northern Karst Belt to the north and the Cordillera Central to the south. Cerro El Malo, on its boundary with Orocovis, is its highest point.

72103.description: Naguabo is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s eastern coast, with Pico del Este in the Sierra de Luquillo as its highest point. The Río Blanco runs through it to the Caribbean Sea, and fishing is a longstanding part of its economy.

72105.description: Naranjito is a municipality in Puerto Rico’s central mountainous region. Its economy includes coffee, tobacco, bananas, oranges, papayas, and garment manufacturing.

72107.description: Orocovis is a mountainous municipality in central Puerto Rico, with many valleys and much of its terrain in the Cordillera Central. Its agricultural products include cattle, coffee, fruit, and tobacco.

72109.description: Patillas is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s southeastern coast, with mountainous territory bordered by the Sierra de Cayey to the north and Sierra de Guardarraya to the east. It was identified in 2021 as one of the island’s main plantain-producing areas.

72111.description: Peñuelas is a municipality in the Peñuelas Valley on Puerto Rico’s southern coast, west of Ponce. Its territory includes high mountain slopes along the boundary with Adjuntas and rivers including the Macaná and Tallaboa.

72113.description: Ponce is a city and municipality on Puerto Rico’s southern Caribbean coast and a regional center for government agencies. Its territory extends from coastal flats and plains through limestone hills to the mountainous interior.

72115.description: Quebradillas is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s Atlantic shore in the Northern Karst region. Its landscape includes Guajataca State Forest, limestone sinkholes and mogotes, and Guajataca Beach at the mouth of the Río Guajataca.

72117.description: Rincón is a municipality on the westernmost coast of the main island of Puerto Rico. Tourism is its major industry, with surfing beaches, scuba diving, and snorkeling among its attractions.

72119.description: Río Grande is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s northeastern coast, north of the Sierra de Luquillo. It contains a large portion of El Yunque National Forest, while its agriculture includes fruits, vegetables, ornamental plants, tobacco, and cattle.

72121.description: Sabana Grande is a municipality in the Lajas Valley of southwestern Puerto Rico. Its rivers include the Río Guanajibo and tributaries, and its highest point is in the western Cordillera Central on the boundary with Maricao.

72123.description: Salinas is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s southern coast, with flat coastal terrain and mountains to the north. Its agriculture includes banana and papaya farms, beef production, and poultry.

72125.description: San Germán is a municipality in southwestern Puerto Rico’s Sabana Grande Valley, between the Cordillera Central and the Santa Marta Hills and Lajas Valley. Fruit and sugarcane cultivation and small dairy farms are among its agricultural activities.

72127.description: San Juan is Puerto Rico’s capital and most populous municipality, on the northeastern coast in the Northern Plains region. Its geography includes San Juan Bay and the Condado and San José lagoons, and it is a major seaport and financial, cultural, and tourism center.

72129.description: San Lorenzo is a municipality in east-central Puerto Rico, with its town in a high valley formed by the Río Grande de Loíza. Its economy includes coffee and fruit cultivation, clothing, pharmaceuticals, footwear, and electromechanical equipment.

72131.description: San Sebastián is a municipality in northwestern Puerto Rico, south of Isabela, Quebradillas, and Camuy. Its agriculture includes coffee, fruit, and dairy farming, with a coffee production plant in the Perchas I barrio.

72133.description: Santa Isabel is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s southern coast, with rivers including the Coamo and Descalabrado. Its economy includes fruit and vegetable cultivation, juice production, and aerospace, electrical, and metal products.

72135.description: Toa Alta is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s Northern Coastal Plain in the Northern Karst zone, crossed by the Río de la Plata. Its population was 66,852 in 2020.

72137.description: Toa Baja is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s northern coast, with mangroves and marshes in the north and karst terrain in the south. Its economy historically relied on sugarcane and cattle before manufacturing became a principal activity after the 1950s.

72139.description: Trujillo Alto is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s northeastern coastal plain, with mostly flat northern terrain and hills to the south. Its Carraízo dam forms Loíza Lake, a reservoir supplying water to San Juan.

72141.description: Utuado is a municipality in Puerto Rico’s mountainous interior, spanning the Northern Karst Belt and the Cordillera Central. Its economy includes coffee, oranges, plantains, bananas, and manufacturing of textiles, paper, and stone products.

72143.description: Vega Alta is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s northern coast in the Northern Karst region, west of Dorado. Its features include Cerro Gordo Beach and the Cibuco, Mavilla, and Unibón rivers.

72145.description: Vega Baja is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s north-central coast in the Northern Karst region, with its town on the Northern Plains. Agricultural land and Puerto Nuevo Beach, also called Mar Bella Beach, are among its local features.

72147.description: Vieques is an island municipality east of the main island of Puerto Rico, between the Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean Sea. Rolling hills, an east-west central ridge, and subtropical dry forest characterize its terrain, with Isabel Segunda and Esperanza in its central inhabited area.

72149.description: Villalba is a municipality in a valley of Puerto Rico’s Cordillera Central, with Cerro El Bolo as its highest point. Its features include Guayabal Lake, Toa Vaca Lake, and Toro Negro Forest Reserve.

72151.description: Yabucoa is a municipality on Puerto Rico’s southeastern coast, with a valley enclosed by hills on three sides and the Caribbean Sea on the fourth. Its agricultural valley produces plantains and bananas and was historically used for sugarcane cultivation.

72153.description: Yauco is a municipality extending from an inland downtown to Puerto Rico’s southern Caribbean coast, with mountainous terrain in the Cordillera Central. It is bisected by the Yauco River, and its crops include coffee, plantains, oranges, and tobacco.
